text: The monk from Obdorsk, having been directed to the apiary by the beekeeper, who was also a very silent and surly monk, went to the corner where Father Ferapont’s cell stood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Maybe he will speak as you are a stranger and maybe you’ll get nothing out of him,” the beekeeper had warned him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk, as he related afterwards, approached in the utmost apprehension.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was rather late in the evening.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Ferapont was sitting at the door of his cell on a low bench.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A huge old elm was lightly rustling overhead.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was an evening freshness in the air.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk from Obdorsk bowed down before the saint and asked his blessing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you want me to bow down to you, monk?” said Father Ferapont.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Get up!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk got up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Blessing, be blessed! Sit beside me. Where have you come from?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What most struck the poor monk was the fact that in spite of his strict fasting and great age, Father Ferapont still looked a vigorous old man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was tall, held himself erect, and had a thin, but fresh and healthy face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was no doubt he still had considerable strength.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was of athletic build.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of his great age he was not even quite gray, and still had very thick hair and a full beard, both of which had once been black.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His eyes were gray, large and luminous, but strikingly prominent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He spoke with a broad accent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was dressed in a peasant’s long reddish coat of coarse convict cloth (as it used to be called) and had a stout rope round his waist.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His throat and chest were bare.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Beneath his coat, his shirt of the coarsest linen showed almost black with dirt, not having been changed for months.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They said that he wore irons weighing thirty pounds under his coat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His stockingless feet were thrust in old slippers almost dropping to pieces.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “From the little Obdorsk monastery, from St. Sylvester,” the monk answered humbly, whilst his keen and inquisitive, but rather frightened little eyes kept watch on the hermit.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I have been at your Sylvester’s. I used to stay there. Is Sylvester well?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The monk hesitated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are a senseless lot! How do you keep the fasts?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Our dietary is according to the ancient conventual rules. During Lent there are no meals provided for Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. For Tuesday and Thursday we have white bread, stewed fruit with honey, wild berries, or salt cabbage and wholemeal stirabout. On Saturday white cabbage soup, noodles with peas, kasha, all with hemp oil. On weekdays we have dried fish and kasha with the cabbage soup. From Monday till Saturday evening, six whole days in Holy Week, nothing is cooked, and we have only bread and water, and that sparingly; if possible not taking food every day, just the same as is ordered for first week in Lent. On Good Friday nothing is eaten. In the same way on the Saturday we have to fast till three o’clock, and then take a little bread and water and drink a single cup of wine. On Holy Thursday we drink wine and have something cooked without oil or not cooked at all, inasmuch as the Laodicean council lays down for Holy Thursday: ‘It is unseemly by remitting the fast on the Holy Thursday to dishonor the whole of Lent! This is how we keep the fast. But what is that compared with you, holy Father,” added the monk, growing more confident, “for all the year round, even at Easter, you take nothing but bread and water, and what we should eat in two days lasts you full seven. It’s truly marvelous—your great abstinence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And mushrooms?” asked Father Ferapont, suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mushrooms?” repeated the surprised monk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes. I can give up their bread, not needing it at all, and go away into the forest and live there on the mushrooms or the berries, but they can’t give up their bread here, wherefore they are in bondage to the devil. Nowadays the unclean deny that there is need of such fasting. Haughty and unclean is their judgment.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Och, true,” sighed the monk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And have you seen devils among them?” asked Ferapont.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Among them? Among whom?” asked the monk, timidly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I went to the Father Superior on Trinity Sunday last year, I haven’t been since. I saw a devil sitting on one man’s chest hiding under his cassock, only his horns poked out; another had one peeping out of his pocket with such sharp eyes, he was afraid of me; another settled in the unclean belly of one, another was hanging round a man’s neck, and so he was carrying him about without seeing him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You—can see spirits?” the monk inquired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I tell you I can see, I can see through them. When I was coming out from the Superior’s I saw one hiding from me behind the door, and a big one, a yard and a half or more high, with a thick long gray tail, and the tip of his tail was in the crack of the door and I was quick and slammed the door, pinching his tail in it. He squealed and began to struggle, and I made the sign of the cross over him three times. And he died on the spot like a crushed spider. He must have rotted there in the corner and be stinking, but they don’t see, they don’t smell it. It’s a year since I have been there. I reveal it to you, as you are a stranger.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Your words are terrible! But, holy and blessed Father,” said the monk, growing bolder and bolder, “is it true, as they noise abroad even to distant lands about you, that you are in continual communication with the Holy Ghost?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He does fly down at times.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How does he fly down? In what form?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As a bird.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The Holy Ghost in the form of a dove?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s the Holy Ghost and there’s the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit can appear as other birds—sometimes as a swallow, sometimes a goldfinch and sometimes as a blue-tit.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you know him from an ordinary tit?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He speaks.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How does he speak, in what language?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Human language.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what does he tell you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, to-day he told me that a fool would visit me and would ask me unseemly questions. You want to know too much, monk.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Terrible are your words, most holy and blessed Father,” the monk shook his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But there was a doubtful look in his frightened little eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you see this tree?” asked Father Ferapont, after a pause.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I do, blessed Father.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You think it’s an elm, but for me it has another shape.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What sort of shape?” inquired the monk, after a pause of vain expectation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It happens at night. You see those two branches? In the night it is Christ holding out His arms to me and seeking me with those arms, I see it clearly and tremble. It’s terrible, terrible!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is there terrible if it’s Christ Himself?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, He’ll snatch me up and carry me away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alive?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In the spirit and glory of Elijah, haven’t you heard? He will take me in His arms and bear me away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though the monk returned to the cell he was sharing with one of the brothers, in considerable perplexity of mind, he still cherished at heart a greater reverence for Father Ferapont than for Father Zossima.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was strongly in favor of fasting, and it was not strange that one who kept so rigid a fast as Father Ferapont should “see marvels. His words seemed certainly queer, but God only could tell what was hidden in those words, and were not worse words and acts commonly seen in those who have sacrificed their intellects for the glory of God? The pinching of the devil’s tail he was ready and eager to believe, and not only in the figurative sense. Besides he had, before visiting the monastery, a strong prejudice against the institution of “elders,” which he only knew of by hearsay and believed to be a pernicious innovation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Before he had been long at the monastery, he had detected the secret murmurings of some shallow brothers who disliked the institution.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was, besides, a meddlesome, inquisitive man, who poked his nose into everything.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was why the news of the fresh “miracle” performed by Father Zossima reduced him to extreme perplexity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha remembered afterwards how their inquisitive guest from Obdorsk had been continually flitting to and fro from one group to another, listening and asking questions among the monks that were crowding within and without the elder’s cell.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he did not pay much attention to him at the time, and only recollected it afterwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had no thought to spare for it indeed, for when Father Zossima, feeling tired again, had gone back to bed, he thought of Alyosha as he was closing his eyes, and sent for him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha ran at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was no one else in the cell but Father Païssy, Father Iosif, and the novice Porfiry.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The elder, opening his weary eyes and looking intently at Alyosha, asked him suddenly:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Are your people expecting you, my son?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha hesitated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Haven’t they need of you? Didn’t you promise some one yesterday to see them to-day?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I did promise—to my father—my brothers—others too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see, you must go. Don’t grieve. Be sure I shall not die without your being by to hear my last word. To you I will say that word, my son, it will be my last gift to you. To you, dear son, because you love me. But now go to keep your promise.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha immediately obeyed, though it was hard to go.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the promise that he should hear his last word on earth, that it should be the last gift to him, Alyosha, sent a thrill of rapture through his soul.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He made haste that he might finish what he had to do in the town and return quickly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Father Païssy, too, uttered some words of exhortation which moved and surprised him greatly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He spoke as they left the cell together.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Remember, young man, unceasingly,” Father Païssy began, without preface, “that the science of this world, which has become a great power, has, especially in the last century, analyzed everything divine handed down to us in the holy books. After this cruel analysis the learned of this world have nothing left of all that was sacred of old. But they have only analyzed the parts and overlooked the whole, and indeed their blindness is marvelous. Yet the whole still stands steadfast before their eyes, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. Has it not lasted nineteen centuries, is it not still a living, a moving power in the individual soul and in the masses of people? It is still as strong and living even in the souls of atheists, who have destroyed everything! For even those who have renounced Christianity and attack it, in their inmost being still follow the Christian ideal, for hitherto neither their subtlety nor the ardor of their hearts has been able to create a higher ideal of man and of virtue than the ideal given by Christ of old. When it has been attempted, the result has been only grotesque. Remember this especially, young man, since you are being sent into the world by your departing elder. Maybe, remembering this great day, you will not forget my words, uttered from the heart for your guidance, seeing you are young, and the temptations of the world are great and beyond your strength to endure. Well, now go, my orphan.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: With these words Father Païssy blessed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As Alyosha left the monastery and thought them over, he suddenly realized that he had met a new and unexpected friend, a warmly loving teacher, in this austere monk who had hitherto treated him sternly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was as though Father Zossima had bequeathed him to him at his death, and “perhaps that’s just what had passed between them,” Alyosha thought suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The philosophic reflections he had just heard so unexpectedly testified to the warmth of Father Païssy’s heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was in haste to arm the boy’s mind for conflict with temptation and to guard the young soul left in his charge with the strongest defense he could imagine.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: First of all, Alyosha went to his father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: On the way he remembered that his father had insisted the day before that he should come without his brother Ivan seeing him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why so? Alyosha wondered suddenly. “Even if my father has something to say to me alone, why should I go in unseen? Most likely in his excitement yesterday he meant to say something different,” he decided.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet he was very glad when Marfa Ignatyevna, who opened the garden gate to him (Grigory, it appeared, was ill in bed in the lodge), told him in answer to his question that Ivan Fyodorovitch had gone out two hours ago.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And my father?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is up, taking his coffee,” Marfa answered somewhat dryly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha went in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man was sitting alone at the table wearing slippers and a little old overcoat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was amusing himself by looking through some accounts, rather inattentively however.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was quite alone in the house, for Smerdyakov too had gone out marketing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though he had got up early and was trying to put a bold face on it, he looked tired and weak.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His forehead, upon which huge purple bruises had come out during the night, was bandaged with a red handkerchief; his nose too had swollen terribly in the night, and some smaller bruises covered it in patches, giving his whole face a peculiarly spiteful and irritable look.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The old man was aware of this, and turned a hostile glance on Alyosha as he came in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The coffee is cold,” he cried harshly; “I won’t offer you any. I’ve ordered nothing but a Lenten fish soup to-day, and I don’t invite any one to share it. Why have you come?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To find out how you are,” said Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes. Besides, I told you to come yesterday. It’s all of no consequence. You need not have troubled. But I knew you’d come poking in directly.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He said this with almost hostile feeling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At the same time he got up and looked anxiously in the looking-glass (perhaps for the fortieth time that morning) at his nose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He began, too, binding his red handkerchief more becomingly on his forehead.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Red’s better. It’s just like the hospital in a white one,” he observed sententiously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, how are things over there? How is your elder?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is very bad; he may die to-day,” answered Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his father had not listened, and had forgotten his own question at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ivan’s gone out,” he said suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is doing his utmost to carry off Mitya’s betrothed. That’s what he is staying here for,” he added maliciously, and, twisting his mouth, looked at Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Surely he did not tell you so?” asked Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, he did, long ago. Would you believe it, he told me three weeks ago? You don’t suppose he too came to murder me, do you? He must have had some object in coming.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What do you mean? Why do you say such things?” said Alyosha, troubled.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He doesn’t ask for money, it’s true, but yet he won’t get a farthing from me. I intend living as long as possible, you may as well know, my dear Alexey Fyodorovitch, and so I need every farthing, and the longer I live, the more I shall need it,” he continued, pacing from one corner of the room to the other, keeping his hands in the pockets of his loose greasy overcoat made of yellow cotton material.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I can still pass for a man at five and fifty, but I want to pass for one for another twenty years. As I get older, you know, I shan’t be a pretty object. The wenches won’t come to me of their own accord, so I shall want my money. So I am saving up more and more, simply for myself, my dear son Alexey Fyodorovitch. You may as well know. For I mean to go on in my sins to the end, let me tell you. For sin is sweet; all abuse it, but all men live in it, only others do it on the sly, and I openly. And so all the other sinners fall upon me for being so simple. And your paradise, Alexey Fyodorovitch, is not to my taste, let me tell you that; and it’s not the proper place for a gentleman, your paradise, even if it exists. I believe that I fall asleep and don’t wake up again, and that’s all. You can pray for my soul if you like. And if you don’t want to, don’t, damn you! That’s my philosophy. Ivan talked well here yesterday, though we were all drunk. Ivan is a conceited coxcomb, but he has no particular learning ... nor education either. He sits silent and smiles at one without speaking—that’s what pulls him through.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha listened to him in silence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why won’t he talk to me? If he does speak, he gives himself airs. Your Ivan is a scoundrel! And I’ll marry Grushenka in a minute if I want to. For if you’ve money, Alexey Fyodorovitch, you have only to want a thing and you can have it. That’s what Ivan is afraid of, he is on the watch to prevent me getting married and that’s why he is egging on Mitya to marry Grushenka himself. He hopes to keep me from Grushenka by that (as though I should leave him my money if I don’t marry her!). Besides if Mitya marries Grushenka, Ivan will carry off his rich betrothed, that’s what he’s reckoning on! He is a scoundrel, your Ivan!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How cross you are! It’s because of yesterday; you had better lie down,” said Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There! you say that,” the old man observed suddenly, as though it had struck him for the first time, “and I am not angry with you. But if Ivan said it, I should be angry with him. It is only with you I have good moments, else you know I am an ill-natured man.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are not ill-natured, but distorted,” said Alyosha with a smile.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Listen. I meant this morning to get that ruffian Mitya locked up and I don’t know now what I shall decide about it. Of course in these fashionable days fathers and mothers are looked upon as a prejudice, but even now the law does not allow you to drag your old father about by the hair, to kick him in the face in his own house, and brag of murdering him outright—all in the presence of witnesses. If I liked, I could crush him and could have him locked up at once for what he did yesterday.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then you don’t mean to take proceedings?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ivan has dissuaded me. I shouldn’t care about Ivan, but there’s another thing.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And bending down to Alyosha, he went on in a confidential half-whisper.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If I send the ruffian to prison, she’ll hear of it and run to see him at once. But if she hears that he has beaten me, a weak old man, within an inch of my life, she may give him up and come to me.... For that’s her way, everything by contraries. I know her through and through! Won’t you have a drop of brandy? Take some cold coffee and I’ll pour a quarter of a glass of brandy into it, it’s delicious, my boy.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, thank you. I’ll take that roll with me if I may,” said Alyosha, and taking a halfpenny French roll he put it in the pocket of his cassock.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you’d better not have brandy, either,” he suggested apprehensively, looking into the old man’s face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are quite right, it irritates my nerves instead of soothing them. Only one little glass. I’ll get it out of the cupboard.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He unlocked the cupboard, poured out a glass, drank it, then locked the cupboard and put the key back in his pocket.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s enough. One glass won’t kill me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see you are in a better humor now,” said Alyosha, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Um! I love you even without the brandy, but with scoundrels I am a scoundrel. Ivan is not going to Tchermashnya—why is that? He wants to spy how much I give Grushenka if she comes. They are all scoundrels! But I don’t recognize Ivan, I don’t know him at all. Where does he come from? He is not one of us in soul. As though I’d leave him anything! I shan’t leave a will at all, you may as well know. And I’ll crush Mitya like a beetle. I squash black-beetles at night with my slipper; they squelch when you tread on them. And your Mitya will squelch too. Your Mitya, for you love him. Yes, you love him and I am not afraid of your loving him. But if Ivan loved him I should be afraid for myself at his loving him. But Ivan loves nobody. Ivan is not one of us. People like Ivan are not our sort, my boy. They are like a cloud of dust. When the wind blows, the dust will be gone.... I had a silly idea in my head when I told you to come to-day; I wanted to find out from you about Mitya. If I were to hand him over a thousand or maybe two now, would the beggarly wretch agree to take himself off altogether for five years or, better still, thirty-five, and without Grushenka, and give her up once for all, eh?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I—I’ll ask him,” muttered Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If you would give him three thousand, perhaps he—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s nonsense! You needn’t ask him now, no need! I’ve changed my mind. It was a nonsensical idea of mine. I won’t give him anything, not a penny, I want my money myself,” cried the old man, waving his hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll crush him like a beetle without it. Don’t say anything to him or else he will begin hoping. There’s nothing for you to do here, you needn’t stay. Is that betrothed of his, Katerina Ivanovna, whom he has kept so carefully hidden from me all this time, going to marry him or not? You went to see her yesterday, I believe?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing will induce her to abandon him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There you see how dearly these fine young ladies love a rake and a scoundrel. They are poor creatures I tell you, those pale young ladies, very different from—Ah, if I had his youth and the looks I had then (for I was better-looking than he at eight and twenty) I’d have been a conquering hero just as he is. He is a low cad! But he shan’t have Grushenka, anyway, he shan’t! I’ll crush him!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His anger had returned with the last words.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You can go. There’s nothing for you to do here to-day,” he snapped harshly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha went up to say good-by to him, and kissed him on the shoulder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What’s that for? The old man was a little surprised. “We shall see each other again, or do you think we shan’t?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not at all, I didn’t mean anything.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nor did I, I did not mean anything,” said the old man, looking at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Listen, listen,” he shouted after him, “make haste and come again and I’ll have a fish soup for you, a fine one, not like to-day. Be sure to come! Come to-morrow, do you hear, to-morrow!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And as soon as Alyosha had gone out of the door, he went to the cupboard again and poured out another half-glass.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I won’t have more!” he muttered, clearing his throat, and again he locked the cupboard and put the key in his pocket.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then he went into his bedroom, lay down on the bed, exhausted, and in one minute he was asleep.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Thank goodness he did not ask me about Grushenka,” thought Alyosha, as he left his father’s house and turned towards Madame Hohlakov’s, “or I might have to tell him of my meeting with Grushenka yesterday.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha felt painfully that since yesterday both combatants had renewed their energies, and that their hearts had grown hard again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Father is spiteful and angry, he’s made some plan and will stick to it. And what of Dmitri? He too will be harder than yesterday, he too must be spiteful and angry, and he too, no doubt, has made some plan. Oh, I must succeed in finding him to-day, whatever happens.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Alyosha had not long to meditate.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: An incident occurred on the road, which, though apparently of little consequence, made a great impression on him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Just after he had crossed the square and turned the corner coming out into Mihailovsky Street, which is divided by a small ditch from the High Street (our whole town is intersected by ditches), he saw a group of schoolboys between the ages of nine and twelve, at the bridge.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They were going home from school, some with their bags on their shoulders, others with leather satchels slung across them, some in short jackets, others in little overcoats.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Some even had those high boots with creases round the ankles, such as little boys spoilt by rich fathers love to wear.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The whole group was talking eagerly about something, apparently holding a council.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha had never from his Moscow days been able to pass children without taking notice of them, and although he was particularly fond of children of three or thereabout, he liked schoolboys of ten and eleven too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so, anxious as he was to-day, he wanted at once to turn aside to talk to them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked into their excited rosy faces, and noticed at once that all the boys had stones in their hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Behind the ditch some thirty paces away, there was another schoolboy standing by a fence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He too had a satchel at his side.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was about ten years old, pale, delicate-looking and with sparkling black eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He kept an attentive and anxious watch on the other six, obviously his schoolfellows with whom he had just come out of school, but with whom he had evidently had a feud.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha went up and, addressing a fair, curly-headed, rosy boy in a black jacket, observed:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When I used to wear a satchel like yours, I always used to carry it on my left side, so as to have my right hand free, but you’ve got yours on your right side. So it will be awkward for you to get at it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha had no art or premeditation in beginning with this practical remark.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But it is the only way for a grown-up person to get at once into confidential relations with a child, or still more with a group of children.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One must begin in a serious, businesslike way so as to be on a perfectly equal footing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha understood it by instinct.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But he is left-handed,” another, a fine healthy-looking boy of eleven, answered promptly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All the others stared at Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He even throws stones with his left hand,” observed a third.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At that instant a stone flew into the group, but only just grazed the left-handed boy, though it was well and vigorously thrown by the boy standing the other side of the ditch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give it him, hit him back, Smurov,” they all shouted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Smurov, the left-handed boy, needed no telling, and at once revenged himself; he threw a stone, but it missed the boy and hit the ground.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy the other side of the ditch, the pocket of whose coat was visibly bulging with stones, flung another stone at the group; this time it flew straight at Alyosha and hit him painfully on the shoulder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He aimed it at you, he meant it for you. You are Karamazov, Karamazov!” the boys shouted, laughing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, all throw at him at once!” and six stones flew at the boy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: One struck the boy on the head and he fell down, but at once leapt up and began ferociously returning their fire.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Both sides threw stones incessantly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Many of the group had their pockets full too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What are you about! Aren’t you ashamed? Six against one! Why, you’ll kill him,” cried Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran forward and met the flying stones to screen the solitary boy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Three or four ceased throwing for a minute.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He began first!” cried a boy in a red shirt in an angry childish voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is a beast, he stabbed Krassotkin in class the other day with a penknife. It bled. Krassotkin wouldn’t tell tales, but he must be thrashed.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what for? I suppose you tease him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There, he sent a stone in your back again, he knows you,” cried the children.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s you he is throwing at now, not us. Come, all of you, at him again, don’t miss, Smurov!” and again a fire of stones, and a very vicious one, began.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy the other side of the ditch was hit in the chest; he screamed, began to cry and ran away uphill towards Mihailovsky Street.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They all shouted: “Aha, he is funking, he is running away. Wisp of tow!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You don’t know what a beast he is, Karamazov, killing is too good for him,” said the boy in the jacket, with flashing eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He seemed to be the eldest.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What’s wrong with him?” asked Alyosha, “is he a tell-tale or what?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boys looked at one another as though derisively.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Are you going that way, to Mihailovsky?” the same boy went on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Catch him up.... You see he’s stopped again, he is waiting and looking at you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is looking at you,” the other boys chimed in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You ask him, does he like a disheveled wisp of tow. Do you hear, ask him that!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a general burst of laughter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha looked at them, and they at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t go near him, he’ll hurt you,” cried Smurov in a warning voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shan’t ask him about the wisp of tow, for I expect you tease him with that question somehow. But I’ll find out from him why you hate him so.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Find out then, find out,” cried the boys, laughing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha crossed the bridge and walked uphill by the fence, straight towards the boy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’d better look out,” the boys called after him; “he won’t be afraid of you. He will stab you in a minute, on the sly, as he did Krassotkin.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy waited for him without budging.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Coming up to him, Alyosha saw facing him a child of about nine years old.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was an undersized weakly boy with a thin pale face, with large dark eyes that gazed at him vindictively.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was dressed in a rather shabby old overcoat, which he had monstrously outgrown.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His bare arms stuck out beyond his sleeves.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a large patch on the right knee of his trousers, and in his right boot just at the toe there was a big hole in the leather, carefully blackened with ink.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Both the pockets of his great-coat were weighed down with stones.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha stopped two steps in front of him, looking inquiringly at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy, seeing at once from Alyosha’s eyes that he wouldn’t beat him, became less defiant, and addressed him first.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am alone, and there are six of them. I’ll beat them all, alone!” he said suddenly, with flashing eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I think one of the stones must have hurt you badly,” observed Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I hit Smurov on the head!” cried the boy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They told me that you know me, and that you threw a stone at me on purpose,” said Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy looked darkly at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know you.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Do you know me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha continued.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Let me alone!” the boy cried irritably; but he did not move, as though he were expecting something, and again there was a vindictive light in his eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Very well, I am going,” said Alyosha; “only I don’t know you and I don’t tease you. They told me how they tease you, but I don’t want to tease you. Good-by!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Monk in silk trousers!” cried the boy, following Alyosha with the same vindictive and defiant expression, and he threw himself into an attitude of defense, feeling sure that now Alyosha would fall upon him; but Alyosha turned, looked at him, and walked away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had not gone three steps before the biggest stone the boy had in his pocket hit him a painful blow in the back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So you’ll hit a man from behind! They tell the truth, then, when they say that you attack on the sly,” said Alyosha, turning round again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This time the boy threw a stone savagely right into Alyosha’s face; but Alyosha just had time to guard himself, and the stone struck him on the elbow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Aren’t you ashamed? What have I done to you?” he cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy waited in silent defiance, certain that now Alyosha would attack him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Seeing that even now he would not, his rage was like a little wild beast’s; he flew at Alyosha himself, and before Alyosha had time to move, the spiteful child had seized his left hand with both of his and bit his middle finger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He fixed his teeth in it and it was ten seconds before he let go.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha cried out with pain and pulled his finger away with all his might.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The child let go at last and retreated to his former distance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha’s finger had been badly bitten to the bone, close to the nail; it began to bleed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha took out his handkerchief and bound it tightly round his injured hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a full minute bandaging it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy stood waiting all the time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last Alyosha raised his gentle eyes and looked at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Very well,” he said, “you see how badly you’ve bitten me. That’s enough, isn’t it? Now tell me, what have I done to you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy stared in amazement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Though I don’t know you and it’s the first time I’ve seen you,” Alyosha went on with the same serenity, “yet I must have done something to you—you wouldn’t have hurt me like this for nothing. So what have I done? How have I wronged you, tell me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Instead of answering, the boy broke into a loud tearful wail and ran away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha walked slowly after him towards Mihailovsky Street, and for a long time he saw the child running in the distance as fast as ever, not turning his head, and no doubt still keeping up his tearful wail.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He made up his mind to find him out as soon as he had time, and to solve this mystery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Just now he had not the time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha soon reached Madame Hohlakov’s house, a handsome stone house of two stories, one of the finest in our town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though Madame Hohlakov spent most of her time in another province where she had an estate, or in Moscow, where she had a house of her own, yet she had a house in our town too, inherited from her forefathers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The estate in our district was the largest of her three estates, yet she had been very little in our province before this time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She ran out to Alyosha in the hall.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did you get my letter about the new miracle?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She spoke rapidly and nervously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did you show it to every one? He restored the son to his mother!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is dying to-day,” said Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I have heard, I know, oh, how I long to talk to you, to you or some one, about all this. No, to you, to you! And how sorry I am I can’t see him! The whole town is in excitement, they are all suspense. But now—do you know Katerina Ivanovna is here now?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, that’s lucky,” cried Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then I shall see her here. She told me yesterday to be sure to come and see her to-day.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know, I know all. I’ve heard exactly what happened yesterday—and the atrocious behavior of that—creature. C’est tragique, and if I’d been in her place I don’t know what I should have done. And your brother Dmitri Fyodorovitch, what do you think of him?—my goodness! Alexey Fyodorovitch, I am forgetting, only fancy; your brother is in there with her, not that dreadful brother who was so shocking yesterday, but the other, Ivan Fyodorovitch, he is sitting with her talking; they are having a serious conversation. If you could only imagine what’s passing between them now—it’s awful, I tell you it’s lacerating, it’s like some incredible tale of horror. They are ruining their lives for no reason any one can see. They both recognize it and revel in it. I’ve been watching for you! I’ve been thirsting for you! It’s too much for me, that’s the worst of it. I’ll tell you all about it presently, but now I must speak of something else, the most important thing—I had quite forgotten what’s most important. Tell me, why has Lise been in hysterics? As soon as she heard you were here, she began to be hysterical!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Maman, it’s you who are hysterical now, not I,” Lise’s voice caroled through a tiny crack of the door at the side.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her voice sounded as though she wanted to laugh, but was doing her utmost to control it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha at once noticed the crack, and no doubt Lise was peeping through it, but that he could not see.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And no wonder, Lise, no wonder ... your caprices will make me hysterical too. But she is so ill, Alexey Fyodorovitch, she has been so ill all night, feverish and moaning! I could hardly wait for the morning and for Herzenstube to come. He says that he can make nothing of it, that we must wait. Herzenstube always comes and says that he can make nothing of it. As soon as you approached the house, she screamed, fell into hysterics, and insisted on being wheeled back into this room here.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mamma, I didn’t know he had come. It wasn’t on his account I wanted to be wheeled into this room.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s not true, Lise, Yulia ran to tell you that Alexey Fyodorovitch was coming. She was on the look-out for you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My darling mamma, it’s not at all clever of you. But if you want to make up for it and say something very clever, dear mamma, you’d better tell our honored visitor, Alexey Fyodorovitch, that he has shown his want of wit by venturing to us after what happened yesterday and although every one is laughing at him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Lise, you go too far. I declare I shall have to be severe. Who laughs at him? I am so glad he has come, I need him, I can’t do without him. Oh, Alexey Fyodorovitch, I am exceedingly unhappy!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But what’s the matter with you, mamma, darling?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, your caprices, Lise, your fidgetiness, your illness, that awful night of fever, that awful everlasting Herzenstube, everlasting, everlasting, that’s the worst of it! Everything, in fact, everything.... Even that miracle, too! Oh, how it has upset me, how it has shattered me, that miracle, dear Alexey Fyodorovitch! And that tragedy in the drawing-room, it’s more than I can bear, I warn you. I can’t bear it. A comedy, perhaps, not a tragedy. Tell me, will Father Zossima live till to-morrow, will he? Oh, my God! What is happening to me? Every minute I close my eyes and see that it’s all nonsense, all nonsense.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I should be very grateful,” Alyosha interrupted suddenly, “if you could give me a clean rag to bind up my finger with. I have hurt it, and it’s very painful.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha unbound his bitten finger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The handkerchief was soaked with blood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Madame Hohlakov screamed and shut her eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good heavens, what a wound, how awful!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But as soon as Lise saw Alyosha’s finger through the crack, she flung the door wide open.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Come, come here,” she cried, imperiously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No nonsense now! Good heavens, why did you stand there saying nothing about it all this time? He might have bled to death, mamma! How did you do it? Water, water! You must wash it first of all, simply hold it in cold water to stop the pain, and keep it there, keep it there.... Make haste, mamma, some water in a slop-basin. But do make haste,” she finished nervously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was quite frightened at the sight of Alyosha’s wound.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Shouldn’t we send for Herzenstube?” cried Madame Hohlakov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mamma, you’ll be the death of me. Your Herzenstube will come and say that he can make nothing of it! Water, water! Mamma, for goodness’ sake go yourself and hurry Yulia, she is such a slowcoach and never can come quickly! Make haste, mamma, or I shall die.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, it’s nothing much,” cried Alyosha, frightened at this alarm.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yulia ran in with water and Alyosha put his finger in it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Some lint, mamma, for mercy’s sake, bring some lint and that muddy caustic lotion for wounds, what’s it called? We’ve got some. You know where the bottle is, mamma; it’s in your bedroom in the right-hand cupboard, there’s a big bottle of it there with the lint.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll bring everything in a minute, Lise, only don’t scream and don’t fuss. You see how bravely Alexey Fyodorovitch bears it. Where did you get such a dreadful wound, Alexey Fyodorovitch?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Madame Hohlakov hastened away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was all Lise was waiting for.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “First of all, answer the question, where did you get hurt like this?” she asked Alyosha, quickly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And then I’ll talk to you about something quite different. Well?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Instinctively feeling that the time of her mother’s absence was precious for her, Alyosha hastened to tell her of his enigmatic meeting with the schoolboys in the fewest words possible.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Lise clasped her hands at his story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How can you, and in that dress too, associate with schoolboys?” she cried angrily, as though she had a right to control him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are nothing but a boy yourself if you can do that, a perfect boy! But you must find out for me about that horrid boy and tell me all about it, for there’s some mystery in it. Now for the second thing, but first a question: does the pain prevent you talking about utterly unimportant things, but talking sensibly?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course not, and I don’t feel much pain now.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s because your finger is in the water. It must be changed directly, for it will get warm in a minute. Yulia, bring some ice from the cellar and another basin of water. Now she is gone, I can speak; will you give me the letter I sent you yesterday, dear Alexey Fyodorovitch—be quick, for mamma will be back in a minute and I don’t want—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I haven’t got the letter.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s not true, you have. I knew you would say that. You’ve got it in that pocket. I’ve been regretting that joke all night. Give me back the letter at once, give it me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve left it at home.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you can’t consider me as a child, a little girl, after that silly joke! I beg your pardon for that silliness, but you must bring me the letter, if you really haven’t got it—bring it to-day, you must, you must.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To-day I can’t possibly, for I am going back to the monastery and I shan’t come and see you for the next two days—three or four perhaps—for Father Zossima—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Four days, what nonsense! Listen. Did you laugh at me very much?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I didn’t laugh at all.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why not?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Because I believed all you said.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are insulting me!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not at all. As soon as I read it, I thought that all that would come to pass, for as soon as Father Zossima dies, I am to leave the monastery. Then I shall go back and finish my studies, and when you reach the legal age we will be married. I shall love you. Though I haven’t had time to think about it, I believe I couldn’t find a better wife than you, and Father Zossima tells me I must marry.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I am a cripple, wheeled about in a chair,” laughed Lise, flushing crimson.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll wheel you about myself, but I’m sure you’ll get well by then.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov

He left off dragging me by my beard and released me: ‘You are an officer,’ he said, ‘and I am an officer, if you can find a decent man to be your second send me your challenge. I will give satisfaction, though you are a scoundrel. That’s what he said. A chivalrous spirit indeed! I retired with Ilusha, and that scene is a family record imprinted for ever on Ilusha’s soul. No, it’s not for us to claim the privileges of noblemen. Judge for yourself. You’ve just been in our mansion, what did you see there? Three ladies, one a cripple and weak-minded, another a cripple and hunchback and the third not crippled but far too clever. She is a student, dying to get back to Petersburg, to work for the emancipation of the Russian woman on the banks of the Neva. I won’t speak of Ilusha, he is only nine. I am alone in the world, and if I die, what will become of all of them? I simply ask you that. And if I challenge him and he kills me on the spot, what then? What will become of them? And worse still, if he doesn’t kill me but only cripples me: I couldn’t work, but I should still be a mouth to feed. Who would feed it and who would feed them all? title: The Brothers Karamazov

Since that incident all the boys have been teasing him about the ‘wisp of tow. Schoolboys are a merciless race, individually they are angels, but together, especially in schools, they are often merciless. Their teasing has stirred up a gallant spirit in Ilusha. An ordinary boy, a weak son, would have submitted, have felt ashamed of his father, sir, but he stood up for his father against them all. For his father and for truth and justice. For what he suffered when he kissed your brother’s hand and cried to him ‘Forgive father, forgive him,’—that only God knows—and I, his father. For our children—not your children, but ours—the children of the poor gentlemen looked down upon by every one—know what justice means, sir, even at nine years old. How should the rich know? They don’t explore such depths once in their lives. But at that moment in the square when he kissed his hand, at that moment my Ilusha had grasped all that justice means. That truth entered into him and crushed him for ever, sir,” the captain said hotly again with a sort of frenzy, and he struck his right fist against his left palm as though he wanted to show how “the truth” crushed Ilusha.

Mamma began crying, too—I am very fond of mamma—well, I spent my last penny drowning my troubles. Don’t despise me for that, sir, in Russia men who drink are the best. The best men amongst us are the greatest drunkards. I lay down and I don’t remember about Ilusha, though all that day the boys had been jeering at him at school. ‘Wisp of tow,’ they shouted, ‘your father was pulled out of the tavern by his wisp of tow, you ran by and begged forgiveness.’”

We walked along, both of us depressed. ‘Well, my boy,’ said I, ‘how about our setting off on our travels? I thought I might bring him back to our talk of the day before. He didn’t answer, but I felt his fingers trembling in my hand. Ah, I thought, it’s a bad job; there’s something fresh. We had reached the stone where we are now. I sat down on the stone. And in the air there were lots of kites flapping and whirling. There were as many as thirty in sight. Of course, it’s just the season for the kites. ‘Look, Ilusha,’ said I, ‘it’s time we got out our last year’s kite again. I’ll mend it, where have you put it away? My boy made no answer. He looked away and turned sideways to me. And then a gust of wind blew up the sand. He suddenly fell on me, threw both his little arms round my neck and held me tight. You know, when children are silent and proud, and try to keep back their tears when they are in great trouble and suddenly break down, their tears fall in streams. With those warm streams of tears, he suddenly wetted my face. He sobbed and shook as though he were in convulsions, and squeezed up against me as I sat on the stone. ‘Father,’ he kept crying, ‘dear father, how he insulted you! And I sobbed too. We sat shaking in each other’s arms. ‘Ilusha,’ I said to him, ‘Ilusha darling. No one saw us then. God alone saw us, I hope He will record it to my credit. And he ordered hot baths for Nina with something dissolved in them, morning and evening. All her right side aches at night, she is in agony, and, would you believe it, the angel bears it without groaning for fear of waking us. We eat what we can get, and she’ll only take the leavings, what you’d scarcely give to a dog. ‘I am not worth it, I am taking it from you, I am a burden on you,’ that’s what her angel eyes try to express.
