title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ech, it’s not a secret, and you know it, too,” Grushenka said, in a voice suddenly anxious, turning her head towards Rakitin, and drawing a little away from Alyosha, though she still sat on his knee with her arm round his neck.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My officer is coming, Rakitin, my officer is coming.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I heard he was coming, but is he so near?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is at Mokroe now; he’ll send a messenger from there, so he wrote; I got a letter from him to-day. I am expecting the messenger every minute.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You don’t say so! Why at Mokroe?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a long story, I’ve told you enough.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya’ll be up to something now—I say! Does he know or doesn’t he?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He know! Of course he doesn’t. If he knew, there would be murder. But I am not afraid of that now, I am not afraid of his knife. Be quiet, Rakitin, don’t remind me of Dmitri Fyodorovitch, he has bruised my heart. And I don’t want to think of that at this moment. I can think of Alyosha here, I can look at Alyosha ... smile at me, dear, cheer up, smile at my foolishness, at my pleasure.... Ah, he’s smiling, he’s smiling! How kindly he looks at me! And you know, Alyosha, I’ve been thinking all this time you were angry with me, because of the day before yesterday, because of that young lady. I was a cur, that’s the truth.... But it’s a good thing it happened so. It was a horrid thing, but a good thing too. Grushenka smiled dreamily and a little cruel line showed in her smile. “Mitya told me that she screamed out that I ‘ought to be flogged. I did insult her dreadfully. She sent for me, she wanted to make a conquest of me, to win me over with her chocolate.... No, it’s a good thing it did end like that. She smiled again. “But I am still afraid of your being angry.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, that’s really true,” Rakitin put in suddenly with genuine surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, she is really afraid of a chicken like you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is a chicken to you, Rakitin ... because you’ve no conscience, that’s what it is! You see, I love him with all my soul, that’s how it is! Alyosha, do you believe I love you with all my soul?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, you shameless woman! She is making you a declaration, Alexey!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, what of it, I love him!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And what about your officer? And the priceless message from Mokroe?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That is quite different.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a woman’s way of looking at it!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t you make me angry, Rakitin. Grushenka caught him up hotly. “This is quite different. I love Alyosha in a different way. It’s true, Alyosha, I had sly designs on you before. For I am a horrid, violent creature. But at other times I’ve looked upon you, Alyosha, as my conscience. I’ve kept thinking ‘how any one like that must despise a nasty thing like me. I thought that the day before yesterday, as I ran home from the young lady’s. I have thought of you a long time in that way, Alyosha, and Mitya knows, I’ve talked to him about it. Mitya understands. Would you believe it, I sometimes look at you and feel ashamed, utterly ashamed of myself.... And how, and since when, I began to think about you like that, I can’t say, I don’t remember....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Fenya came in and put a tray with an uncorked bottle and three glasses of champagne on the table.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here’s the champagne!” cried Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re excited, Agrafena Alexandrovna, and not yourself. When you’ve had a glass of champagne, you’ll be ready to dance. Eh, they can’t even do that properly,” he added, looking at the bottle.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The old woman’s poured it out in the kitchen and the bottle’s been brought in warm and without a cork. Well, let me have some, anyway.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went up to the table, took a glass, emptied it at one gulp and poured himself out another.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “One doesn’t often stumble upon champagne,” he said, licking his lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Now, Alyosha, take a glass, show what you can do! What shall we drink to? The gates of paradise? Take a glass, Grushenka, you drink to the gates of paradise, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What gates of paradise?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She took a glass, Alyosha took his, tasted it and put it back.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I’d better not,” he smiled gently.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And you bragged!” cried Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, if so, I won’t either,” chimed in Grushenka, “I really don’t want any. You can drink the whole bottle alone, Rakitin. If Alyosha has some, I will.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What touching sentimentality!” said Rakitin tauntingly; “and she’s sitting on his knee, too! He’s got something to grieve over, but what’s the matter with you? He is rebelling against his God and ready to eat sausage....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How so?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “His elder died to-day, Father Zossima, the saint.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So Father Zossima is dead,” cried Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good God, I did not know!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She crossed herself devoutly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Goodness, what have I been doing, sitting on his knee like this at such a moment!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She started up as though in dismay, instantly slipped off his knee and sat down on the sofa.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha bent a long wondering look upon her and a light seemed to dawn in his face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Rakitin,” he said suddenly, in a firm and loud voice; “don’t taunt me with having rebelled against God. I don’t want to feel angry with you, so you must be kinder, too, I’ve lost a treasure such as you have never had, and you cannot judge me now. You had much better look at her—do you see how she has pity on me? I came here to find a wicked soul—I felt drawn to evil because I was base and evil myself, and I’ve found a true sister, I have found a treasure—a loving heart. She had pity on me just now.... Agrafena Alexandrovna, I am speaking of you. You’ve raised my soul from the depths.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha’s lips were quivering and he caught his breath.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She has saved you, it seems,” laughed Rakitin spitefully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And she meant to get you in her clutches, do you realize that?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Stay, Rakitin. Grushenka jumped up. “Hush, both of you. Now I’ll tell you all about it. Hush, Alyosha, your words make me ashamed, for I am bad and not good—that’s what I am. And you hush, Rakitin, because you are telling lies. I had the low idea of trying to get him in my clutches, but now you are lying, now it’s all different. And don’t let me hear anything more from you, Rakitin.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All this Grushenka said with extreme emotion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They are both crazy,” said Rakitin, looking at them with amazement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I feel as though I were in a madhouse. They’re both getting so feeble they’ll begin crying in a minute.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall begin to cry, I shall,” repeated Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He called me his sister and I shall never forget that. Only let me tell you, Rakitin, though I am bad, I did give away an onion.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “An onion? Hang it all, you really are crazy.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin wondered at their enthusiasm.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was aggrieved and annoyed, though he might have reflected that each of them was just passing through a spiritual crisis such as does not come often in a lifetime.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But though Rakitin was very sensitive about everything that concerned himself, he was very obtuse as regards the feelings and sensations of others—partly from his youth and inexperience, partly from his intense egoism.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You see, Alyosha,” Grushenka turned to him with a nervous laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I was boasting when I told Rakitin I had given away an onion, but it’s not to boast I tell you about it. It’s only a story, but it’s a nice story. I used to hear it when I was a child from Matryona, my cook, who is still with me. It’s like this. Once upon a time there was a peasant woman and a very wicked woman she was. And she died and did not leave a single good deed behind. The devils caught her and plunged her into the lake of fire. So her guardian angel stood and wondered what good deed of hers he could remember to tell to God; ‘She once pulled up an onion in her garden,’ said he, ‘and gave it to a beggar woman. And God answered: ‘You take that onion then, hold it out to her in the lake, and let her take hold and be pulled out. And if you can pull her out of the lake, let her come to Paradise, but if the onion breaks, then the woman must stay where she is. The angel ran to the woman and held out the onion to her. ‘Come,’ said he, ‘catch hold and I’ll pull you out. And he began cautiously pulling her out. He had just pulled her right out, when the other sinners in the lake, seeing how she was being drawn out, began catching hold of her so as to be pulled out with her. But she was a very wicked woman and she began kicking them. ‘I’m to be pulled out, not you. It’s my onion, not yours. As soon as she said that, the onion broke. And the woman fell into the lake and she is burning there to this day. So the angel wept and went away. So that’s the story, Alyosha; I know it by heart, for I am that wicked woman myself. I boasted to Rakitin that I had given away an onion, but to you I’ll say: ‘I’ve done nothing but give away one onion all my life, that’s the only good deed I’ve done. So don’t praise me, Alyosha, don’t think me good, I am bad, I am a wicked woman and you make me ashamed if you praise me. Eh, I must confess everything. Listen, Alyosha. I was so anxious to get hold of you that I promised Rakitin twenty-five roubles if he would bring you to me. Stay, Rakitin, wait!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She went with rapid steps to the table, opened a drawer, pulled out a purse and took from it a twenty-five rouble note.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What nonsense! What nonsense!” cried Rakitin, disconcerted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Take it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin, I owe it you, there’s no fear of your refusing it, you asked for it yourself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she threw the note to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Likely I should refuse it,” boomed Rakitin, obviously abashed, but carrying off his confusion with a swagger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That will come in very handy; fools are made for wise men’s profit.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And now hold your tongue, Rakitin, what I am going to say now is not for your ears. Sit down in that corner and keep quiet. You don’t like us, so hold your tongue.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What should I like you for?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Rakitin snarled, not concealing his ill-humor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He put the twenty-five rouble note in his pocket and he felt ashamed at Alyosha’s seeing it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had reckoned on receiving his payment later, without Alyosha’s knowing of it, and now, feeling ashamed, he lost his temper.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Till that moment he had thought it discreet not to contradict Grushenka too flatly in spite of her snubbing, since he had something to get out of her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But now he, too, was angry:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “One loves people for some reason, but what have either of you done for me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You should love people without a reason, as Alyosha does.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How does he love you? How has he shown it, that you make such a fuss about it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka was standing in the middle of the room; she spoke with heat and there were hysterical notes in her voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hush, Rakitin, you know nothing about us! And don’t dare to speak to me like that again. How dare you be so familiar! Sit in that corner and be quiet, as though you were my footman! And now, Alyosha, I’ll tell you the whole truth, that you may see what a wretch I am! I am not talking to Rakitin, but to you. I wanted to ruin you, Alyosha, that’s the holy truth; I quite meant to. I wanted to so much, that I bribed Rakitin to bring you. And why did I want to do such a thing? You knew nothing about it, Alyosha, you turned away from me; if you passed me, you dropped your eyes. And I’ve looked at you a hundred times before to-day; I began asking every one about you. Your face haunted my heart. ‘He despises me,’ I thought; ‘he won’t even look at me. And I felt it so much at last that I wondered at myself for being so frightened of a boy. I’ll get him in my clutches and laugh at him. I was full of spite and anger. Would you believe it, nobody here dares talk or think of coming to Agrafena Alexandrovna with any evil purpose. Old Kuzma is the only man I have anything to do with here; I was bound and sold to him; Satan brought us together, but there has been no one else. But looking at you, I thought, I’ll get him in my clutches and laugh at him. You see what a spiteful cur I am, and you called me your sister! And now that man who wronged me has come; I sit here waiting for a message from him. And do you know what that man has been to me? Five years ago, when Kuzma brought me here, I used to shut myself up, that no one might have sight or sound of me. I was a silly slip of a girl; I used to sit here sobbing; I used to lie awake all night, thinking: ‘Where is he now, the man who wronged me? He is laughing at me with another woman, most likely. If only I could see him, if I could meet him again, I’d pay him out, I’d pay him out! At night I used to lie sobbing into my pillow in the dark, and I used to brood over it; I used to tear my heart on purpose and gloat over my anger. ‘I’ll pay him out, I’ll pay him out! That’s what I used to cry out in the dark. And when I suddenly thought that I should really do nothing to him, and that he was laughing at me then, or perhaps had utterly forgotten me, I would fling myself on the floor, melt into helpless tears, and lie there shaking till dawn. In the morning I would get up more spiteful than a dog, ready to tear the whole world to pieces. And then what do you think? I began saving money, I became hard-hearted, grew stout—grew wiser, would you say? No, no one in the whole world sees it, no one knows it, but when night comes on, I sometimes lie as I did five years ago, when I was a silly girl, clenching my teeth and crying all night, thinking, ‘I’ll pay him out, I’ll pay him out! Do you hear? Well then, now you understand me. A month ago a letter came to me—he was coming, he was a widower, he wanted to see me. It took my breath away; then I suddenly thought: ‘If he comes and whistles to call me, I shall creep back to him like a beaten dog. I couldn’t believe myself. Am I so abject? Shall I run to him or not? And I’ve been in such a rage with myself all this month that I am worse than I was five years ago. Do you see now, Alyosha, what a violent, vindictive creature I am? I have shown you the whole truth! I played with Mitya to keep me from running to that other. Hush, Rakitin, it’s not for you to judge me, I am not speaking to you. Before you came in, I was lying here waiting, brooding, deciding my whole future life, and you can never know what was in my heart. Yes, Alyosha, tell your young lady not to be angry with me for what happened the day before yesterday.... Nobody in the whole world knows what I am going through now, and no one ever can know.... For perhaps I shall take a knife with me to-day, I can’t make up my mind ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And at this “tragic” phrase Grushenka broke down, hid her face in her hands, flung herself on the sofa pillows, and sobbed like a little child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha got up and went to Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Misha,” he said, “don’t be angry. She wounded you, but don’t be angry. You heard what she said just now? You mustn’t ask too much of human endurance, one must be merciful.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha said this at the instinctive prompting of his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt obliged to speak and he turned to Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If Rakitin had not been there, he would have spoken to the air.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Rakitin looked at him ironically and Alyosha stopped short.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You were so primed up with your elder’s teaching last night that now you have to let it off on me, Alexey, man of God!” said Rakitin, with a smile of hatred.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t laugh, Rakitin, don’t smile, don’t talk of the dead—he was better than any one in the world!” cried Alyosha, with tears in his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I didn’t speak to you as a judge but as the lowest of the judged. What am I beside her? I came here seeking my ruin, and said to myself, ‘What does it matter?’ in my cowardliness, but she, after five years in torment, as soon as any one says a word from the heart to her—it makes her forget everything, forgive everything, in her tears! The man who has wronged her has come back, he sends for her and she forgives him everything, and hastens joyfully to meet him and she won’t take a knife with her. She won’t! No, I am not like that. I don’t know whether you are, Misha, but I am not like that. It’s a lesson to me.... She is more loving than we.... Have you heard her speak before of what she has just told us? No, you haven’t; if you had, you’d have understood her long ago ... and the person insulted the day before yesterday must forgive her, too! She will, when she knows ... and she shall know.... This soul is not yet at peace with itself, one must be tender with it ... there may be a treasure in that soul....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha stopped, because he caught his breath.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In spite of his ill-humor Rakitin looked at him with astonishment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had never expected such a tirade from the gentle Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “She’s found some one to plead her cause! Why, are you in love with her? Agrafena Alexandrovna, our monk’s really in love with you, you’ve made a conquest!” he cried, with a coarse laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka lifted her head from the pillow and looked at Alyosha with a tender smile shining on her tear-stained face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Let him alone, Alyosha, my cherub; you see what he is, he is not a person for you to speak to. Mihail Osipovitch,” she turned to Rakitin, “I meant to beg your pardon for being rude to you, but now I don’t want to. Alyosha, come to me, sit down here. She beckoned to him with a happy smile. “That’s right, sit here. Tell me,” she shook him by the hand and peeped into his face, smiling, “tell me, do I love that man or not? the man who wronged me, do I love him or not? Before you came, I lay here in the dark, asking my heart whether I loved him. Decide for me, Alyosha, the time has come, it shall be as you say. Am I to forgive him or not?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But you have forgiven him already,” said Alyosha, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I really have forgiven him,” Grushenka murmured thoughtfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What an abject heart!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To my abject heart!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She snatched up a glass from the table, emptied it at a gulp, lifted it in the air and flung it on the floor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The glass broke with a crash.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A little cruel line came into her smile.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps I haven’t forgiven him, though,” she said, with a sort of menace in her voice, and she dropped her eyes to the ground as though she were talking to herself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perhaps my heart is only getting ready to forgive. I shall struggle with my heart. You see, Alyosha, I’ve grown to love my tears in these five years.... Perhaps I only love my resentment, not him ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, I shouldn’t care to be in his shoes,” hissed Rakitin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, you won’t be, Rakitin, you’ll never be in his shoes. You shall black my shoes, Rakitin, that’s the place you are fit for. You’ll never get a woman like me ... and he won’t either, perhaps ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Won’t he? Then why are you dressed up like that?” said Rakitin, with a venomous sneer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t taunt me with dressing up, Rakitin, you don’t know all that is in my heart! If I choose to tear off my finery, I’ll tear it off at once, this minute,” she cried in a resonant voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You don’t know what that finery is for, Rakitin! Perhaps I shall see him and say: ‘Have you ever seen me look like this before? He left me a thin, consumptive cry-baby of seventeen. I’ll sit by him, fascinate him and work him up. ‘Do you see what I am like now? I’ll say to him; ‘well, and that’s enough for you, my dear sir, there’s many a slip twixt the cup and the lip! title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How much in the bank? To correspond?” asked Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s according, panie, maybe a hundred, maybe two hundred, as much as you will stake.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A million!” laughed Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The Pan Captain has heard of Pan Podvysotsky, perhaps?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What Podvysotsky?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In Warsaw there was a bank and any one comes and stakes against it. Podvysotsky comes, sees a thousand gold pieces, stakes against the bank. The banker says, ‘Panie Podvysotsky, are you laying down the gold, or must we trust to your honor? ‘To my honor, panie,’ says Podvysotsky. ‘So much the better. The banker throws the dice. Podvysotsky wins. ‘Take it, panie,’ says the banker, and pulling out the drawer he gives him a million. ‘Take it, panie, this is your gain. There was a million in the bank. ‘I didn’t know that,’ says Podvysotsky. ‘Panie Podvysotsky,’ said the banker, ‘you pledged your honor and we pledged ours. Podvysotsky took the million.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s not true,” said Kalganov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Panie Kalganov, in gentlemanly society one doesn’t say such things.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As if a Polish gambler would give away a million!” cried Mitya, but checked himself at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Forgive me, panie, it’s my fault again, he would, he would give away a million, for honor, for Polish honor. You see how I talk Polish, ha ha! Here, I stake ten roubles, the knave leads.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I put a rouble on the queen, the queen of hearts, the pretty little panienotchka, he he!” laughed Maximov, pulling out his queen, and, as though trying to conceal it from every one, he moved right up and crossed himself hurriedly under the table.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya won.

text: “Lost!” shouted Mitya.

text: “Double!

text: Double!

text: The rouble stakes kept winning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’ve lost two hundred, panie. Will you stake another hundred?” the Pole on the sofa inquired.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: “What’s the matter?

text: “Why?”

text: Mitya gazed at him in astonishment.

text: “How dare you!

text: “Ah, you turkey-cocks!”

text: Mitya looked at each of them in turn.

text: But something in Grushenka’s face suddenly struck him, and at the same instant something new flashed into his mind—a strange new thought!

text: “What do you want?”

text: “March, panovie!”

text: There was a sort of boldness, a sudden confidence shining in his eyes.

text: His face had looked very different when he entered the room an hour before.

text: He led the Poles, not into the large room where the chorus of girls was assembling and the table was being laid, but into the bedroom on the right, where the trunks and packages were kept, and there were two large beds, with pyramids of cotton pillows on each.

text: There was a lighted candle on a small deal table in the corner.

text: The Poles looked severe but were evidently inquisitive.

text: “What can I do for you, panie?” lisped the little Pole.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Three thousand, panie?

text: He exchanged glances with Vrublevsky.

text: Mitya awaited an answer with assurance.

text: He had no doubts.

text: An expression of extraordinary resolution passed over the Pole’s face.

text: “And the money, panie?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The Poles exchanged glances again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The short man’s face looked more forbidding.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Seven hundred, seven hundred, not five hundred, at once, this minute, cash down! Mitya added, feeling something wrong. “What’s the matter, panie? Don’t you trust me? I can’t give you the whole three thousand straight off. If I give it, you may come back to her to-morrow.... Besides, I haven’t the three thousand with me. I’ve got it at home in the town,” faltered Mitya, his spirit sinking at every word he uttered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Upon my word, the money’s there, hidden.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In an instant an extraordinary sense of personal dignity showed itself in the little man’s face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What next?” he asked ironically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “For shame!” and he spat on the floor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Pan Vrublevsky spat too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You do that, panie,” said Mitya, recognizing with despair that all was over, “because you hope to make more out of Grushenka? You’re a couple of capons, that’s what you are!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “This is a mortal insult!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The little Pole turned as red as a crab, and he went out of the room, briskly, as though unwilling to hear another word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Vrublevsky swung out after him, and Mitya followed, confused and crestfallen.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was afraid of Grushenka, afraid that the pan would at once raise an outcry.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so indeed he did.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The Pole walked into the room and threw himself in a theatrical attitude before Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Pani Agrippina, I have received a mortal insult!” he exclaimed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Grushenka suddenly lost all patience, as though they had wounded her in the tenderest spot.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Speak Russian! Speak Russian!” she cried, “not another word of Polish! You used to talk Russian. You can’t have forgotten it in five years.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was red with passion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Pani Agrippina—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My name’s Agrafena, Grushenka, speak Russian or I won’t listen!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The Pole gasped with offended dignity, and quickly and pompously delivered himself in broken Russian:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Pani Agrafena, I came here to forget the past and forgive it, to forget all that has happened till to-day—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Forgive?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Came here to forgive me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka cut him short, jumping up from her seat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Just so, pani, I’m not pusillanimous, I’m magnanimous. But I was astounded when I saw your lovers. Pan Mitya offered me three thousand, in the other room to depart. I spat in the pan’s face.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What? He offered you money for me?” cried Grushenka, hysterically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is it true, Mitya? How dare you? Am I for sale?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Panie, panie!” yelled Mitya, “she’s pure and shining, and I have never been her lover! That’s a lie....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How dare you defend me to him?” shrieked Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It wasn’t virtue kept me pure, and it wasn’t that I was afraid of Kuzma, but that I might hold up my head when I met him, and tell him he’s a scoundrel. And he did actually refuse the money?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He took it! He took it!” cried Mitya; “only he wanted to get the whole three thousand at once, and I could only give him seven hundred straight off.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I see: he heard I had money, and came here to marry me!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Pani Agrippina!” cried the little Pole.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m—a knight, I’m—a nobleman, and not a lajdak. I came here to make you my wife and I find you a different woman, perverse and shameless.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, go back where you came from! I’ll tell them to turn you out and you’ll be turned out,” cried Grushenka, furious.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve been a fool, a fool, to have been miserable these five years! And it wasn’t for his sake, it was my anger made me miserable. And this isn’t he at all! Was he like this? It might be his father! Where did you get your wig from? He was a falcon, but this is a gander. He used to laugh and sing to me.... And I’ve been crying for five years, damned fool, abject, shameless I was!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She sank back in her low chair and hid her face in her hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At that instant the chorus of Mokroe began singing in the room on the left—a rollicking dance song.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A regular Sodom! Vrublevsky roared suddenly. “Landlord, send the shameless hussies away!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The landlord, who had been for some time past inquisitively peeping in at the door, hearing shouts and guessing that his guests were quarreling, at once entered the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What are you shouting for? D’you want to split your throat?” he said, addressing Vrublevsky, with surprising rudeness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Animal!” bellowed Pan Vrublevsky.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Animal? And what sort of cards were you playing with just now? I gave you a pack and you hid it. You played with marked cards! I could send you to Siberia for playing with false cards, d’you know that, for it’s just the same as false banknotes....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And going up to the sofa he thrust his fingers between the sofa back and the cushion, and pulled out an unopened pack of cards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here’s my pack unopened!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He held it up and showed it to all in the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “From where I stood I saw him slip my pack away, and put his in place of it—you’re a cheat and not a gentleman!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I twice saw the pan change a card!” cried Kalganov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How shameful! How shameful!” exclaimed Grushenka, clasping her hands, and blushing for genuine shame.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good Lord, he’s come to that!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I thought so, too!” said Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But before he had uttered the words, Vrublevsky, with a confused and infuriated face, shook his fist at Grushenka, shouting:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You low harlot!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya flew at him at once, clutched him in both hands, lifted him in the air, and in one instant had carried him into the room on the right, from which they had just come.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve laid him on the floor, there,” he announced, returning at once, gasping with excitement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s struggling, the scoundrel! But he won’t come back, no fear of that!...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He closed one half of the folding doors, and holding the other ajar called out to the little Pole:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Most illustrious, will you be pleased to retire as well?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My dear Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” said Trifon Borissovitch, “make them give you back the money you lost. It’s as good as stolen from you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t want my fifty roubles back,” Kalganov declared suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t want my two hundred, either,” cried Mitya, “I wouldn’t take it for anything! Let him keep it as a consolation.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Bravo, Mitya! You’re a trump, Mitya!” cried Grushenka, and there was a note of fierce anger in the exclamation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The little pan, crimson with fury but still mindful of his dignity, was making for the door, but he stopped short and said suddenly, addressing Grushenka:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Pani, if you want to come with me, come. If not, good-by.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And swelling with indignation and importance he went to the door.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was a man of character: he had so good an opinion of himself that after all that had passed, he still expected that she would marry him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya slammed the door after him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Lock it,” said Kalganov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the key clicked on the other side, they had locked it from within.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s capital!” exclaimed Grushenka relentlessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Serve them right!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What followed was almost an orgy, a feast to which all were welcome.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka was the first to call for wine.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I want to drink. I want to be quite drunk, as we were before. Do you remember, Mitya, do you remember how we made friends here last time!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya himself was almost delirious, feeling that his happiness was at hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Grushenka was continually sending him away from her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Go and enjoy yourself. Tell them to dance, to make merry, ‘let the stove and cottage dance’; as we had it last time,” she kept exclaiming.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was tremendously excited.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And Mitya hastened to obey her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The chorus were in the next room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The room in which they had been sitting till that moment was too small, and was divided in two by cotton curtains, behind which was a huge bed with a puffy feather mattress and a pyramid of cotton pillows.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the four rooms for visitors there were beds.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka settled herself just at the door.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya set an easy chair for her.

text: She had sat in the same place to watch the dancing and singing “the time before,” when they had made merry there.

text: All the girls who had come had been there then; the Jewish band with fiddles and zithers had come, too, and at last the long expected cart had arrived with the wines and provisions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya bustled about.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All sorts of people began coming into the room to look on, peasants and their women, who had been roused from sleep and attracted by the hopes of another marvelous entertainment such as they had enjoyed a month before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya remembered their faces, greeting and embracing every one he knew.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He uncorked bottles and poured out wine for every one who presented himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Only the girls were very eager for the champagne.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The men preferred rum, brandy, and, above all, hot punch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya had chocolate made for all the girls, and ordered that three samovars should be kept boiling all night to provide tea and punch for everyone to help himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: An absurd chaotic confusion followed, but Mitya was in his natural element, and the more foolish it became, the more his spirits rose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If the peasants had asked him for money at that moment, he would have pulled out his notes and given them away right and left.

text: This was probably why the landlord, Trifon Borissovitch, kept hovering about Mitya to protect him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He seemed to have given up all idea of going to bed that night; but he drank little, only one glass of punch, and kept a sharp look-out on Mitya’s interests after his own fashion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They’re a lousy lot, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” he said.

text: Mitya remembered Andrey again, and ordered punch to be sent out to him.

text: Maximov, blissfully drunk, never left his side.

text: Grushenka, too, was beginning to get drunk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Pointing to Kalganov, she said to Mitya:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What a dear, charming boy he is!”

text: And Mitya, delighted, ran to kiss Kalganov and Maximov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, great were his hopes!

text: “Thanks. You’re tired perhaps? What are you looking for here? Would you like some sweets? A cigar, perhaps?”

text: “A cigarette.”

text: “I’ll just have a liqueur.... Have you any chocolates?”

text: “Yes, there’s a heap of them on the table there. Choose one, my dear soul!”

text: “I like one with vanilla ... for old people. He he!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I say,” the old man bent down to whisper in Mitya’s ear.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That girl there, little Marya, he he! How would it be if you were to help me make friends with her?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So that’s what you’re after! No, brother, that won’t do!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’d do no harm to any one,” Maximov muttered disconsolately.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, all right, all right. They only come here to dance and sing, you know, brother. But damn it all, wait a bit!... Eat and drink and be merry, meanwhile. Don’t you want money?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Later on, perhaps,” smiled Maximov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “All right, all right....”

text: Mitya’s head was burning.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went outside to the wooden balcony which ran round the whole building on the inner side, overlooking the courtyard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The fresh air revived him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He stood alone in a dark corner, and suddenly clutched his head in both hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His scattered thoughts came together; his sensations blended into a whole and threw a sudden light into his mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A fearful and terrible light!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “If I’m to shoot myself, why not now?” passed through his mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why not go for the pistols, bring them here, and here, in this dark dirty corner, make an end?

text: Almost a minute he stood, undecided.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A few hours earlier, when he had been dashing here, he was pursued by disgrace, by the theft he had committed, and that blood, that blood!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But yet it was easier for him then.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then everything was over: he had lost her, given her up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was gone, for him—oh, then his death sentence had been easier for him; at least it had seemed necessary, inevitable, for what had he to stay on earth for?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But now?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Was it the same as then?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Now one phantom, one terror at least was at an end: that first, rightful lover, that fateful figure had vanished, leaving no trace.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The terrible phantom had turned into something so small, so comic; it had been carried into the bedroom and locked in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It would never return.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was ashamed, and from her eyes he could see now whom she loved.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Now he had everything to make life happy ... but he could not go on living, he could not; oh, damnation!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “O God! restore to life the man I knocked down at the fence! Let this fearful cup pass from me! Lord, thou hast wrought miracles for such sinners as me! But what, what if the old man’s alive? Oh, then the shame of the other disgrace I would wipe away. I would restore the stolen money. I’d give it back; I’d get it somehow.... No trace of that shame will remain except in my heart for ever! But no, no; oh, impossible cowardly dreams! Oh, damnation!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet there was a ray of light and hope in his darkness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He jumped up and ran back to the room—to her, to her, his queen for ever!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Was not one moment of her love worth all the rest of life, even in the agonies of disgrace?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This wild question clutched at his heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To her, to her alone, to see her, to hear her, to think of nothing, to forget everything, if only for that night, for an hour, for a moment!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Just as he turned from the balcony into the passage, he came upon the landlord, Trifon Borissovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He thought he looked gloomy and worried, and fancied he had come to find him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is it, Trifon Borissovitch? are you looking for me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, sir. The landlord seemed disconcerted. “Why should I be looking for you? Where have you been?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why do you look so glum? You’re not angry, are you? Wait a bit, you shall soon get to bed.... What’s the time?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’ll be three o’clock. Past three, it must be.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We’ll leave off soon. We’ll leave off.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t mention it; it doesn’t matter. Keep it up as long as you like....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What’s the matter with him?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya wondered for an instant, and he ran back to the room where the girls were dancing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But she was not there.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was not in the blue room either; there was no one but Kalganov asleep on the sofa.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya peeped behind the curtain—she was there.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was sitting in the corner, on a trunk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Bent forward, with her head and arms on the bed close by, she was crying bitterly, doing her utmost to stifle her sobs that she might not be heard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Seeing Mitya, she beckoned him to her, and when he ran to her, she grasped his hand tightly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya, Mitya, I loved him, you know. How I have loved him these five years, all that time! Did I love him or only my own anger? No, him, him! It’s a lie that it was my anger I loved and not him. Mitya, I was only seventeen then; he was so kind to me, so merry; he used to sing to me.... Or so it seemed to a silly girl like me.... And now, O Lord, it’s not the same man. Even his face is not the same; he’s different altogether. I shouldn’t have known him. I drove here with Timofey, and all the way I was thinking how I should meet him, what I should say to him, how we should look at one another. My soul was faint, and all of a sudden it was just as though he had emptied a pail of dirty water over me. He talked to me like a schoolmaster, all so grave and learned; he met me so solemnly that I was struck dumb. I couldn’t get a word in. At first I thought he was ashamed to talk before his great big Pole. I sat staring at him and wondering why I couldn’t say a word to him now. It must have been his wife that ruined him; you know he threw me up to get married. She must have changed him like that. Mitya, how shameful it is! Oh, Mitya, I’m ashamed, I’m ashamed for all my life. Curse it, curse it, curse those five years!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And again she burst into tears, but clung tight to Mitya’s hand and did not let it go.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya, darling, stay, don’t go away. I want to say one word to you,” she whispered, and suddenly raised her face to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Listen, tell me who it is I love? I love one man here. Who is that man? That’s what you must tell me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A smile lighted up her face that was swollen with weeping, and her eyes shone in the half darkness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A falcon flew in, and my heart sank.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘Fool! that’s the man you love! That was what my heart whispered to me at once. You came in and all grew bright. What’s he afraid of? I wondered. For you were frightened; you couldn’t speak. It’s not them he’s afraid of—could you be frightened of any one? It’s me he’s afraid of, I thought, only me. So Fenya told you, you little stupid, how I called to Alyosha out of the window that I’d loved Mityenka for one hour, and that I was going now to love ... another.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya, Mitya, how could I be such a fool as to think I could love any one after you?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Do you forgive me, Mitya?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Do you forgive me or not?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Do you love me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Do you love me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She jumped up and held him with both hands on his shoulders.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya, dumb with rapture, gazed into her eyes, at her face, at her smile, and suddenly clasped her tightly in his arms and kissed her passionately.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You will forgive me for having tormented you? It was through spite I tormented you all. It was for spite I drove the old man out of his mind.... Do you remember how you drank at my house one day and broke the wine-glass? I remembered that and I broke a glass to-day and drank ‘to my vile heart. Mitya, my falcon, why don’t you kiss me? He kissed me once, and now he draws back and looks and listens. Why listen to me? Kiss me, kiss me hard, that’s right. If you love, well, then, love! I’ll be your slave now, your slave for the rest of my life. It’s sweet to be a slave. Kiss me! Beat me, ill-treat me, do what you will with me.... And I do deserve to suffer. Stay, wait, afterwards, I won’t have that....” she suddenly thrust him away. “Go along, Mitya, I’ll come and have some wine, I want to be drunk, I’m going to get drunk and dance; I must, I must!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She tore herself away from him and disappeared behind the curtain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya followed like a drunken man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, come what may—whatever may happen now, for one minute I’d give the whole world,” he thought.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka did, in fact, toss off a whole glass of champagne at one gulp, and became at once very tipsy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She sat down in the same chair as before, with a blissful smile on her face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her cheeks were glowing, her lips were burning, her flashing eyes were moist; there was passionate appeal in her eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Even Kalganov felt a stir at the heart and went up to her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did you feel how I kissed you when you were asleep just now?” she said thickly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m drunk now, that’s what it is.... And aren’t you drunk? And why isn’t Mitya drinking? Why don’t you drink, Mitya? I’m drunk, and you don’t drink....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am drunk! I’m drunk as it is ... drunk with you ... and now I’ll be drunk with wine, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He drank off another glass, and—he thought it strange himself—that glass made him completely drunk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was suddenly drunk, although till that moment he had been quite sober, he remembered that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: From that moment everything whirled about him, as though he were delirious.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He walked, laughed, talked to everybody, without knowing what he was doing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Only one persistent burning sensation made itself felt continually, “like a red-hot coal in his heart,” he said afterwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He went up to her, sat beside her, gazed at her, listened to her....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She became very talkative, kept calling every one to her, and beckoned to different girls out of the chorus.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When the girl came up, she either kissed her, or made the sign of the cross over her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In another minute she might have cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was greatly amused by the “little old man,” as she called Maximov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran up every minute to kiss her hands, “each little finger,” and finally he danced another dance to an old song, which he sang himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He danced with special vigor to the refrain:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The little pig says—umph! umph! umph!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The little calf says—moo, moo, moo, The little duck says—quack, quack, quack, The little goose says—ga, ga, ga.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The hen goes strutting through the porch; Troo-roo-roo-roo-roo, she’ll say, Troo-roo-roo-roo-roo, she’ll say!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give him something, Mitya,” said Grushenka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give him a present, he’s poor, you know. Ah, the poor, the insulted!... Do you know, Mitya, I shall go into a nunnery. No, I really shall one day, Alyosha said something to me to-day that I shall remember all my life.... Yes.... But to-day let us dance. To-morrow to the nunnery, but to-day we’ll dance. I want to play to-day, good people, and what of it? God will forgive us. If I were God, I’d forgive every one: ‘My dear sinners, from this day forth I forgive you. I’m going to beg forgiveness: ‘Forgive me, good people, a silly wench. I’m a beast, that’s what I am. But I want to pray. I gave a little onion. Wicked as I’ve been, I want to pray. Mitya, let them dance, don’t stop them. Every one in the world is good. Every one—even the worst of them. The world’s a nice place. Though we’re bad the world’s all right. We’re good and bad, good and bad.... Come, tell me, I’ve something to ask you: come here every one, and I’ll ask you: Why am I so good? You know I am good. I’m very good.... Come, why am I so good?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So Grushenka babbled on, getting more and more drunk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At last she announced that she was going to dance, too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She got up from her chair, staggering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya, don’t give me any more wine—if I ask you, don’t give it to me. Wine doesn’t give peace. Everything’s going round, the stove, and everything. I want to dance. Let every one see how I dance ... let them see how beautifully I dance....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She really meant it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She pulled a white cambric handkerchief out of her pocket, and took it by one corner in her right hand, to wave it in the dance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya ran to and fro, the girls were quiet, and got ready to break into a dancing song at the first signal.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Maximov, hearing that Grushenka wanted to dance, squealed with delight, and ran skipping about in front of her, humming:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: With legs so slim and sides so trim And its little tail curled tight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Grushenka waved her handkerchief at him and drove him away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Sh-h! Mitya, why don’t they come? Let every one come ... to look on. Call them in, too, that were locked in.... Why did you lock them in? Tell them I’m going to dance. Let them look on, too....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya walked with a drunken swagger to the locked door, and began knocking to the Poles with his fist.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hi, you ... Podvysotskys! Come, she’s going to dance. She calls you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Lajdak!” one of the Poles shouted in reply.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re a lajdak yourself! You’re a little scoundrel, that’s what you are.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Leave off laughing at Poland,” said Kalganov sententiously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He too was drunk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Be quiet, boy! If I call him a scoundrel, it doesn’t mean that I called all Poland so. One lajdak doesn’t make a Poland. Be quiet, my pretty boy, eat a sweetmeat.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ach, what fellows! As though they were not men. Why won’t they make friends?” said Grushenka, and went forward to dance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The chorus broke into “Ah, my porch, my new porch!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka flung back her head, half opened her lips, smiled, waved her handkerchief, and suddenly, with a violent lurch, stood still in the middle of the room, looking bewildered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m weak....” she said in an exhausted voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Forgive me.... I’m weak, I can’t.... I’m sorry.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She bowed to the chorus, and then began bowing in all directions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’m sorry.... Forgive me....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The lady’s been drinking. The pretty lady has been drinking,” voices were heard saying.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The lady’s drunk too much,” Maximov explained to the girls, giggling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya, lead me away ... take me,” said Grushenka helplessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya pounced on her, snatched her up in his arms, and carried the precious burden through the curtains.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, now I’ll go,” thought Kalganov, and walking out of the blue room, he closed the two halves of the door after him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the orgy in the larger room went on and grew louder and louder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya laid Grushenka on the bed and kissed her on the lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t touch me....” she faltered, in an imploring voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t touch me, till I’m yours.... I’ve told you I’m yours, but don’t touch me ... spare me.... With them here, with them close, you mustn’t. He’s here. It’s nasty here....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll obey you! I won’t think of it ... I worship you!” muttered Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, it’s nasty here, it’s abominable.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And still holding her in his arms, he sank on his knees by the bedside.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know, though you’re a brute, you’re generous,” Grushenka articulated with difficulty.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It must be honorable ... it shall be honorable for the future ... and let us be honest, let us be good, not brutes, but good ... take me away, take me far away, do you hear? I don’t want it to be here, but far, far away....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, yes, yes, it must be!” said Mitya, pressing her in his arms.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll take you and we’ll fly away.... Oh, I’d give my whole life for one year only to know about that blood!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What blood?” asked Grushenka, bewildered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing,” muttered Mitya, through his teeth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Grusha, you wanted to be honest, but I’m a thief. But I’ve stolen money from Katya.... Disgrace, a disgrace!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “From Katya, from that young lady? No, you didn’t steal it. Give it her back, take it from me.... Why make a fuss? Now everything of mine is yours. What does money matter? We shall waste it anyway.... Folks like us are bound to waste money. But we’d better go and work the land. I want to dig the earth with my own hands. We must work, do you hear? Alyosha said so. I won’t be your mistress, I’ll be faithful to you, I’ll be your slave, I’ll work for you. We’ll go to the young lady and bow down to her together, so that she may forgive us, and then we’ll go away. And if she won’t forgive us, we’ll go, anyway. Take her her money and love me.... Don’t love her.... Don’t love her any more. If you love her, I shall strangle her.... I’ll put out both her eyes with a needle....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I love you. I love only you. I’ll love you in Siberia....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why Siberia? Never mind, Siberia, if you like. I don’t care ... we’ll work ... there’s snow in Siberia.... I love driving in the snow ... and must have bells.... Do you hear, there’s a bell ringing? Where is that bell ringing? There are people coming.... Now it’s stopped.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She closed her eyes, exhausted, and suddenly fell asleep for an instant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There had certainly been the sound of a bell in the distance, but the ringing had ceased.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya let his head sink on her breast.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did not notice that the bell had ceased ringing, nor did he notice that the songs had ceased, and that instead of singing and drunken clamor there was absolute stillness in the house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Grushenka opened her eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What’s the matter? Was I asleep? Yes ... a bell ... I’ve been asleep and dreamt I was driving over the snow with bells, and I dozed. I was with some one I loved, with you. And far, far away. I was holding you and kissing you, nestling close to you. I was cold, and the snow glistened.... You know how the snow glistens at night when the moon shines. It was as though I was not on earth. I woke up, and my dear one is close to me. How sweet that is!...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Close to you,” murmured Mitya, kissing her dress, her bosom, her hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And suddenly he had a strange fancy: it seemed to him that she was looking straight before her, not at him, not into his face, but over his head, with an intent, almost uncanny fixity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: An expression of wonder, almost of alarm, came suddenly into her face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mitya, who is that looking at us?” she whispered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya turned, and saw that some one had, in fact, parted the curtains and seemed to be watching them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And not one person alone, it seemed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He jumped up and walked quickly to the intruder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here, come to us, come here,” said a voice, speaking not loudly, but firmly and peremptorily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya passed to the other side of the curtain and stood stock still.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The room was filled with people, but not those who had been there before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: An instantaneous shiver ran down his back, and he shuddered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He recognized all those people instantly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That tall, stout old man in the overcoat and forage-cap with a cockade—was the police captain, Mihail Makarovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And that “consumptive-looking” trim dandy, “who always has such polished boots”—that was the deputy prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He has a chronometer worth four hundred roubles; he showed it to me. And that small young man in spectacles.... Mitya forgot his surname though he knew him, had seen him: he was the “investigating lawyer,” from the “school of jurisprudence,” who had only lately come to the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And this man—the inspector of police, Mavriky Mavrikyevitch, a man he knew well.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

text: He could never, even a minute before, have conceived that any one could behave like that to him, Mitya Karamazov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What was worst of all, there was something humiliating in it, and on their side something “supercilious and scornful. It was nothing to take off his coat, but he was asked to undress further, or rather not asked but “commanded,” he quite understood that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: From pride and contempt he submitted without a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Several peasants accompanied the lawyers and remained on the same side of the curtain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To be ready if force is required,” thought Mitya, “and perhaps for some other reason, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, must I take off my shirt, too?” he asked sharply, but Nikolay Parfenovitch did not answer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was busily engaged with the prosecutor in examining the coat, the trousers, the waistcoat and the cap; and it was evident that they were both much interested in the scrutiny.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “They make no bones about it,” thought Mitya, “they don’t keep up the most elementary politeness.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I ask you for the second time—need I take off my shirt or not?” he said, still more sharply and irritably.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t trouble yourself. We will tell you what to do,” Nikolay Parfenovitch said, and his voice was positively peremptory, or so it seemed to Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Meantime a consultation was going on in undertones between the lawyers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There turned out to be on the coat, especially on the left side at the back, a huge patch of blood, dry, and still stiff.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There were bloodstains on the trousers, too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch, moreover, in the presence of the peasant witnesses, passed his fingers along the collar, the cuffs, and all the seams of the coat and trousers, obviously looking for something—money, of course.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He didn’t even hide from Mitya his suspicion that he was capable of sewing money up in his clothes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He treats me not as an officer but as a thief,” Mitya muttered to himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They communicated their ideas to one another with amazing frankness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The secretary, for instance, who was also behind the curtain, fussing about and listening, called Nikolay Parfenovitch’s attention to the cap, which they were also fingering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You remember Gridyenko, the copying-clerk,” observed the secretary.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Last summer he received the wages of the whole office, and pretended to have lost the money when he was drunk. And where was it found? Why, in just such pipings in his cap. The hundred-rouble notes were screwed up in little rolls and sewed in the piping.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Both the lawyers remembered Gridyenko’s case perfectly, and so laid aside Mitya’s cap, and decided that all his clothes must be more thoroughly examined later.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Excuse me,” cried Nikolay Parfenovitch, suddenly, noticing that the right cuff of Mitya’s shirt was turned in, and covered with blood, “excuse me, what’s that, blood?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes,” Mitya jerked out.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That is, what blood? ... and why is the cuff turned in?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya told him how he had got the sleeve stained with blood looking after Grigory, and had turned it inside when he was washing his hands at Perhotin’s.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You must take off your shirt, too. That’s very important as material evidence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya flushed red and flew into a rage.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What, am I to stay naked?” he shouted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t disturb yourself. We will arrange something. And meanwhile take off your socks.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’re not joking?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is that really necessary?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya’s eyes flashed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We are in no mood for joking,” answered Nikolay Parfenovitch sternly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, if I must—” muttered Mitya, and sitting down on the bed, he took off his socks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt unbearably awkward.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All were clothed, while he was naked, and strange to say, when he was undressed he felt somehow guilty in their presence, and was almost ready to believe himself that he was inferior to them, and that now they had a perfect right to despise him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When all are undressed, one is somehow not ashamed, but when one’s the only one undressed and everybody is looking, it’s degrading,” he kept repeating to himself, again and again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s like a dream, I’ve sometimes dreamed of being in such degrading positions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a misery to him to take off his socks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They were very dirty, and so were his underclothes, and now every one could see it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And what was worse, he disliked his feet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All his life he had thought both his big toes hideous.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He particularly loathed the coarse, flat, crooked nail on the right one, and now they would all see it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Feeling intolerably ashamed made him, at once and intentionally, rougher.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He pulled off his shirt, himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Would you like to look anywhere else if you’re not ashamed to?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, there’s no need to, at present.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, am I to stay naked like this?” he added savagely.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, that can’t be helped for the time.... Kindly sit down here for a while. You can wrap yourself in a quilt from the bed, and I ... I’ll see to all this.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All the things were shown to the witnesses.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The report of the search was drawn up, and at last Nikolay Parfenovitch went out, and the clothes were carried out after him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ippolit Kirillovitch went out, too.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya was left alone with the peasants, who stood in silence, never taking their eyes off him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya wrapped himself up in the quilt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt cold.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His bare feet stuck out, and he couldn’t pull the quilt over so as to cover them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Nikolay Parfenovitch seemed to be gone a long time, “an insufferable time. “He thinks of me as a puppy,” thought Mitya, gnashing his teeth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That rotten prosecutor has gone, too, contemptuous no doubt, it disgusts him to see me naked!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya imagined, however, that his clothes would be examined and returned to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But what was his indignation when Nikolay Parfenovitch came back with quite different clothes, brought in behind him by a peasant.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here are clothes for you,” he observed airily, seeming well satisfied with the success of his mission.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mr. Kalganov has kindly provided these for this unusual emergency, as well as a clean shirt. Luckily he had them all in his trunk. You can keep your own socks and underclothes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya flew into a passion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I won’t have other people’s clothes!” he shouted menacingly, “give me my own!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s impossible!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give me my own. Damn Kalganov and his clothes, too!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was a long time before they could persuade him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But they succeeded somehow in quieting him down.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They impressed upon him that his clothes, being stained with blood, must be “included with the other material evidence,” and that they “had not even the right to let him have them now ... taking into consideration the possible outcome of the case. Mitya at last understood this. He subsided into gloomy silence and hurriedly dressed himself. He merely observed, as he put them on, that the clothes were much better than his old ones, and that he disliked “gaining by the change. The coat was, besides, “ridiculously tight. Am I to be dressed up like a fool ... for your amusement?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They urged upon him again that he was exaggerating, that Kalganov was only a little taller, so that only the trousers might be a little too long.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the coat turned out to be really tight in the shoulders.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Damn it all! I can hardly button it,” Mitya grumbled.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Be so good as to tell Mr. Kalganov from me that I didn’t ask for his clothes, and it’s not my doing that they’ve dressed me up like a clown.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He understands that, and is sorry ... I mean, not sorry to lend you his clothes, but sorry about all this business,” mumbled Nikolay Parfenovitch.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Confound his sorrow! Well, where now? Am I to go on sitting here?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was asked to go back to the “other room. Mitya went in, scowling with anger, and trying to avoid looking at any one. Dressed in another man’s clothes he felt himself disgraced, even in the eyes of the peasants, and of Trifon Borissovitch, whose face appeared, for some reason, in the doorway, and vanished immediately. “He’s come to look at me dressed up,” thought Mitya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He sat down on the same chair as before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had an absurd nightmarish feeling, as though he were out of his mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, what now? Are you going to flog me? That’s all that’s left for you,” he said, clenching his teeth and addressing the prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He would not turn to Nikolay Parfenovitch, as though he disdained to speak to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He looked too closely at my socks, and turned them inside out on purpose to show every one how dirty they were—the scoundrel!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, now we must proceed to the examination of witnesses,” observed Nikolay Parfenovitch, as though in reply to Mitya’s question.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes,” said the prosecutor thoughtfully, as though reflecting on something.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We’ve done what we could in your interest, Dmitri Fyodorovitch,” Nikolay Parfenovitch went on, “but having received from you such an uncompromising refusal to explain to us the source from which you obtained the money found upon you, we are, at the present moment—”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is the stone in your ring?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya interrupted suddenly, as though awakening from a reverie.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He pointed to one of the three large rings adorning Nikolay Parfenovitch’s right hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ring?” repeated Nikolay Parfenovitch with surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, that one ... on your middle finger, with the little veins in it, what stone is that?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya persisted, like a peevish child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s a smoky topaz,” said Nikolay Parfenovitch, smiling.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Would you like to look at it? I’ll take it off ...”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, don’t take it off,” cried Mitya furiously, suddenly waking up, and angry with himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Don’t take it off ... there’s no need.... Damn it!... Gentlemen, you’ve sullied my heart! Can you suppose that I would conceal it from you, if I had really killed my father, that I would shuffle, lie, and hide myself? No, that’s not like Dmitri Karamazov, that he couldn’t do, and if I were guilty, I swear I shouldn’t have waited for your coming, or for the sunrise as I meant at first, but should have killed myself before this, without waiting for the dawn! I know that about myself now. I couldn’t have learnt so much in twenty years as I’ve found out in this accursed night!... And should I have been like this on this night, and at this moment, sitting with you, could I have talked like this, could I have moved like this, could I have looked at you and at the world like this, if I had really been the murderer of my father, when the very thought of having accidentally killed Grigory gave me no peace all night—not from fear—oh, not simply from fear of your punishment! The disgrace of it! And you expect me to be open with such scoffers as you, who see nothing and believe in nothing, blind moles and scoffers, and to tell you another nasty thing I’ve done, another disgrace, even if that would save me from your accusation! No, better Siberia! The man who opened the door to my father and went in at that door, he killed him, he robbed him. Who was he? I’m racking my brains and can’t think who. But I can tell you it was not Dmitri Karamazov, and that’s all I can tell you, and that’s enough, enough, leave me alone.... Exile me, punish me, but don’t bother me any more. I’ll say no more. Call your witnesses!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya uttered his sudden monologue as though he were determined to be absolutely silent for the future.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor watched him the whole time and only when he had ceased speaking, observed, as though it were the most ordinary thing, with the most frigid and composed air:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, about the open door of which you spoke just now, we may as well inform you, by the way, now, of a very interesting piece of evidence of the greatest importance both to you and to us, that has been given us by Grigory, the old man you wounded. On his recovery, he clearly and emphatically stated, in reply to our questions, that when, on coming out to the steps, and hearing a noise in the garden, he made up his mind to go into it through the little gate which stood open, before he noticed you running, as you have told us already, in the dark from the open window where you saw your father, he, Grigory, glanced to the left, and, while noticing the open window, observed at the same time, much nearer to him, the door, standing wide open—that door which you have stated to have been shut the whole time you were in the garden. I will not conceal from you that Grigory himself confidently affirms and bears witness that you must have run from that door, though, of course, he did not see you do so with his own eyes, since he only noticed you first some distance away in the garden, running towards the fence.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mitya had leapt up from his chair half-way through this speech.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nonsense!” he yelled, in a sudden frenzy, “it’s a barefaced lie. He couldn’t have seen the door open because it was shut. He’s lying!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
