text: Since then she had been lavish in helping them, and the captain, terror-stricken at the thought that his boy might be dying, forgot his pride and humbly accepted her assistance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All this time Doctor Herzenstube, who was called in by Katerina Ivanovna, came punctually every other day, but little was gained by his visits and he dosed the invalid mercilessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But on that Sunday morning a new doctor was expected, who had come from Moscow, where he had a great reputation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Katerina Ivanovna had sent for him from Moscow at great expense, not expressly for Ilusha, but for another object of which more will be said in its place hereafter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, as he had come, she had asked him to see Ilusha as well, and the captain had been told to expect him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hadn’t the slightest idea that Kolya Krassotkin was coming, though he had long wished for a visit from the boy for whom Ilusha was fretting.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At the moment when Krassotkin opened the door and came into the room, the captain and all the boys were round Ilusha’s bed, looking at a tiny mastiff pup, which had only been born the day before, though the captain had bespoken it a week ago to comfort and amuse Ilusha, who was still fretting over the lost and probably dead Zhutchka.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha, who had heard three days before that he was to be presented with a puppy, not an ordinary puppy, but a pedigree mastiff (a very important point, of course), tried from delicacy of feeling to pretend that he was pleased.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his father and the boys could not help seeing that the puppy only served to recall to his little heart the thought of the unhappy dog he had killed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The puppy lay beside him feebly moving and he, smiling sadly, stroked it with his thin, pale, wasted hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Clearly he liked the puppy, but ... it wasn’t Zhutchka; if he could have had Zhutchka and the puppy, too, then he would have been completely happy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Krassotkin!” cried one of the boys suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was the first to see him come in.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin’s entrance made a general sensation; the boys moved away and stood on each side of the bed, so that he could get a full view of Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain ran eagerly to meet Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Please come in ... you are welcome!” he said hurriedly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ilusha, Mr. Krassotkin has come to see you!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Krassotkin, shaking hands with him hurriedly, instantly showed his complete knowledge of the manners of good society.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He turned first to the captain’s wife sitting in her arm-chair, who was very ill-humored at the moment, and was grumbling that the boys stood between her and Ilusha’s bed and did not let her see the new puppy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: With the greatest courtesy he made her a bow, scraping his foot, and turning to Nina, he made her, as the only other lady present, a similar bow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This polite behavior made an extremely favorable impression on the deranged lady.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There, you can see at once he is a young man that has been well brought up,” she commented aloud, throwing up her hands; “but as for our other visitors they come in one on the top of another.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you mean, mamma, one on the top of another, how is that?” muttered the captain affectionately, though a little anxious on her account.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s how they ride in. They get on each other’s shoulders in the passage and prance in like that on a respectable family. Strange sort of visitors!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But who’s come in like that, mamma?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why, that boy came in riding on that one’s back and this one on that one’s.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya was already by Ilusha’s bedside.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sick boy turned visibly paler.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He raised himself in the bed and looked intently at Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya had not seen his little friend for two months, and he was overwhelmed at the sight of him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had never imagined that he would see such a wasted, yellow face, such enormous, feverishly glowing eyes and such thin little hands.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He saw, with grieved surprise, Ilusha’s rapid, hard breathing and dry lips.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He stepped close to him, held out his hand, and almost overwhelmed, he said:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, old man ... how are you?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his voice failed him, he couldn’t achieve an appearance of ease; his face suddenly twitched and the corners of his mouth quivered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha smiled a pitiful little smile, still unable to utter a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Something moved Kolya to raise his hand and pass it over Ilusha’s hair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Never mind!” he murmured softly to him to cheer him up, or perhaps not knowing why he said it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: For a minute they were silent again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Hallo, so you’ve got a new puppy?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya said suddenly, in a most callous voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ye—es,” answered Ilusha in a long whisper, gasping for breath.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A black nose, that means he’ll be fierce, a good house-dog,” Kolya observed gravely and stolidly, as if the only thing he cared about was the puppy and its black nose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But in reality he still had to do his utmost to control his feelings not to burst out crying like a child, and do what he would he could not control it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When it grows up, you’ll have to keep it on the chain, I’m sure.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’ll be a huge dog!” cried one of the boys.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course he will,” “a mastiff,” “large,” “like this,” “as big as a calf,” shouted several voices.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “As big as a calf, as a real calf,” chimed in the captain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I got one like that on purpose, one of the fiercest breed, and his parents are huge and very fierce, they stand as high as this from the floor.... Sit down here, on Ilusha’s bed, or here on the bench. You are welcome, we’ve been hoping to see you a long time.... You were so kind as to come with Alexey Fyodorovitch?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin sat on the edge of the bed, at Ilusha’s feet.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though he had perhaps prepared a free-and-easy opening for the conversation on his way, now he completely lost the thread of it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No ... I came with Perezvon. I’ve got a dog now, called Perezvon. A Slavonic name. He’s out there ... if I whistle, he’ll run in. I’ve brought a dog, too,” he said, addressing Ilusha all at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you remember Zhutchka, old man?” he suddenly fired the question at him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha’s little face quivered.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked with an agonized expression at Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha, standing at the door, frowned and signed to Kolya not to speak of Zhutchka, but he did not or would not notice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Where ... is Zhutchka?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha asked in a broken voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, well, my boy, your Zhutchka’s lost and done for!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha did not speak, but he fixed an intent gaze once more on Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha, catching Kolya’s eye, signed to him vigorously again, but he turned away his eyes pretending not to have noticed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It must have run away and died somewhere. It must have died after a meal like that,” Kolya pronounced pitilessly, though he seemed a little breathless.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I’ve got a dog, Perezvon ... A Slavonic name.... I’ve brought him to show you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t want him!” said Ilusha suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, no, you really must see him ... it will amuse you.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I brought him on purpose....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He’s the same sort of shaggy dog....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You allow me to call in my dog, madam?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He suddenly addressed Madame Snegiryov, with inexplicable excitement in his manner.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t want him, I don’t want him!” cried Ilusha, with a mournful break in his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a reproachful light in his eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’d better,” the captain started up from the chest by the wall on which he had just sat down, “you’d better ... another time,” he muttered, but Kolya could not be restrained.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hurriedly shouted to Smurov, “Open the door,” and as soon as it was open, he blew his whistle.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Perezvon dashed headlong into the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Jump, Perezvon, beg! Beg!” shouted Kolya, jumping up, and the dog stood erect on its hind-legs by Ilusha’s bedside.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What followed was a surprise to every one: Ilusha started, lurched violently forward, bent over Perezvon and gazed at him, faint with suspense.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s ... Zhutchka!” he cried suddenly, in a voice breaking with joy and suffering.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And who did you think it was?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Krassotkin shouted with all his might, in a ringing, happy voice, and bending down he seized the dog and lifted him up to Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Look, old man, you see, blind of one eye and the left ear is torn, just the marks you described to me. It was by that I found him. I found him directly. He did not belong to any one!” he explained, turning quickly to the captain, to his wife, to Alyosha and then again to Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He used to live in the Fedotovs’ back-yard.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Though he made his home there, they did not feed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was a stray dog that had run away from the village ...

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I found him....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You see, old man, he couldn’t have swallowed what you gave him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he had, he must have died, he must have!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So he must have spat it out, since he is alive.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You did not see him do it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the pin pricked his tongue, that is why he squealed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He ran away squealing and you thought he’d swallowed it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He might well squeal, because the skin of dogs’ mouths is so tender ... tenderer than in men, much tenderer!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya cried impetuously, his face glowing and radiant with delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha could not speak.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: White as a sheet, he gazed open-mouthed at Kolya, with his great eyes almost starting out of his head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And if Krassotkin, who had no suspicion of it, had known what a disastrous and fatal effect such a moment might have on the sick child’s health, nothing would have induced him to play such a trick on him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Alyosha was perhaps the only person in the room who realized it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for the captain he behaved like a small child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Zhutchka! It’s Zhutchka!” he cried in a blissful voice, “Ilusha, this is Zhutchka, your Zhutchka!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mamma, this is Zhutchka!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was almost weeping.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I never guessed!” cried Smurov regretfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Bravo, Krassotkin! I said he’d find the dog and here he’s found him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Here he’s found him!” another boy repeated gleefully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Krassotkin’s a brick!” cried a third voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He’s a brick, he’s a brick!” cried the other boys, and they began clapping.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Wait, wait,” Krassotkin did his utmost to shout above them all.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll tell you how it happened, that’s the whole point. I found him, I took him home and hid him at once. I kept him locked up at home and did not show him to any one till to-day. Only Smurov has known for the last fortnight, but I assured him this dog was called Perezvon and he did not guess. And meanwhile I taught the dog all sorts of tricks. You should only see all the things he can do! I trained him so as to bring you a well-trained dog, in good condition, old man, so as to be able to say to you, ‘See, old man, what a fine dog your Zhutchka is now! Haven’t you a bit of meat? He’ll show you a trick that will make you die with laughing. A piece of meat, haven’t you got any?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain ran across the passage to the landlady, where their cooking was done.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Not to lose precious time, Kolya, in desperate haste, shouted to Perezvon, “Dead! And the dog immediately turned round and lay on his back with its four paws in the air. The boys laughed. Ilusha looked on with the same suffering smile, but the person most delighted with the dog’s performance was “mamma. She laughed at the dog and began snapping her fingers and calling it, “Perezvon, Perezvon!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nothing will make him get up, nothing!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya cried triumphantly, proud of his success.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He won’t move for all the shouting in the world, but if I call to him, he’ll jump up in a minute.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ici, Perezvon!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The dog leapt up and bounded about, whining with delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain ran back with a piece of cooked beef.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is it hot? Kolya inquired hurriedly, with a business-like air, taking the meat. “Dogs don’t like hot things. No, it’s all right. Look, everybody, look, Ilusha, look, old man; why aren’t you looking? He does not look at him, now I’ve brought him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The new trick consisted in making the dog stand motionless with his nose out and putting a tempting morsel of meat just on his nose.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The luckless dog had to stand without moving, with the meat on his nose, as long as his master chose to keep him, without a movement, perhaps for half an hour.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he kept Perezvon only for a brief moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Paid for!” cried Kolya, and the meat passed in a flash from the dog’s nose to his mouth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The audience, of course, expressed enthusiasm and surprise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Can you really have put off coming all this time simply to train the dog?” exclaimed Alyosha, with an involuntary note of reproach in his voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Simply for that!” answered Kolya, with perfect simplicity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I wanted to show him in all his glory.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Perezvon! Perezvon,” called Ilusha suddenly, snapping his thin fingers and beckoning to the dog.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What is it?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Let him jump up on the bed!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ici, Perezvon!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya slapped the bed and Perezvon darted up by Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boy threw both arms round his head and Perezvon instantly licked his cheek.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha crept close to him, stretched himself out in bed and hid his face in the dog’s shaggy coat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Dear, dear!” kept exclaiming the captain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya sat down again on the edge of the bed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ilusha, I can show you another trick. I’ve brought you a little cannon. You remember, I told you about it before and you said how much you’d like to see it. Well, here, I’ve brought it to you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And Kolya hurriedly pulled out of his satchel the little bronze cannon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hurried, because he was happy himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Another time he would have waited till the sensation made by Perezvon had passed off, now he hurried on regardless of all consideration.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are all happy now,” he felt, “so here’s something to make you happier!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was perfectly enchanted himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve been coveting this thing for a long while; it’s for you, old man, it’s for you. It belonged to Morozov, it was no use to him, he had it from his brother. I swopped a book from father’s book-case for it, A Kinsman of Mahomet or Salutary Folly, a scandalous book published in Moscow a hundred years ago, before they had any censorship. And Morozov has a taste for such things. He was grateful to me, too....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya held the cannon in his hand so that all could see and admire it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ilusha raised himself, and, with his right arm still round the dog, he gazed enchanted at the toy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sensation was even greater when Kolya announced that he had gunpowder too, and that it could be fired off at once “if it won’t alarm the ladies. “Mamma” immediately asked to look at the toy closer and her request was granted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was much pleased with the little bronze cannon on wheels and began rolling it to and fro on her lap.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She readily gave permission for the cannon to be fired, without any idea of what she had been asked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya showed the powder and the shot.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain, as a military man, undertook to load it, putting in a minute quantity of powder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He asked that the shot might be put off till another time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The cannon was put on the floor, aiming towards an empty part of the room, three grains of powder were thrust into the touch-hole and a match was put to it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A magnificent explosion followed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Mamma was startled, but at once laughed with delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The boys gazed in speechless triumph.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the captain, looking at Ilusha, was more enchanted than any of them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya picked up the cannon and immediately presented it to Ilusha, together with the powder and the shot.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I got it for you, for you! I’ve been keeping it for you a long time,” he repeated once more in his delight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, give it to me! No, give me the cannon!” mamma began begging like a little child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her face showed a piteous fear that she would not get it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya was disconcerted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain fidgeted uneasily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mamma, mamma,” he ran to her, “the cannon’s yours, of course, but let Ilusha have it, because it’s a present to him, but it’s just as good as yours. Ilusha will always let you play with it; it shall belong to both of you, both of you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I don’t want it to belong to both of us, I want it to be mine altogether, not Ilusha’s,” persisted mamma, on the point of tears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Take it, mother, here, keep it! Ilusha cried. “Krassotkin, may I give it to my mother?” he turned to Krassotkin with an imploring face, as though he were afraid he might be offended at his giving his present to some one else.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course you may,” Krassotkin assented heartily, and, taking the cannon from Ilusha, he handed it himself to mamma with a polite bow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was so touched that she cried.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ilusha, darling, he’s the one who loves his mamma!” she said tenderly, and at once began wheeling the cannon to and fro on her lap again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Mamma, let me kiss your hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain darted up to her at once and did so.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I never saw such a charming fellow as this nice boy,” said the grateful lady, pointing to Krassotkin.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And I’ll bring you as much powder as you like, Ilusha. We make the powder ourselves now. Borovikov found out how it’s made—twenty-four parts of saltpeter, ten of sulphur and six of birchwood charcoal. It’s all pounded together, mixed into a paste with water and rubbed through a tammy sieve—that’s how it’s done.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Smurov told me about your powder, only father says it’s not real gunpowder,” responded Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not real? Kolya flushed. “It burns. I don’t know, of course.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I didn’t mean that,” put in the captain with a guilty face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I only said that real powder is not made like that, but that’s nothing, it can be made so.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know, you know best. We lighted some in a pomatum pot, it burned splendidly, it all burnt away leaving only a tiny ash. But that was only the paste, and if you rub it through ... but of course you know best, I don’t know.... And Bulkin’s father thrashed him on account of our powder, did you hear?” he turned to Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes,” answered Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He listened to Kolya with immense interest and enjoyment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “We had prepared a whole bottle of it and he used to keep it under his bed. His father saw it. He said it might explode, and thrashed him on the spot. He was going to make a complaint against me to the masters. He is not allowed to go about with me now, no one is allowed to go about with me now. Smurov is not allowed to either, I’ve got a bad name with every one. They say I’m a ‘desperate character,’”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Kolya smiled scornfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It all began from what happened on the railway.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, we’ve heard of that exploit of yours, too,” cried the captain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How could you lie still on the line? Is it possible you weren’t the least afraid, lying there under the train? Weren’t you frightened?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The captain was abject in his flattery of Kolya.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “N—not particularly,” answered Kolya carelessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “What’s blasted my reputation more than anything here was that cursed goose,” he said, turning again to Ilusha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But though he assumed an unconcerned air as he talked, he still could not control himself and was continually missing the note he tried to keep up.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah! I heard about the goose! Ilusha laughed, beaming all over. “They told me, but I didn’t understand. Did they really take you to the court?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The most stupid, trivial affair, they made a mountain of a molehill as they always do,” Kolya began carelessly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I was walking through the market-place here one day, just when they’d driven in the geese. I stopped and looked at them. All at once a fellow, who is an errand-boy at Plotnikov’s now, looked at me and said, ‘What are you looking at the geese for? I looked at him; he was a stupid, moon-faced fellow of twenty. I am always on the side of the peasantry, you know. I like talking to the peasants.... We’ve dropped behind the peasants—that’s an axiom. I believe you are laughing, Karamazov?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, Heaven forbid, I am listening,” said Alyosha with a most good-natured air, and the sensitive Kolya was immediately reassured.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “My theory, Karamazov, is clear and simple,” he hurried on again, looking pleased.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I believe in the people and am always glad to give them their due, but I am not for spoiling them, that is a sine qua non ... But I was telling you about the goose. So I turned to the fool and answered, ‘I am wondering what the goose thinks about. He looked at me quite stupidly, ‘And what does the goose think about?’ he asked. ‘Do you see that cart full of oats? I said. ‘The oats are dropping out of the sack, and the goose has put its neck right under the wheel to gobble them up—do you see? ‘I see that quite well,’ he said. ‘Well,’ said I, ‘if that cart were to move on a little, would it break the goose’s neck or not? ‘It’d be sure to break it,’ and he grinned all over his face, highly delighted. ‘Come on, then,’ said I, ‘let’s try. ‘Let’s,’ he said. And it did not take us long to arrange: he stood at the bridle without being noticed, and I stood on one side to direct the goose. And the owner wasn’t looking, he was talking to some one, so I had nothing to do, the goose thrust its head in after the oats of itself, under the cart, just under the wheel. I winked at the lad, he tugged at the bridle, and crack. The goose’s neck was broken in half. And, as luck would have it, all the peasants saw us at that moment and they kicked up a shindy at once. ‘You did that on purpose! ‘No, not on purpose. ‘Yes, you did, on purpose! Well, they shouted, ‘Take him to the justice of the peace! They took me, too. ‘You were there, too,’ they said, ‘you helped, you’re known all over the market! And, for some reason, I really am known all over the market,” Kolya added conceitedly. “We all went off to the justice’s, they brought the goose, too. The fellow was crying in a great funk, simply blubbering like a woman. And the farmer kept shouting that you could kill any number of geese like that. Well, of course, there were witnesses. The justice of the peace settled it in a minute, that the farmer was to be paid a rouble for the goose, and the fellow to have the goose. And he was warned not to play such pranks again. And the fellow kept blubbering like a woman. ‘It wasn’t me,’ he said, ‘it was he egged me on,’ and he pointed to me. I answered with the utmost composure that I hadn’t egged him on, that I simply stated the general proposition, had spoken hypothetically.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

She was with me some time ago and I couldn’t get anything out of her. Especially as she won’t talk to me except on the surface now. She is always talking about my health and nothing else, and she takes up such a tone with me, too. I simply said to myself, ‘Well, so be it. I don’t care’... Oh, yes. I was talking of aberration. This doctor has come. You know a doctor has come? Of course, you know it—the one who discovers madmen. You wrote for him. No, it wasn’t you, but Katya. It’s all Katya’s doing. Well, you see, a man may be sitting perfectly sane and suddenly have an aberration. He may be conscious and know what he is doing and yet be in a state of aberration. And there’s no doubt that Dmitri Fyodorovitch was suffering from aberration. They found out about aberration as soon as the law courts were reformed. It’s all the good effect of the reformed law courts. The doctor has been here and questioned me about that evening, about the gold mines. ‘How did he seem then?’ he asked me. He must have been in a state of aberration. He came in shouting, ‘Money, money, three thousand! Give me three thousand!’ and then went away and immediately did the murder. ‘I don’t want to murder him,’ he said, and he suddenly went and murdered him. That’s why they’ll acquit him, because he struggled against it and yet he murdered him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But he didn’t murder him,” Alyosha interrupted rather sharply.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He felt more and more sick with anxiety and impatience.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I know it was that old man Grigory murdered him.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Grigory?” cried Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, yes; it was Grigory. He lay as Dmitri Fyodorovitch struck him down, and then got up, saw the door open, went in and killed Fyodor Pavlovitch.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But why, why?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Suffering from aberration. When he recovered from the blow Dmitri Fyodorovitch gave him on the head, he was suffering from aberration; he went and committed the murder. As for his saying he didn’t, he very likely doesn’t remember. Only, you know, it’ll be better, ever so much better, if Dmitri Fyodorovitch murdered him. And that’s how it must have been, though I say it was Grigory. It certainly was Dmitri Fyodorovitch, and that’s better, ever so much better! Oh! not better that a son should have killed his father, I don’t defend that. Children ought to honor their parents, and yet it would be better if it were he, as you’d have nothing to cry over then, for he did it when he was unconscious or rather when he was conscious, but did not know what he was doing. Let them acquit him—that’s so humane, and would show what a blessing reformed law courts are. I knew nothing about it, but they say they have been so a long time. And when I heard it yesterday, I was so struck by it that I wanted to send for you at once. And if he is acquitted, make him come straight from the law courts to dinner with me, and I’ll have a party of friends, and we’ll drink to the reformed law courts. I don’t believe he’d be dangerous; besides, I’ll invite a great many friends, so that he could always be led out if he did anything. And then he might be made a justice of the peace or something in another town, for those who have been in trouble themselves make the best judges. And, besides, who isn’t suffering from aberration nowadays?—you, I, all of us are in a state of aberration, and there are ever so many examples of it: a man sits singing a song, suddenly something annoys him, he takes a pistol and shoots the first person he comes across, and no one blames him for it. I read that lately, and all the doctors confirm it. The doctors are always confirming; they confirm anything. Why, my Lise is in a state of aberration. She made me cry again yesterday, and the day before, too, and to-day I suddenly realized that it’s all due to aberration. Oh, Lise grieves me so! I believe she’s quite mad. Why did she send for you? Did she send for you or did you come of yourself?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, she sent for me, and I am just going to her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha got up resolutely.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, my dear, dear Alexey Fyodorovitch, perhaps that’s what’s most important,” Madame Hohlakov cried, suddenly bursting into tears.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “God knows I trust Lise to you with all my heart, and it’s no matter her sending for you on the sly, without telling her mother. But forgive me, I can’t trust my daughter so easily to your brother Ivan Fyodorovitch, though I still consider him the most chivalrous young man. But only fancy, he’s been to see Lise and I knew nothing about it!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: When?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha was exceedingly surprised.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He had not sat down again and listened standing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I will tell you; that’s perhaps why I asked you to come, for I don’t know now why I did ask you to come. Well, Ivan Fyodorovitch has been to see me twice, since he came back from Moscow. First time he came as a friend to call on me, and the second time Katya was here and he came because he heard she was here. I didn’t, of course, expect him to come often, knowing what a lot he has to do as it is, vous comprenez, cette affaire et la mort terrible de votre papa. But I suddenly heard he’d been here again, not to see me but to see Lise. That’s six days ago now. He came, stayed five minutes, and went away. And I didn’t hear of it till three days afterwards, from Glafira, so it was a great shock to me. I sent for Lise directly. She laughed. ‘He thought you were asleep,’ she said, ‘and came in to me to ask after your health. Of course, that’s how it happened. But Lise, Lise, mercy on us, how she distresses me! Would you believe it, one night, four days ago, just after you saw her last time, and had gone away, she suddenly had a fit, screaming, shrieking, hysterics! Why is it I never have hysterics? Then, next day another fit, and the same thing on the third, and yesterday too, and then yesterday that aberration. She suddenly screamed out, ‘I hate Ivan Fyodorovitch. I insist on your never letting him come to the house again. I was struck dumb at these amazing words, and answered, ‘On what grounds could I refuse to see such an excellent young man, a young man of such learning too, and so unfortunate?’—for all this business is a misfortune, isn’t it? She suddenly burst out laughing at my words, and so rudely, you know. Well, I was pleased; I thought I had amused her and the fits would pass off, especially as I wanted to refuse to see Ivan Fyodorovitch anyway on account of his strange visits without my knowledge, and meant to ask him for an explanation. But early this morning Lise waked up and flew into a passion with Yulia and, would you believe it, slapped her in the face. That’s monstrous; I am always polite to my servants. And an hour later she was hugging Yulia’s feet and kissing them. She sent a message to me that she wasn’t coming to me at all, and would never come and see me again, and when I dragged myself down to her, she rushed to kiss me, crying, and as she kissed me, she pushed me out of the room without saying a word, so I couldn’t find out what was the matter. Now, dear Alexey Fyodorovitch, I rest all my hopes on you, and, of course, my whole life is in your hands. I simply beg you to go to Lise and find out everything from her, as you alone can, and come back and tell me—me, her mother, for you understand it will be the death of me, simply the death of me, if this goes on, or else I shall run away. I can stand no more. I have patience; but I may lose patience, and then ... then something awful will happen. Ah, dear me! At last, Pyotr Ilyitch!” cried Madame Hohlakov, beaming all over as she saw Perhotin enter the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are late, you are late! Well, sit down, speak, put us out of suspense. What does the counsel say. Where are you off to, Alexey Fyodorovitch?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To Lise.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, yes. You won’t forget, you won’t forget what I asked you? It’s a question of life and death!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Of course, I won’t forget, if I can ... but I am so late,” muttered Alyosha, beating a hasty retreat.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, be sure, be sure to come in; don’t say ‘If you can. I shall die if you don’t,” Madame Hohlakov called after him, but Alyosha had already left the room.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Going in to Lise, he found her half reclining in the invalid-chair, in which she had been wheeled when she was unable to walk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She did not move to meet him, but her sharp, keen eyes were simply riveted on his face.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was a feverish look in her eyes, her face was pale and yellow.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha was amazed at the change that had taken place in her in three days.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was positively thinner.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She did not hold out her hand to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He touched the thin, long fingers which lay motionless on her dress, then he sat down facing her, without a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I know you are in a hurry to get to the prison,” Lise said curtly, “and mamma’s kept you there for hours; she’s just been telling you about me and Yulia.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How do you know?” asked Alyosha.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve been listening. Why do you stare at me? I want to listen and I do listen, there’s no harm in that. I don’t apologize.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are upset about something?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “On the contrary, I am very happy. I’ve only just been reflecting for the thirtieth time what a good thing it is I refused you and shall not be your wife. You are not fit to be a husband. If I were to marry you and give you a note to take to the man I loved after you, you’d take it and be sure to give it to him and bring an answer back, too. If you were forty, you would still go on taking my love-letters for me.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She suddenly laughed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is something spiteful and yet open-hearted about you,” Alyosha smiled to her.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The open-heartedness consists in my not being ashamed of myself with you. What’s more, I don’t want to feel ashamed with you, just with you. Alyosha, why is it I don’t respect you? I am very fond of you, but I don’t respect you. If I respected you, I shouldn’t talk to you without shame, should I?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But do you believe that I am not ashamed with you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I don’t believe it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Lise laughed nervously again; she spoke rapidly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I sent your brother, Dmitri Fyodorovitch, some sweets in prison. Alyosha, you know, you are quite pretty! I shall love you awfully for having so quickly allowed me not to love you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why did you send for me to-day, Lise?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I wanted to tell you of a longing I have. I should like some one to torture me, marry me and then torture me, deceive me and go away. I don’t want to be happy.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are in love with disorder?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I want disorder. I keep wanting to set fire to the house. I keep imagining how I’ll creep up and set fire to the house on the sly; it must be on the sly. They’ll try to put it out, but it’ll go on burning. And I shall know and say nothing. Ah, what silliness! And how bored I am!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She waved her hand with a look of repulsion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s your luxurious life,” said Alyosha, softly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is it better, then, to be poor?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, it is better.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s what your monk taught you. That’s not true. Let me be rich and all the rest poor, I’ll eat sweets and drink cream and not give any to any one else. Ach, don’t speak, don’t say anything,” she shook her hand at him, though Alyosha had not opened his mouth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You’ve told me all that before, I know it all by heart. It bores me. If I am ever poor, I shall murder somebody, and even if I am rich, I may murder some one, perhaps—why do nothing! But do you know, I should like to reap, cut the rye? I’ll marry you, and you shall become a peasant, a real peasant; we’ll keep a colt, shall we? Do you know Kalganov?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He is always wandering about, dreaming. He says, ‘Why live in real life? It’s better to dream. One can dream the most delightful things, but real life is a bore. But he’ll be married soon for all that; he’s been making love to me already. Can you spin tops?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Well, he’s just like a top: he wants to be wound up and set spinning and then to be lashed, lashed, lashed with a whip. If I marry him, I’ll keep him spinning all his life. You are not ashamed to be with me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are awfully cross, because I don’t talk about holy things. I don’t want to be holy. What will they do to one in the next world for the greatest sin? You must know all about that.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “God will censure you.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha was watching her steadily.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s just what I should like. I would go up and they would censure me, and I would burst out laughing in their faces. I should dreadfully like to set fire to the house, Alyosha, to our house; you still don’t believe me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why? There are children of twelve years old, who have a longing to set fire to something and they do set things on fire, too. It’s a sort of disease.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That’s not true, that’s not true; there may be children, but that’s not what I mean.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You take evil for good; it’s a passing crisis, it’s the result of your illness, perhaps.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You do despise me, though! It’s simply that I don’t want to do good, I want to do evil, and it has nothing to do with illness.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Why do evil?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “So that everything might be destroyed. Ah, how nice it would be if everything were destroyed! You know, Alyosha, I sometimes think of doing a fearful lot of harm and everything bad, and I should do it for a long while on the sly and suddenly every one would find it out. Every one will stand round and point their fingers at me and I would look at them all. That would be awfully nice. Why would it be so nice, Alyosha?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know. It’s a craving to destroy something good or, as you say, to set fire to something. It happens sometimes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I not only say it, I shall do it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I believe you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Ah, how I love you for saying you believe me. And you are not lying one little bit. But perhaps you think that I am saying all this on purpose to annoy you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, I don’t think that ... though perhaps there is a little desire to do that in it, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is a little. I never can tell lies to you,” she declared, with a strange fire in her eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What struck Alyosha above everything was her earnestness.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was not a trace of humor or jesting in her face now, though, in old days, fun and gayety never deserted her even at her most “earnest” moments.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There are moments when people love crime,” said Alyosha thoughtfully.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, yes! You have uttered my thought; they love crime, every one loves crime, they love it always, not at some ‘moments. You know, it’s as though people have made an agreement to lie about it and have lied about it ever since. They all declare that they hate evil, but secretly they all love it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And are you still reading nasty books?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I am. Mamma reads them and hides them under her pillow and I steal them.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Aren’t you ashamed to destroy yourself?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I want to destroy myself. There’s a boy here, who lay down between the railway lines when the train was passing. Lucky fellow! Listen, your brother is being tried now for murdering his father and every one loves his having killed his father.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Loves his having killed his father?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, loves it; every one loves it! Everybody says it’s so awful, but secretly they simply love it. I for one love it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There is some truth in what you say about every one,” said Alyosha softly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, what ideas you have! Lise shrieked in delight. “And you a monk, too! You wouldn’t believe how I respect you, Alyosha, for never telling lies. Oh, I must tell you a funny dream of mine. I sometimes dream of devils. It’s night; I am in my room with a candle and suddenly there are devils all over the place, in all the corners, under the table, and they open the doors; there’s a crowd of them behind the doors and they want to come and seize me. And they are just coming, just seizing me. But I suddenly cross myself and they all draw back, though they don’t go away altogether, they stand at the doors and in the corners, waiting. And suddenly I have a frightful longing to revile God aloud, and so I begin, and then they come crowding back to me, delighted, and seize me again and I cross myself again and they all draw back. It’s awful fun. it takes one’s breath away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ve had the same dream, too,” said Alyosha suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Really?” cried Lise, surprised.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I say, Alyosha, don’t laugh, that’s awfully important. Could two different people have the same dream?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It seems they can.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, I tell you, it’s awfully important,” Lise went on, with really excessive amazement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s not the dream that’s important, but your having the same dream as me. You never lie to me, don’t lie now: is it true? You are not laughing?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s true.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Lise seemed extraordinarily impressed and for half a minute she was silent.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Alyosha, come and see me, come and see me more often,” she said suddenly, in a supplicating voice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I’ll always come to see you, all my life,” answered Alyosha firmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You are the only person I can talk to, you know,” Lise began again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I talk to no one but myself and you. Only you in the whole world. And to you more readily than to myself. And I am not a bit ashamed with you, not a bit. Alyosha, why am I not ashamed with you, not a bit? Alyosha, is it true that at Easter the Jews steal a child and kill it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I don’t know.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “There’s a book here in which I read about the trial of a Jew, who took a child of four years old and cut off the fingers from both hands, and then crucified him on the wall, hammered nails into him and crucified him, and afterwards, when he was tried, he said that the child died soon, within four hours. That was ‘soon’! He said the child moaned, kept on moaning and he stood admiring it. That’s nice!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nice?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Nice; I sometimes imagine that it was I who crucified him. He would hang there moaning and I would sit opposite him eating pineapple compote. I am awfully fond of pineapple compote. Do you like it?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha looked at her in silence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her pale, sallow face was suddenly contorted, her eyes burned.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You know, when I read about that Jew I shook with sobs all night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I kept fancying how the little thing cried and moaned (a child of four years old understands, you know), and all the while the thought of pineapple compote haunted me.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the morning I wrote a letter to a certain person, begging him particularly to come and see me.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He came and I suddenly told him all about the child and the pineapple compote.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All about it, all, and said that it was nice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He laughed and said it really was nice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then he got up and went away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was only here five minutes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did he despise me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did he despise me?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Tell me, tell me, Alyosha, did he despise me or not?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She sat up on the couch, with flashing eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Tell me,” Alyosha asked anxiously, “did you send for that person?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I did.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Did you send him a letter?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Simply to ask about that, about that child?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, not about that at all. But when he came, I asked him about that at once. He answered, laughed, got up and went away.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “That person behaved honorably,” Alyosha murmured.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And did he despise me? Did he laugh at me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “No, for perhaps he believes in the pineapple compote himself. He is very ill now, too, Lise.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, he does believe in it,” said Lise, with flashing eyes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “He doesn’t despise any one,” Alyosha went on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Only he does not believe any one. If he doesn’t believe in people, of course, he does despise them.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Then he despises me, me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You, too.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Good,” Lise seemed to grind her teeth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “When he went out laughing, I felt that it was nice to be despised. The child with fingers cut off is nice, and to be despised is nice....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she laughed in Alyosha’s face, a feverish malicious laugh.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you know, Alyosha, do you know, I should like—Alyosha, save me! She suddenly jumped from the couch, rushed to him and seized him with both hands. “Save me!” she almost groaned.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Is there any one in the world I could tell what I’ve told you? I’ve told you the truth, the truth. I shall kill myself, because I loathe everything! I don’t want to live, because I loathe everything! I loathe everything, everything. Alyosha, why don’t you love me in the least?” she finished in a frenzy.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I do love you!” answered Alyosha warmly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And will you weep over me, will you?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not because I won’t be your wife, but simply weep for me?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Thank you! It’s only your tears I want. Every one else may punish me and trample me under foot, every one, every one, not excepting any one. For I don’t love any one. Do you hear, not any one! On the contrary, I hate him! Go, Alyosha; it’s time you went to your brother”; she tore herself away from him suddenly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “How can I leave you like this?” said Alyosha, almost in alarm.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Go to your brother, the prison will be shut; go, here’s your hat. Give my love to Mitya, go, go!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she almost forcibly pushed Alyosha out of the door.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked at her with pained surprise, when he was suddenly aware of a letter in his right hand, a tiny letter folded up tight and sealed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He glanced at it and instantly read the address, “To Ivan Fyodorovitch Karamazov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He looked quickly at Lise.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her face had become almost menacing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Give it to him, you must give it to him!” she ordered him, trembling and beside herself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “To-day, at once, or I’ll poison myself! That’s why I sent for you.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And she slammed the door quickly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The bolt clicked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Alyosha put the note in his pocket and went straight downstairs, without going back to Madame Hohlakov; forgetting her, in fact.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as Alyosha had gone, Lise unbolted the door, opened it a little, put her finger in the crack and slammed the door with all her might, pinching her finger.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Ten seconds after, releasing her finger, she walked softly, slowly to her chair, sat up straight in it and looked intently at her blackened finger and at the blood that oozed from under the nail.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Her lips were quivering and she kept whispering rapidly to herself:

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I am a wretch, wretch, wretch, wretch!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was quite late (days are short in November) when Alyosha rang at the prison gate.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was beginning to get dusk.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But Alyosha knew that he would be admitted without difficulty.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Things were managed in our little town, as everywhere else.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At first, of course, on the conclusion of the preliminary inquiry, relations and a few other persons could only obtain interviews with Mitya by going through certain inevitable formalities.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But later, though the formalities were not relaxed, exceptions were made for some, at least, of Mitya’s visitors.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So much so, that sometimes the interviews with the prisoner in the room set aside for the purpose were practically tête-à-tête.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “In regard to my epilepsy, sir, you had much better inquire of the doctors here. You can ask them whether it was a real fit or a sham; it’s no use my saying any more about it.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “And the cellar? How could you know beforehand of the cellar?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “You don’t seem able to get over that cellar! As I was going down to the cellar, I was in terrible dread and doubt. What frightened me most was losing you and being left without defense in all the world. So I went down into the cellar thinking, ‘Here, it’ll come on directly, it’ll strike me down directly, shall I fall? And it was through this fear that I suddenly felt the spasm that always comes ... and so I went flying. All that and all my previous conversation with you at the gate the evening before, when I told you how frightened I was and spoke of the cellar, I told all that to Doctor Herzenstube and Nikolay Parfenovitch, the investigating lawyer, and it’s all been written down in the protocol. And the doctor here, Mr. Varvinsky, maintained to all of them that it was just the thought of it brought it on, the apprehension that I might fall. It was just then that the fit seized me. And so they’ve written it down, that it’s just how it must have happened, simply from my fear.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As he finished, Smerdyakov drew a deep breath, as though exhausted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov

And if anything had happened, you might have come to protect me, too, for I warned you of Grigory Vassilyevitch’s illness, and that I was afraid of having a fit. And when I explained those knocks to you, by means of which one could go in to the deceased, and that Dmitri Fyodorovitch knew them all through me, I thought that you would guess yourself that he would be sure to do something, and so wouldn’t go to Tchermashnya even, but would stay.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
