title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I was somewhat surprised just now to hear the highly talented prosecutor declare of himself—of himself, observe—that but for that envelope, but for its being left on the floor, no one in the world would have known of the existence of that envelope and the notes in it, and therefore of the prisoner’s having stolen it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so that torn scrap of paper is, by the prosecutor’s own admission, the sole proof on which the charge of robbery rests, ‘otherwise no one would have known of the robbery, nor perhaps even of the money. But is the mere fact that that scrap of paper was lying on the floor a proof that there was money in it, and that that money had been stolen? Yet, it will be objected, Smerdyakov had seen the money in the envelope. But when, when had he seen it for the last time, I ask you that? I talked to Smerdyakov, and he told me that he had seen the notes two days before the catastrophe. Then why not imagine that old Fyodor Pavlovitch, locked up alone in impatient and hysterical expectation of the object of his adoration, may have whiled away the time by breaking open the envelope and taking out the notes. ‘What’s the use of the envelope?’ he may have asked himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘She won’t believe the notes are there, but when I show her the thirty rainbow-colored notes in one roll, it will make more impression, you may be sure, it will make her mouth water.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And so he tears open the envelope, takes out the money, and flings the envelope on the floor, conscious of being the owner and untroubled by any fears of leaving evidence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Listen, gentlemen, could anything be more likely than this theory and such an action?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why is it out of the question?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But if anything of the sort could have taken place, the charge of robbery falls to the ground; if there was no money, there was no theft of it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If the envelope on the floor may be taken as evidence that there had been money in it, why may I not maintain the opposite, that the envelope was on the floor because the money had been taken from it by its owner?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I shall be asked what became of the money if Fyodor Pavlovitch took it out of the envelope since it was not found when the police searched the house?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the first place, part of the money was found in the cash-box, and secondly, he might have taken it out that morning or the evening before to make some other use of it, to give or send it away; he may have changed his idea, his plan of action completely, without thinking it necessary to announce the fact to Smerdyakov beforehand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And if there is the barest possibility of such an explanation, how can the prisoner be so positively accused of having committed murder for the sake of robbery, and of having actually carried out that robbery?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This is encroaching on the domain of romance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If it is maintained that something has been stolen, the thing must be produced, or at least its existence must be proved beyond doubt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yet no one had ever seen these notes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not long ago in Petersburg a young man of eighteen, hardly more than a boy, who carried on a small business as a costermonger, went in broad daylight into a moneychanger’s shop with an ax, and with extraordinary, typical audacity killed the master of the shop and carried off fifteen hundred roubles.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Five hours later he was arrested, and, except fifteen roubles he had already managed to spend, the whole sum was found on him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Moreover, the shopman, on his return to the shop after the murder, informed the police not only of the exact sum stolen, but even of the notes and gold coins of which that sum was made up, and those very notes and coins were found on the criminal.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: This was followed by a full and genuine confession on the part of the murderer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That’s what I call evidence, gentlemen of the jury!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In that case I know, I see, I touch the money, and cannot deny its existence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is it the same in the present case?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And yet it is a question of life and death.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, I shall be told, but he was carousing that night, squandering money; he was shown to have had fifteen hundred roubles—where did he get the money?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the very fact that only fifteen hundred could be found, and the other half of the sum could nowhere be discovered, shows that that money was not the same, and had never been in any envelope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: By strict calculation of time it was proved at the preliminary inquiry that the prisoner ran straight from those women servants to Perhotin’s without going home, and that he had been nowhere.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So he had been all the time in company and therefore could not have divided the three thousand in half and hidden half in the town.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It’s just this consideration that has led the prosecutor to assume that the money is hidden in some crevice at Mokroe.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why not in the dungeons of the castle of Udolpho, gentlemen?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Isn’t this supposition really too fantastic and too romantic?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And observe, if that supposition breaks down, the whole charge of robbery is scattered to the winds, for in that case what could have become of the other fifteen hundred roubles?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: By what miracle could they have disappeared, since it’s proved the prisoner went nowhere else?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And we are ready to ruin a man’s life with such tales!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall be told that he could not explain where he got the fifteen hundred that he had, and every one knew that he was without money before that night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Who knew it, pray?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prisoner has made a clear and unflinching statement of the source of that money, and if you will have it so, gentlemen of the jury, nothing can be more probable than that statement, and more consistent with the temper and spirit of the prisoner.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor is charmed with his own romance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A man of weak will, who had brought himself to take the three thousand so insultingly offered by his betrothed, could not, we are told, have set aside half and sewn it up, but would, even if he had done so, have unpicked it every two days and taken out a hundred, and so would have spent it all in a month.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: All this, you will remember, was put forward in a tone that brooked no contradiction.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But what if the thing happened quite differently?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What if you’ve been weaving a romance, and about quite a different kind of man?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That’s just it, you have invented quite a different man!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall be told, perhaps, there are witnesses that he spent on one day all that three thousand given him by his betrothed a month before the catastrophe, so he could not have divided the sum in half.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But who are these witnesses?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The value of their evidence has been shown in court already.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Besides, in another man’s hand a crust always seems larger, and no one of these witnesses counted that money; they all judged simply at sight.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the witness Maximov has testified that the prisoner had twenty thousand in his hand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You see, gentlemen of the jury, psychology is a two-edged weapon.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Let me turn the other edge now and see what comes of it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “A month before the catastrophe the prisoner was entrusted by Katerina Ivanovna with three thousand roubles to send off by post.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the question is: is it true that they were entrusted to him in such an insulting and degrading way as was proclaimed just now?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The first statement made by the young lady on the subject was different, perfectly different.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the second statement we heard only cries of resentment and revenge, cries of long-concealed hatred.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the very fact that the witness gave her first evidence incorrectly, gives us a right to conclude that her second piece of evidence may have been incorrect also.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor will not, dare not (his own words) touch on that story.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So be it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I will not touch on it either, but will only venture to observe that if a lofty and high-principled person, such as that highly respected young lady unquestionably is, if such a person, I say, allows herself suddenly in court to contradict her first statement, with the obvious motive of ruining the prisoner, it is clear that this evidence has been given not impartially, not coolly.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Have not we the right to assume that a revengeful woman might have exaggerated much?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yes, she may well have exaggerated, in particular, the insult and humiliation of her offering him the money.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, it was offered in such a way that it was possible to take it, especially for a man so easy-going as the prisoner, above all, as he expected to receive shortly from his father the three thousand roubles that he reckoned was owing to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was unreflecting of him, but it was just his irresponsible want of reflection that made him so confident that his father would give him the money, that he would get it, and so could always dispatch the money entrusted to him and repay the debt.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But the prosecutor refuses to allow that he could the same day have set aside half the money and sewn it up in a little bag.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That’s not his character, he tells us, he couldn’t have had such feelings.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But yet he talked himself of the broad Karamazov nature; he cried out about the two extremes which a Karamazov can contemplate at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Karamazov is just such a two-sided nature, fluctuating between two extremes, that even when moved by the most violent craving for riotous gayety, he can pull himself up, if something strikes him on the other side.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And on the other side is love—that new love which had flamed up in his heart, and for that love he needed money; oh, far more than for carousing with his mistress.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If she were to say to him, ‘I am yours, I won’t have Fyodor Pavlovitch,’ then he must have money to take her away.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That was more important than carousing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Could a Karamazov fail to understand it?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That anxiety was just what he was suffering from—what is there improbable in his laying aside that money and concealing it in case of emergency?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But time passed, and Fyodor Pavlovitch did not give the prisoner the expected three thousand; on the contrary, the latter heard that he meant to use this sum to seduce the woman he, the prisoner, loved.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘If Fyodor Pavlovitch doesn’t give the money,’ he thought, ‘I shall be put in the position of a thief before Katerina Ivanovna. And then the idea presented itself to him that he would go to Katerina Ivanovna, lay before her the fifteen hundred roubles he still carried round his neck, and say, ‘I am a scoundrel, but not a thief. So here we have already a twofold reason why he should guard that sum of money as the apple of his eye, why he shouldn’t unpick the little bag, and spend it a hundred at a time. Why should you deny the prisoner a sense of honor? Yes, he has a sense of honor, granted that it’s misplaced, granted it’s often mistaken, yet it exists and amounts to a passion, and he has proved that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But now the affair becomes even more complex; his jealous torments reach a climax, and those same two questions torture his fevered brain more and more: ‘If I repay Katerina Ivanovna, where can I find the means to go off with Grushenka?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he behaved wildly, drank, and made disturbances in the taverns in the course of that month, it was perhaps because he was wretched and strained beyond his powers of endurance.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: These two questions became so acute that they drove him at last to despair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He sent his younger brother to beg for the last time for the three thousand roubles, but without waiting for a reply, burst in himself and ended by beating the old man in the presence of witnesses.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: After that he had no prospect of getting it from any one; his father would not give it him after that beating.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The same evening he struck himself on the breast, just on the upper part of the breast where the little bag was, and swore to his brother that he had the means of not being a scoundrel, but that still he would remain a scoundrel, for he foresaw that he would not use that means, that he wouldn’t have the character, that he wouldn’t have the will-power to do it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why, why does the prosecutor refuse to believe the evidence of Alexey Karamazov, given so genuinely and sincerely, so spontaneously and convincingly?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And why, on the contrary, does he force me to believe in money hidden in a crevice, in the dungeons of the castle of Udolpho?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The same evening, after his talk with his brother, the prisoner wrote that fatal letter, and that letter is the chief, the most stupendous proof of the prisoner having committed robbery!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘I shall beg from every one, and if I don’t get it I shall murder my father and shall take the envelope with the pink ribbon on it from under his mattress as soon as Ivan has gone. A full program of the murder, we are told, so it must have been he. ‘It has all been done as he wrote,’ cries the prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But in the first place, it’s the letter of a drunken man and written in great irritation; secondly, he writes of the envelope from what he has heard from Smerdyakov again, for he has not seen the envelope himself; and thirdly, he wrote it indeed, but how can you prove that he did it? Did the prisoner take the envelope from under the pillow, did he find the money, did that money exist indeed? And was it to get money that the prisoner ran off, if you remember? He ran off post-haste not to steal, but to find out where she was, the woman who had crushed him. He was not running to carry out a program, to carry out what he had written, that is, not for an act of premeditated robbery, but he ran suddenly, spontaneously, in a jealous fury. Yes! I shall be told, but when he got there and murdered him he seized the money, too. But did he murder him after all? The charge of robbery I repudiate with indignation. A man cannot be accused of robbery, if it’s impossible to state accurately what he has stolen; that’s an axiom. But did he murder him without robbery, did he murder him at all? Is that proved? Isn’t that, too, a romance?”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Allow me, gentlemen of the jury, to remind you that a man’s life is at stake and that you must be careful.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: We have heard the prosecutor himself admit that until to-day he hesitated to accuse the prisoner of a full and conscious premeditation of the crime; he hesitated till he saw that fatal drunken letter which was produced in court to-day.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘All was done as written. But, I repeat again, he was running to her, to seek her, solely to find out where she was. That’s a fact that can’t be disputed. Had she been at home, he would not have run away, but would have remained at her side, and so would not have done what he promised in the letter. He ran unexpectedly and accidentally, and by that time very likely he did not even remember his drunken letter. ‘He snatched up the pestle,’ they say, and you will remember how a whole edifice of psychology was built on that pestle—why he was bound to look at that pestle as a weapon, to snatch it up, and so on, and so on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A very commonplace idea occurs to me at this point: What if that pestle had not been in sight, had not been lying on the shelf from which it was snatched by the prisoner, but had been put away in a cupboard?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It would not have caught the prisoner’s eye, and he would have run away without a weapon, with empty hands, and then he would certainly not have killed any one.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: How then can I look upon the pestle as a proof of premeditation?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, but he talked in the taverns of murdering his father, and two days before, on the evening when he wrote his drunken letter, he was quiet and only quarreled with a shopman in the tavern, because a Karamazov could not help quarreling, forsooth!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But my answer to that is, that, if he was planning such a murder in accordance with his letter, he certainly would not have quarreled even with a shopman, and probably would not have gone into the tavern at all, because a person plotting such a crime seeks quiet and retirement, seeks to efface himself, to avoid being seen and heard, and that not from calculation, but from instinct.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentlemen of the jury, the psychological method is a two-edged weapon, and we, too, can use it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As for all this shouting in taverns throughout the month, don’t we often hear children, or drunkards coming out of taverns shout, ‘I’ll kill you’?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: but they don’t murder any one.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And that fatal letter—isn’t that simply drunken irritability, too?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Isn’t that simply the shout of the brawler outside the tavern, ‘I’ll kill you! I’ll kill the lot of you! Why not, why could it not be that? What reason have we to call that letter ‘fatal’ rather than absurd?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Because his father has been found murdered, because a witness saw the prisoner running out of the garden with a weapon in his hand, and was knocked down by him: therefore, we are told, everything was done as he had planned in writing, and the letter was not ‘absurd,’ but ‘fatal.’

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Now, thank God! we’ve come to the real point: ‘since he was in the garden, he must have murdered him. In those few words: ‘since he was, then he must’ lies the whole case for the prosecution.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was there, so he must have.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And what if there is no must about it, even if he was there?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, I admit that the chain of evidence—the coincidences—are really suggestive.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But examine all these facts separately, regardless of their connection.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why, for instance, does the prosecution refuse to admit the truth of the prisoner’s statement that he ran away from his father’s window?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Remember the sarcasms in which the prosecutor indulged at the expense of the respectful and ‘pious’ sentiments which suddenly came over the murderer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But what if there were something of the sort, a feeling of religious awe, if not of filial respect?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘My mother must have been praying for me at that moment,’ were the prisoner’s words at the preliminary inquiry, and so he ran away as soon as he convinced himself that Madame Svyetlov was not in his father’s house.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘But he could not convince himself by looking through the window,’ the prosecutor objects.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But why couldn’t he?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The window opened at the signals given by the prisoner.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Some word might have been uttered by Fyodor Pavlovitch, some exclamation which showed the prisoner that she was not there.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why should we assume everything as we imagine it, as we make up our minds to imagine it?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A thousand things may happen in reality which elude the subtlest imagination.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “‘Yes, but Grigory saw the door open and so the prisoner certainly was in the house, therefore he killed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Now about that door, gentlemen of the jury....

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Observe that we have only the statement of one witness as to that door, and he was at the time in such a condition, that— But supposing the door was open; supposing the prisoner has lied in denying it, from an instinct of self-defense, natural in his position; supposing he did go into the house—well, what then?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: How does it follow that because he was there he committed the murder?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He might have dashed in, run through the rooms; might have pushed his father away; might have struck him; but as soon as he had made sure Madame Svyetlov was not there, he may have run away rejoicing that she was not there and that he had not killed his father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And it was perhaps just because he had escaped from the temptation to kill his father, because he had a clear conscience and was rejoicing at not having killed him, that he was capable of a pure feeling, the feeling of pity and compassion, and leapt off the fence a minute later to the assistance of Grigory after he had, in his excitement, knocked him down.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “With terrible eloquence the prosecutor has described to us the dreadful state of the prisoner’s mind at Mokroe when love again lay before him calling him to new life, while love was impossible for him because he had his father’s bloodstained corpse behind him and beyond that corpse—retribution.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And yet the prosecutor allowed him love, which he explained, according to his method, talking about his drunken condition, about a criminal being taken to execution, about it being still far off, and so on and so on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But again I ask, Mr. Prosecutor, have you not invented a new personality?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is the prisoner so coarse and heartless as to be able to think at that moment of love and of dodges to escape punishment, if his hands were really stained with his father’s blood?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, no, no!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As soon as it was made plain to him that she loved him and called him to her side, promising him new happiness, oh! then, I protest he must have felt the impulse to suicide doubled, trebled, and must have killed himself, if he had his father’s murder on his conscience.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, no! he would not have forgotten where his pistols lay!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I know the prisoner: the savage, stony heartlessness ascribed to him by the prosecutor is inconsistent with his character.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He would have killed himself, that’s certain.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He did not kill himself just because ‘his mother’s prayers had saved him,’ and he was innocent of his father’s blood.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was troubled, he was grieving that night at Mokroe only about old Grigory and praying to God that the old man would recover, that his blow had not been fatal, and that he would not have to suffer for it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why not accept such an interpretation of the facts?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What trustworthy proof have we that the prisoner is lying?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But we shall be told at once again, ‘There is his father’s corpse! If he ran away without murdering him, who did murder him? Here, I repeat, you have the whole logic of the prosecution. Who murdered him, if not he? There’s no one to put in his place.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury, is that really so?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Is it positively, actually true that there is no one else at all?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: We’ve heard the prosecutor count on his fingers all the persons who were in that house that night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They were five in number; three of them, I agree, could not have been responsible—the murdered man himself, old Grigory, and his wife.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There are left then the prisoner and Smerdyakov, and the prosecutor dramatically exclaims that the prisoner pointed to Smerdyakov because he had no one else to fix on, that had there been a sixth person, even a phantom of a sixth person, he would have abandoned the charge against Smerdyakov at once in shame and have accused that other.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, gentlemen of the jury, why may I not draw the very opposite conclusion?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There are two persons—the prisoner and Smerdyakov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why can I not say that you accuse my client, simply because you have no one else to accuse?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And you have no one else only because you have determined to exclude Smerdyakov from all suspicion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s true, indeed, Smerdyakov is accused only by the prisoner, his two brothers, and Madame Svyetlov.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But there are others who accuse him: there are vague rumors of a question, of a suspicion, an obscure report, a feeling of expectation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Finally, we have the evidence of a combination of facts very suggestive, though, I admit, inconclusive.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the first place we have precisely on the day of the catastrophe that fit, for the genuineness of which the prosecutor, for some reason, has felt obliged to make a careful defense.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then Smerdyakov’s sudden suicide on the eve of the trial.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Then the equally startling evidence given in court to-day by the elder of the prisoner’s brothers, who had believed in his guilt, but has to-day produced a bundle of notes and proclaimed Smerdyakov as the murderer.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, I fully share the court’s and the prosecutor’s conviction that Ivan Karamazov is suffering from brain fever, that his statement may really be a desperate effort, planned in delirium, to save his brother by throwing the guilt on the dead man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But again Smerdyakov’s name is pronounced, again there is a suggestion of mystery.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There is something unexplained, incomplete.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And perhaps it may one day be explained.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But we won’t go into that now.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Of that later.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The court has resolved to go on with the trial, but, meantime, I might make a few remarks about the character-sketch of Smerdyakov drawn with subtlety and talent by the prosecutor.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But while I admire his talent I cannot agree with him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I have visited Smerdyakov, I have seen him and talked to him, and he made a very different impression on me.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was weak in health, it is true; but in character, in spirit, he was by no means the weak man the prosecutor has made him out to be.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I found in him no trace of the timidity on which the prosecutor so insisted.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was no simplicity about him, either.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I found in him, on the contrary, an extreme mistrustfulness concealed under a mask of naïveté, and an intelligence of considerable range.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The prosecutor was too simple in taking him for weak-minded.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He made a very definite impression on me: I left him with the conviction that he was a distinctly spiteful creature, excessively ambitious, vindictive, and intensely envious.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I made some inquiries: he resented his parentage, was ashamed of it, and would clench his teeth when he remembered that he was the son of ‘stinking Lizaveta. He was disrespectful to the servant Grigory and his wife, who had cared for him in his childhood. He cursed and jeered at Russia. He dreamed of going to France and becoming a Frenchman. He used often to say that he hadn’t the means to do so. I fancy he loved no one but himself and had a strangely high opinion of himself. His conception of culture was limited to good clothes, clean shirt-fronts and polished boots. Believing himself to be the illegitimate son of Fyodor Pavlovitch (there is evidence of this), he might well have resented his position, compared with that of his master’s legitimate sons.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They had everything, he nothing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They had all the rights, they had the inheritance, while he was only the cook.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He told me himself that he had helped Fyodor Pavlovitch to put the notes in the envelope.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The destination of that sum—a sum which would have made his career—must have been hateful to him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Moreover, he saw three thousand roubles in new rainbow-colored notes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: (I asked him about that on purpose.)

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, beware of showing an ambitious and envious man a large sum of money at once!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And it was the first time he had seen so much money in the hands of one man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sight of the rainbow-colored notes may have made a morbid impression on his imagination, but with no immediate results.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The talented prosecutor, with extraordinary subtlety, sketched for us all the arguments for and against the hypothesis of Smerdyakov’s guilt, and asked us in particular what motive he had in feigning a fit.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But he may not have been feigning at all, the fit may have happened quite naturally, but it may have passed off quite naturally, and the sick man may have recovered, not completely perhaps, but still regaining consciousness, as happens with epileptics.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The prosecutor asks at what moment could Smerdyakov have committed the murder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But it is very easy to point out that moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He might have waked up from deep sleep (for he was only asleep—an epileptic fit is always followed by a deep sleep) at that moment when the old Grigory shouted at the top of his voice ‘Parricide!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That shout in the dark and stillness may have waked Smerdyakov whose sleep may have been less sound at the moment: he might naturally have waked up an hour before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Getting out of bed, he goes almost unconsciously and with no definite motive towards the sound to see what’s the matter.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His head is still clouded with his attack, his faculties are half asleep; but, once in the garden, he walks to the lighted windows and he hears terrible news from his master, who would be, of course, glad to see him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: His mind sets to work at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He hears all the details from his frightened master, and gradually in his disordered brain there shapes itself an idea—terrible, but seductive and irresistibly logical.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To kill the old man, take the three thousand, and throw all the blame on to his young master.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A terrible lust of money, of booty, might seize upon him as he realized his security from detection.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh! these sudden and irresistible impulses come so often when there is a favorable opportunity, and especially with murderers who have had no idea of committing a murder beforehand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And Smerdyakov may have gone in and carried out his plan.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: With what weapon?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why, with any stone picked up in the garden.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But what for, with what object?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why, the three thousand which means a career for him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, I am not contradicting myself—the money may have existed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And perhaps Smerdyakov alone knew where to find it, where his master kept it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And the covering of the money—the torn envelope on the floor?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Just now, when the prosecutor was explaining his subtle theory that only an inexperienced thief like Karamazov would have left the envelope on the floor, and not one like Smerdyakov, who would have avoided leaving a piece of evidence against himself, I thought as I listened that I was hearing something very familiar, and, would you believe it, I have heard that very argument, that very conjecture, of how Karamazov would have behaved, precisely two days before, from Smerdyakov himself.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What’s more, it struck me at the time.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I fancied that there was an artificial simplicity about him; that he was in a hurry to suggest this idea to me that I might fancy it was my own.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He insinuated it, as it were.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did he not insinuate the same idea at the inquiry and suggest it to the talented prosecutor?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I shall be asked, ‘What about the old woman, Grigory’s wife? She heard the sick man moaning close by, all night. Yes, she heard it, but that evidence is extremely unreliable. I knew a lady who complained bitterly that she had been kept awake all night by a dog in the yard. Yet the poor beast, it appeared, had only yelped once or twice in the night. And that’s natural.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If any one is asleep and hears a groan he wakes up, annoyed at being waked, but instantly falls asleep again.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Two hours later, again a groan, he wakes up and falls asleep again; and the same thing again two hours later—three times altogether in the night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Next morning the sleeper wakes up and complains that some one has been groaning all night and keeping him awake.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And it is bound to seem so to him: the intervals of two hours of sleep he does not remember, he only remembers the moments of waking, so he feels he has been waked up all night.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But why, why, asks the prosecutor, did not Smerdyakov confess in his last letter?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Why did his conscience prompt him to one step and not to both?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But, excuse me, conscience implies penitence, and the suicide may not have felt penitence, but only despair.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Despair and penitence are two very different things.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Despair may be vindictive and irreconcilable, and the suicide, laying his hands on himself, may well have felt redoubled hatred for those whom he had envied all his life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury, beware of a miscarriage of justice!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What is there unlikely in all I have put before you just now?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Find the error in my reasoning; find the impossibility, the absurdity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And if there is but a shade of possibility, but a shade of probability in my propositions, do not condemn him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And is there only a shade?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I swear by all that is sacred, I fully believe in the explanation of the murder I have just put forward.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What troubles me and makes me indignant is that of all the mass of facts heaped up by the prosecution against the prisoner, there is not a single one certain and irrefutable.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And yet the unhappy man is to be ruined by the accumulation of these facts.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yes, the accumulated effect is awful: the blood, the blood dripping from his fingers, the bloodstained shirt, the dark night resounding with the shout ‘Parricide!’ and the old man falling with a broken head.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And then the mass of phrases, statements, gestures, shouts!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh! this has so much influence, it can so bias the mind; but, gentlemen of the jury, can it bias your minds?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Remember, you have been given absolute power to bind and to loose, but the greater the power, the more terrible its responsibility.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I do not draw back one iota from what I have said just now, but suppose for one moment I agreed with the prosecution that my luckless client had stained his hands with his father’s blood. This is only hypothesis, I repeat; I never for one instant doubt of his innocence. But, so be it, I assume that my client is guilty of parricide. Even so, hear what I have to say. I have it in my heart to say something more to you, for I feel that there must be a great conflict in your hearts and minds.... Forgive my referring to your hearts and minds, gentlemen of the jury, but I want to be truthful and sincere to the end. Let us all be sincere!”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At this point the speech was interrupted by rather loud applause.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The last words, indeed, were pronounced with a note of such sincerity that every one felt that he really might have something to say, and that what he was about to say would be of the greatest consequence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But the President, hearing the applause, in a loud voice threatened to clear the court if such an incident were repeated.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Every sound was hushed and Fetyukovitch began in a voice full of feeling quite unlike the tone he had used hitherto.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “It’s not only the accumulation of facts that threatens my client with ruin, gentlemen of the jury,” he began, “what is really damning for my client is one fact—the dead body of his father.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Had it been an ordinary case of murder you would have rejected the charge in view of the triviality, the incompleteness, and the fantastic character of the evidence, if you examine each part of it separately; or, at least, you would have hesitated to ruin a man’s life simply from the prejudice against him which he has, alas! only too well deserved.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But it’s not an ordinary case of murder, it’s a case of parricide.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That impresses men’s minds, and to such a degree that the very triviality and incompleteness of the evidence becomes less trivial and less incomplete even to an unprejudiced mind.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: How can such a prisoner be acquitted?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What if he committed the murder and gets off unpunished?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That is what every one, almost involuntarily, instinctively, feels at heart.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Yes, it’s a fearful thing to shed a father’s blood—the father who has begotten me, loved me, not spared his life for me, grieved over my illnesses from childhood up, troubled all his life for my happiness, and has lived in my joys, in my successes.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: To murder such a father—that’s inconceivable.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentlemen of the jury, what is a father—a real father?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What is the meaning of that great word?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What is the great idea in that name?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: We have just indicated in part what a true father is and what he ought to be.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the case in which we are now so deeply occupied and over which our hearts are aching—in the present case, the father, Fyodor Pavlovitch Karamazov, did not correspond to that conception of a father to which we have just referred.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That’s the misfortune.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And indeed some fathers are a misfortune.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Let us examine this misfortune rather more closely: we must shrink from nothing, gentlemen of the jury, considering the importance of the decision you have to make.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It’s our particular duty not to shrink from any idea, like children or frightened women, as the talented prosecutor happily expresses it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But in the course of his heated speech my esteemed opponent (and he was my opponent before I opened my lips) exclaimed several times, ‘Oh, I will not yield the defense of the prisoner to the lawyer who has come down from Petersburg. I accuse, but I defend also! He exclaimed that several times, but forgot to mention that if this terrible prisoner was for twenty-three years so grateful for a mere pound of nuts given him by the only man who had been kind to him, as a child in his father’s house, might not such a man well have remembered for twenty-three years how he ran in his father’s back-yard, ‘without boots on his feet and with his little trousers hanging by one button’—to use the expression of the kind-hearted doctor, Herzenstube?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, gentlemen of the jury, why need we look more closely at this misfortune, why repeat what we all know already?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What did my client meet with when he arrived here, at his father’s house, and why depict my client as a heartless egoist and monster?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He is uncontrolled, he is wild and unruly—we are trying him now for that—but who is responsible for his life?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Who is responsible for his having received such an unseemly bringing up, in spite of his excellent disposition and his grateful and sensitive heart?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did any one train him to be reasonable?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Was he enlightened by study?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Did any one love him ever so little in his childhood?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: My client was left to the care of Providence like a beast of the field.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He thirsted perhaps to see his father after long years of separation.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A thousand times perhaps he may, recalling his childhood, have driven away the loathsome phantoms that haunted his childish dreams and with all his heart he may have longed to embrace and to forgive his father!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And what awaited him?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He was met by cynical taunts, suspicions and wrangling about money.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He heard nothing but revolting talk and vicious precepts uttered daily over the brandy, and at last he saw his father seducing his mistress from him with his own money.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, gentlemen of the jury, that was cruel and revolting!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And that old man was always complaining of the disrespect and cruelty of his son.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He slandered him in society, injured him, calumniated him, bought up his unpaid debts to get him thrown into prison.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury, people like my client, who are fierce, unruly, and uncontrolled on the surface, are sometimes, most frequently indeed, exceedingly tender-hearted, only they don’t express it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Don’t laugh, don’t laugh at my idea!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The talented prosecutor laughed mercilessly just now at my client for loving Schiller—loving the sublime and beautiful!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I should not have laughed at that in his place.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Yes, such natures—oh, let me speak in defense of such natures, so often and so cruelly misunderstood—these natures often thirst for tenderness, goodness, and justice, as it were, in contrast to themselves, their unruliness, their ferocity—they thirst for it unconsciously.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Passionate and fierce on the surface, they are painfully capable of loving woman, for instance, and with a spiritual and elevated love.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Again do not laugh at me, this is very often the case in such natures.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But they cannot hide their passions—sometimes very coarse—and that is conspicuous and is noticed, but the inner man is unseen.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Their passions are quickly exhausted; but, by the side of a noble and lofty creature that seemingly coarse and rough man seeks a new life, seeks to correct himself, to be better, to become noble and honorable, ‘sublime and beautiful,’ however much the expression has been ridiculed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I said just now that I would not venture to touch upon my client’s engagement.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But I may say half a word.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What we heard just now was not evidence, but only the scream of a frenzied and revengeful woman, and it was not for her—oh, not for her!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: —to reproach him with treachery, for she has betrayed him!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If she had had but a little time for reflection she would not have given such evidence.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Oh, do not believe her!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, my client is not a monster, as she called him!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “The Lover of Mankind on the eve of His Crucifixion said: ‘I am the Good Shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep, so that not one of them might be lost. Let not a man’s soul be lost through us!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “I asked just now what does ‘father’ mean, and exclaimed that it was a great word, a precious name.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But one must use words honestly, gentlemen, and I venture to call things by their right names: such a father as old Karamazov cannot be called a father and does not deserve to be.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Filial love for an unworthy father is an absurdity, an impossibility.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Love cannot be created from nothing: only God can create something from nothing.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “‘Fathers, provoke not your children to wrath,’ the apostle writes, from a heart glowing with love.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It’s not for the sake of my client that I quote these sacred words, I mention them for all fathers.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Who has authorized me to preach to fathers?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No one.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But as a man and a citizen I make my appeal—vivos voco!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: We are not long on earth, we do many evil deeds and say many evil words.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: So let us all catch a favorable moment when we are all together to say a good word to each other.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That’s what I am doing: while I am in this place I take advantage of my opportunity.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Not for nothing is this tribune given us by the highest authority—all Russia hears us!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I am not speaking only for the fathers here present, I cry aloud to all fathers: ‘Fathers, provoke not your children to wrath. Yes, let us first fulfill Christ’s injunction ourselves and only then venture to expect it of our children. Otherwise we are not fathers, but enemies of our children, and they are not our children, but our enemies, and we have made them our enemies ourselves. ‘What measure ye mete it shall be measured unto you again’—it’s not I who say that, it’s the Gospel precept, measure to others according as they measure to you.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: How can we blame children if they measure us according to our measure?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Not long ago a servant girl in Finland was suspected of having secretly given birth to a child.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She was watched, and a box of which no one knew anything was found in the corner of the loft, behind some bricks.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was opened and inside was found the body of a new-born child which she had killed.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: In the same box were found the skeletons of two other babies which, according to her own confession, she had killed at the moment of their birth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury, was she a mother to her children?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: She gave birth to them, indeed; but was she a mother to them?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Would any one venture to give her the sacred name of mother?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Let us be bold, gentlemen, let us be audacious even: it’s our duty to be so at this moment and not to be afraid of certain words and ideas like the Moscow women in Ostrovsky’s play, who are scared at the sound of certain words.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, let us prove that the progress of the last few years has touched even us, and let us say plainly, the father is not merely he who begets the child, but he who begets it and does his duty by it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, of course, there is the other meaning, there is the other interpretation of the word ‘father,’ which insists that any father, even though he be a monster, even though he be the enemy of his children, still remains my father simply because he begot me. But this is, so to say, the mystical meaning which I cannot comprehend with my intellect, but can only accept by faith, or, better to say, on faith, like many other things which I do not understand, but which religion bids me believe. But in that case let it be kept outside the sphere of actual life. In the sphere of actual life, which has, indeed, its own rights, but also lays upon us great duties and obligations, in that sphere, if we want to be humane—Christian, in fact—we must, or ought to, act only upon convictions justified by reason and experience, which have been passed through the crucible of analysis; in a word, we must act rationally, and not as though in dream and delirium, that we may not do harm, that we may not ill-treat and ruin a man. Then it will be real Christian work, not only mystic, but rational and philanthropic....”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There was violent applause at this passage from many parts of the court, but Fetyukovitch waved his hands as though imploring them to let him finish without interruption.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The court relapsed into silence at once.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The orator went on.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Do you suppose, gentlemen, that our children as they grow up and begin to reason can avoid such questions?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, they cannot, and we will not impose on them an impossible restriction.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The sight of an unworthy father involuntarily suggests tormenting questions to a young creature, especially when he compares him with the excellent fathers of his companions.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The conventional answer to this question is: ‘He begot you, and you are his flesh and blood, and therefore you are bound to love him. The youth involuntarily reflects: ‘But did he love me when he begot me?’ he asks, wondering more and more.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘Was it for my sake he begot me? He did not know me, not even my sex, at that moment, at the moment of passion, perhaps, inflamed by wine, and he has only transmitted to me a propensity to drunkenness—that’s all he’s done for me.... Why am I bound to love him simply for begetting me when he has cared nothing for me all my life after?’

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, perhaps those questions strike you as coarse and cruel, but do not expect an impossible restraint from a young mind. ‘Drive nature out of the door and it will fly in at the window,’ and, above all, let us not be afraid of words, but decide the question according to the dictates of reason and humanity and not of mystic ideas. How shall it be decided? Why, like this. Let the son stand before his father and ask him, ‘Father, tell me, why must I love you? Father, show me that I must love you,’ and if that father is able to answer him and show him good reason, we have a real, normal, parental relation, not resting on mystical prejudice, but on a rational, responsible and strictly humanitarian basis. But if he does not, there’s an end to the family tie. He is not a father to him, and the son has a right to look upon him as a stranger, and even an enemy. Our tribune, gentlemen of the jury, ought to be a school of true and sound ideas.”

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: (Here the orator was interrupted by irrepressible and almost frantic applause. Of course, it was not the whole audience, but a good half of it applauded. The fathers and mothers present applauded. Shrieks and exclamations were heard from the gallery, where the ladies were sitting. Handkerchiefs were waved. The President began ringing his bell with all his might. He was obviously irritated by the behavior of the audience, but did not venture to clear the court as he had threatened. Even persons of high position, old men with stars on their breasts, sitting on specially reserved seats behind the judges, applauded the orator and waved their handkerchiefs. So that when the noise died down, the President confined himself to repeating his stern threat to clear the court, and Fetyukovitch, excited and triumphant, continued his speech.)

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Gentlemen of the jury, you remember that awful night of which so much has been said to-day, when the son got over the fence and stood face to face with the enemy and persecutor who had begotten him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I insist most emphatically it was not for money he ran to his father’s house: the charge of robbery is an absurdity, as I proved before.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And it was not to murder him he broke into the house, oh, no!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If he had had that design he would, at least, have taken the precaution of arming himself beforehand.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The brass pestle he caught up instinctively without knowing why he did it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Granted that he deceived his father by tapping at the window, granted that he made his way in—I’ve said already that I do not for a moment believe that legend, but let it be so, let us suppose it for a moment.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentlemen, I swear to you by all that’s holy, if it had not been his father, but an ordinary enemy, he would, after running through the rooms and satisfying himself that the woman was not there, have made off, post-haste, without doing any harm to his rival.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He would have struck him, pushed him away perhaps, nothing more, for he had no thought and no time to spare for that.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: What he wanted to know was where she was.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But his father, his father!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: The mere sight of the father who had hated him from his childhood, had been his enemy, his persecutor, and now his unnatural rival, was enough!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: A feeling of hatred came over him involuntarily, irresistibly, clouding his reason.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It all surged up in one moment!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It was an impulse of madness and insanity, but also an impulse of nature, irresistibly and unconsciously (like everything in nature) avenging the violation of its eternal laws.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But the prisoner even then did not murder him—I maintain that, I cry that aloud!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: —no, he only brandished the pestle in a burst of indignant disgust, not meaning to kill him, not knowing that he would kill him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Had he not had this fatal pestle in his hand, he would have only knocked his father down perhaps, but would not have killed him.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: As he ran away, he did not know whether he had killed the old man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Such a murder is not a murder.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Such a murder is not a parricide.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: No, the murder of such a father cannot be called parricide.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Such a murder can only be reckoned parricide by prejudice.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But I appeal to you again and again from the depths of my soul; did this murder actually take place?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Gentlemen of the jury, if we convict and punish him, he will say to himself: ‘These people have done nothing for my bringing up, for my education, nothing to improve my lot, nothing to make me better, nothing to make me a man.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: These people have not given me to eat and to drink, have not visited me in prison and nakedness, and here they have sent me to penal servitude.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: I am quits, I owe them nothing now, and owe no one anything for ever.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They are wicked and I will be wicked.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: They are cruel and I will be cruel.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: That is what he will say, gentlemen of the jury.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And I swear, by finding him guilty you will only make it easier for him: you will ease his conscience, he will curse the blood he has shed and will not regret it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: At the same time you will destroy in him the possibility of becoming a new man, for he will remain in his wickedness and blindness all his life.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “But do you want to punish him fearfully, terribly, with the most awful punishment that could be imagined, and at the same time to save him and regenerate his soul?

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: If so, overwhelm him with your mercy!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: You will see, you will hear how he will tremble and be horror-struck.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: ‘How can I endure this mercy? How can I endure so much love? Am I worthy of it? That’s what he will exclaim.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: “Oh, I know, I know that heart, that wild but grateful heart, gentlemen of the jury!

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: It will bow before your mercy; it thirsts for a great and loving action, it will melt and mount upwards.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: There are souls which, in their limitation, blame the whole world.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: But subdue such a soul with mercy, show it love, and it will curse its past, for there are many good impulses in it.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: Such a heart will expand and see that God is merciful and that men are good and just.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: He will be horror-stricken; he will be crushed by remorse and the vast obligation laid upon him henceforth.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
text: And he will not say then, ‘I am quits,’ but will say, ‘I am guilty in the sight of all men and am more unworthy than all. With tears of penitence and poignant, tender anguish, he will exclaim: ‘Others are better than I, they wanted to save me, not to ruin me! Oh, this act of mercy is so easy for you, for in the absence of anything like real evidence it will be too awful for you to pronounce: ‘Yes, he is guilty.’

title: The Brothers Karamazov

title: The Brothers Karamazov

But you are innocent, and such a cross is too much for you. You wanted to make yourself another man by suffering. I say, only remember that other man always, all your life and wherever you go; and that will be enough for you. Your refusal of that great cross will only serve to make you feel all your life an even greater duty, and that constant feeling will do more to make you a new man, perhaps, than if you went there. title: The Brothers Karamazov

Work and grammar—that’s how we’ll spend three years. And by that time we shall speak English like any Englishman. And as soon as we’ve learnt it—good-by to America! We’ll run here to Russia as American citizens. Don’t be uneasy—we would not come to this little town. We’d hide somewhere, a long way off, in the north or in the south. I shall be changed by that time, and she will, too, in America. The doctors shall make me some sort of wart on my face—what’s the use of their being so mechanical!—or else I’ll put out one eye, let my beard grow a yard, and I shall turn gray, fretting for Russia. People talk to you a great deal about your education, but some good, sacred memory, preserved from childhood, is perhaps the best education. If a man carries many such memories with him into life, he is safe to the end of his days, and if one has only one good memory left in one’s heart, even that may sometime be the means of saving us. Perhaps we may even grow wicked later on, may be unable to refrain from a bad action, may laugh at men’s tears and at those people who say as Kolya did just now, ‘I want to suffer for all men,’ and may even jeer spitefully at such people. title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: All at once, on the Promenade, as it was called—that is to say, in the Chestnut Avenue—I came face to face with my Englishman.

title: The Gambler
text: “I was just coming to see you,” he said; “and you appear to be out on a similar errand. So you have parted with your employers?”

title: The Gambler
text: “How do you know that? I asked in astonishment. “Is every one aware of the fact?”

title: The Gambler
text: “By no means. Not every one would consider such a fact to be of moment. Indeed, I have never heard any one speak of it.”

title: The Gambler
text: “Then how come you to know it?”

title: The Gambler
text: “Because I have had occasion to do so. Whither are you bound? I like you, and was therefore coming to pay you a visit.”

title: The Gambler
text: “What a splendid fellow you are, Mr. Astley! I cried, though still wondering how he had come by his knowledge. “And since I have not yet had my coffee, and you have, in all probability, scarcely tasted yours, let us adjourn to the Casino Café, where we can sit and smoke and have a talk.”

title: The Gambler
text: The café in question was only a hundred paces away; so, when coffee had been brought, we seated ourselves, and I lit a cigarette.

title: The Gambler
text: Astley was no smoker, but, taking a seat by my side, he prepared himself to listen.

title: The Gambler
text: “I do not intend to go away,” was my first remark.

title: The Gambler
text: “I intend, on the contrary, to remain here.”

title: The Gambler
text: “That I never doubted,” he answered good-humouredly.

title: The Gambler
text: It is a curious fact that, on my way to see him, I had never even thought of telling him of my love for Polina.

title: The Gambler
text: In fact, I had purposely meant to avoid any mention of the subject.

title: The Gambler
text: Nor, during our stay in the place, had I ever made aught but the scantiest reference to it.

title: The Gambler
text: You see, not only was Astley a man of great reserve, but also from the first I had perceived that Polina had made a great impression upon him, although he never spoke of her.

title: The Gambler
text: But now, strangely enough, he had no sooner seated himself and bent his steely gaze upon me, than, for some reason or another, I felt moved to tell him everything—to speak to him of my love in all its phases.

title: The Gambler
text: For an hour and a half did I discourse on the subject, and found it a pleasure to do so, even though this was the first occasion on which I had referred to the matter.

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: Yet one thing I regret: and that is that I made references to the Frenchman which were a little over-personal.

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: “No, I fear not,” I replied.

title: The Gambler
text: “And concerning this Marquis and Mlle. Polina you know nothing beyond surmise?”

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: “No, I know nothing for certain about them” was my reply.

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: “Then you have done very wrong to speak of them to me, or even to imagine things about them.”

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: In conclusion, I showed Astley the note which I had lately received.

title: The Gambler
text: “What do you make of it? I asked. “When I met you I was just coming to ask you your opinion. For myself, I could have killed this Frenchman, and am not sure that I shall not do so even yet.”

title: The Gambler

title: The Gambler
text: “As for Mlle. Polina—well, you yourself know that, if necessity drives, one enters into relation with people whom one simply detests. Even between this couple there may be something which, though unknown to you, depends upon extraneous circumstances. For, my own part, I think that you may reassure yourself—or at all events partially. And as for Mlle. Polina’s proceedings of two days ago, they were, of course, strange; not because she can have meant to get rid of you, or to earn for you a thrashing from the Baron’s cudgel (which for some curious reason, he did not use, although he had it ready in his hands), but because such proceedings on the part of such—well, of such a refined lady as Mlle. Polina are, to say the least of it, unbecoming. But she cannot have guessed that you would carry out her absurd wish to the letter?”

title: The Gambler
text: “Do you know what?” suddenly I cried as I fixed Mr. Astley with my gaze.

title: The Gambler
text: “I believe that you have already heard the story from some one—very possibly from Mlle. Polina herself?”

title: The Gambler
text: In return he gave me an astonished stare.

title: The Gambler
text: “Your eyes look very fiery,” he said with a return of his former calm, “and in them I can read suspicion. Now, you have no right whatever to be suspicious. It is not a right which I can for a moment recognise, and I absolutely refuse to answer your questions.”

title: The Gambler
text: “Enough! You need say no more,” I cried with a strange emotion at my heart, yet not altogether understanding what had aroused that emotion in my breast.

title: The Gambler
text: Indeed, when, where, and how could Polina have chosen Astley to be one of her confidants?

title: The Gambler
text: Of late I had come rather to overlook him in this connection, even though Polina had always been a riddle to me—so much so that now, when I had just permitted myself to tell my friend of my infatuation in all its aspects, I had found myself struck, during the very telling, with the fact that in my relations with her I could specify nothing that was explicit, nothing that was positive.

title: The Gambler
text: On the contrary, my relations had been purely fantastic, strange, and unreal; they had been unlike anything else that I could think of.

title: The Gambler
text: “Very well, very well,” I replied with a warmth equal to Astley’s own.

title: The Gambler
text: “Then I stand confounded, and have no further opinions to offer. But you are a good fellow, and I am glad to know what you think about it all, even though I do not need your advice.”

title: The Gambler
text: Then, after a pause, I resumed:

title: The Gambler
text: “For instance, what reason should you assign for the General taking fright in this way? Why should my stupid clowning have led the world to elevate it into a serious incident? Even De Griers has found it necessary to put in his oar (and he only interferes on the most important occasions), and to visit me, and to address to me the most earnest supplications. Yes, he, De Griers, has actually been playing the suppliant to me! And, mark you, although he came to me as early as nine o’clock, he had ready-prepared in his hand Mlle. Polina’s note. When, I would ask, was that note written? Mlle. Polina must have been aroused from sleep for the express purpose of writing it. At all events the circumstance shows that she is an absolute slave to the Frenchman, since she actually begs my pardon in the note—actually begs my pardon! Yet what is her personal concern in the matter? Why is she interested in it at all? Why, too, is the whole party so afraid of this precious Baron? And what sort of a business do you call it for the General to be going to marry Mlle. Blanche de Cominges? He told me last night that, because of the circumstance, he must ‘move with especial care at present. What is your opinion of it all? Your look convinces me that you know more about it than I do.”

title: The Gambler
text: Mr. Astley smiled and nodded.

title: The Gambler
text: “Yes, I think I do know more about it than you do,” he assented.

title: The Gambler
text: “The affair centres around this Mlle. Blanche. Of that I feel certain.”

title: The Gambler
text: “And what of Mlle.

title: The Gambler
text: Blanche?

title: The Gambler
