text: Who is he?

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Who is Shatov?

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Will he inform, or won't he?

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: There was a shower of questions.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "If he were an informer he would have kept up appearances instead of cursing it all and going away," observed someone.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "See, Stavrogin is getting up too. Stavrogin has not answered the question either," cried the girl-student.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin did actually stand up, and at the other end of the table Kirillov rose at the same time.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Excuse me, Mr. Stavrogin," Madame Virginsky addressed him sharply, "we all answered the question, while you are going away without a word."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I see no necessity to answer the question which interests you," muttered Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "But we've compromised ourselves and you won't," shouted several voices.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "What business is it of mine if you have compromised yourselves?" laughed Stavrogin, but his eyes flashed.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "What business? What business?" voices exclaimed.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Many people got up from their chairs.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Allow me, gentlemen, allow me," cried the lame man.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Mr. Verhovensky hasn't answered the question either; he has only asked it."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: The remark produced a striking effect.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: All looked at one another.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin laughed aloud in the lame man's face and went out; Kirillov followed him; Verhovensky ran after them into the passage.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "What are you doing?" he faltered, seizing Stavrogin's hand and gripping it with all his might in his.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin pulled away his hand without a word.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Be at Kirillov's directly, I'll come.... It's absolutely necessary for me to see you!..."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "It isn't necessary for me," Stavrogin cut him short.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Stavrogin will be there," Kirillov said finally.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Stavrogin, it is necessary for you. I will show you that there."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: They went out.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: They had gone.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Pyotr Stepanovitch was about to rush back to the meeting to bring order into chaos, but probably reflecting that it wasn't worth bothering about, left everything, and two minutes later was flying after the other two.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: On the way he remembered a short cut to Filipov's house.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He rushed along it, up to his knees in mud, and did in fact arrive at the very moment when Stavrogin and Kirillov were coming in at the gate.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You here already?" observed Kirillov.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "That's good. Come in."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "How is it you told us you lived alone," asked Stavrogin, passing a boiling samovar in the passage.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You will see directly who it is I live with," muttered Kirillov.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Go in."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: They had hardly entered when Verhovensky at once took out of his pocket the anonymous letter he had taken from Lembke, and laid it before Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: They all then sat down.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin read the letter in silence.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Well?" he asked.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "That scoundrel will do as he writes," Verhovensky explained.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "So, as he is under your control, tell me how to act. I assure you he may go to Lembke to-morrow."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Well, let him go."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Let him go! And when we can prevent him, too!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You are mistaken. He is not dependent on me. Besides, I don't care; he doesn't threaten me in any way; he only threatens you."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You too."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I don't think so."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "But there are other people who may not spare you. Surely you understand that? Listen, Stavrogin. This is only playing with words. Surely you don't grudge the money?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Why, would it cost money?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "It certainly would; two thousand or at least fifteen hundred. Give it to me to-morrow or even to-day, and to-morrow evening I'll send him to Petersburg for you. That's just what he wants. If you like, he can take Marya Timofyevna. Note that."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: There was something distracted about him.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He spoke, as it were, without caution, and he did not reflect on his words.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin watched him, wondering.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I've no reason to send Marya Timofyevna away."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Perhaps you don't even want to," Pyotr Stepanovitch smiled ironically.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Perhaps I don't."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "In short, will there be the money or not?" he cried with angry impatience, and as it were peremptorily, to Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: The latter scrutinised him gravely.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "There won't be the money."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Look here, Stavrogin! You know something, or have done something already! You are going it!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: His face worked, the corners of his mouth twitched, and he suddenly laughed an unprovoked and irrelevant laugh.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "But you've had money from your father for the estate," Stavrogin observed calmly.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Maman sent you six or eight thousand for Stepan Trofimovitch.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: So you can pay the fifteen hundred out of your own money.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: I don't care to pay for other people.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: I've given a lot as it is.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: It annoys me....

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He smiled himself at his own words.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Ah, you are beginning to joke!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin got up from his chair.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Verhovensky instantly jumped up too, and mechanically stood with his back to the door as though barring the way to him.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin had already made a motion to push him aside and go out, when he stopped short.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I won't give up Shatov to you," he said.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Pyotr Stepanovitch started.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: They looked at one another.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I told you this evening why you needed Shatov's blood," said Stavrogin, with flashing eyes.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "It's the cement you want to bind your groups together with. You drove Shatov away cleverly just now. You knew very well that he wouldn't promise not to inform and he would have thought it mean to lie to you. But what do you want with me? What do you want with me? Ever since we met abroad you won't let me alone. The explanation you've given me so far was simply raving. Meanwhile you are driving at my giving Lebyadkin fifteen hundred roubles, so as to give Fedka an opportunity to murder him. I know that you think I want my wife murdered too. You think to tie my hands by this crime, and have me in your power. That's it, isn't it? What good will that be to you? What the devil do you want with me? Look at me. Once for all, am I the man for you? And let me alone."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Has Fedka been to you himself?

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Verhovensky asked breathlessly.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Yes, he came.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: His price is fifteen hundred too....

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: But here; he'll repeat it himself.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: There he stands.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin stretched out his hand.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Pyotr Stepanovitch turned round quickly.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: A new figure, Fedka, wearing a sheep-skin coat, but without a cap, as though he were at home, stepped out of the darkness in the doorway.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He stood there laughing and showing his even white teeth.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: His black eyes, with yellow whites, darted cautiously about the room watching the gentlemen.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: There was something he did not understand.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He had evidently been just brought in by Kirillov, and his inquiring eyes turned to the latter.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He stood in the doorway, but was unwilling to come into the room.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I suppose you got him ready here to listen to our bargaining, or that he may actually see the money in our hands. Is that it?" asked Stavrogin; and without waiting for an answer he walked out of the house.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Verhovensky, almost frantic, overtook him at the gate.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Stop! Not another step!" he cried, seizing him by the arm.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin tried to pull away his arm, but did not succeed.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He was overcome with fury.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Seizing Verhovensky by the hair with his left hand he flung him with all his might on the ground and went out at the gate.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: But he had not gone thirty paces before Verhovensky overtook him again.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Let us make it up; let us make it up!" he murmured in a spasmodic whisper.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin shrugged his shoulders, but neither answered nor turned round.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Listen. I will bring you Lizaveta Nikolaevna to-morrow; shall I? No? Why don't you answer? Tell me what you want. I'll do it. Listen. I'll let you have Shatov. Shall I?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Then it's true that you meant to kill him?" cried Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "What do you want with Shatov? What is he to you? Pyotr Stepanovitch went on, gasping, speaking rapidly. He was in a frenzy, and kept running forward and seizing Stavrogin by the elbow, probably unaware of what he was doing. "Listen.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: I'll let you have him.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Let's make it up.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Your price is a very great one, but...

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Let's make it up!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin glanced at him at last, and was amazed.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: The eyes, the voice, were not the same as always, or as they had been in the room just now.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: What he saw was almost another face.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: The intonation of the voice was different.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Verhovensky besought, implored.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He was a man from whom what was most precious was being taken or had been taken, and who was still stunned by the shock.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "But what's the matter with you?" cried Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: The other did not answer, but ran after him and gazed at him with the same imploring but yet inflexible expression.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Let's make it up!" he whispered once more.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Listen. Like Fedka, I have a knife in my boot, but I'll make it up with you!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "But what do you want with me, damn you? Stavrogin cried, with intense anger and amazement. "Is there some mystery about it?

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Am I a sort of talisman for you?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Listen. We are going to make a revolution," the other muttered rapidly, and almost in delirium.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You don't believe we shall make a revolution? We are going to make such an upheaval that everything will be uprooted from its foundation. Karmazinov is right that there is nothing to lay hold of. Karmazinov is very intelligent. Another ten such groups in different parts of Russia--and I am safe."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Groups of fools like that?" broke reluctantly from Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Oh, don't be so clever, Stavrogin; don't be so clever yourself. And you know you are by no means so intelligent that you need wish others to be. You are afraid, you have no faith. You are frightened at our doing things on such a scale. And why are they fools? They are not such fools. No one has a mind of his own nowadays. There are terribly few original minds nowadays. Virginsky is a pure-hearted man, ten times as pure as you or I; but never mind about him. Liputin is a rogue, but I know one point about him. Every rogue has some point in him.... Lyamshin is the only one who hasn't, but he is in my hands. A few more groups, and I should have money and passports everywhere; so much at least. Suppose it were only that? And safe places, so that they can search as they like. They might uproot one group but they'd stick at the next. We'll set things in a ferment.... Surely you don't think that we two are not enough?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Take Shigalov, and let me alone...."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Shigalov is a man of genius! Do you know he is a genius like Fourier, but bolder than Fourier; stronger. I'll look after him. He's discovered 'equality'!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "He is in a fever; he is raving; something very queer has happened to him," thought Stavrogin, looking at him once more.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Both walked on without stopping.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "He's written a good thing in that manuscript," Verhovensky went on.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "He suggests a system of spying. Every member of the society spies on the others, and it's his duty to inform against them. Every one belongs to all and all to every one. All are slaves and equal in their slavery. In extreme cases he advocates slander and murder, but the great thing about it is equality. To begin with, the level of education, science, and talents is lowered. A high level of education and science is only possible for great intellects, and they are not wanted. The great intellects have always seized the power and been despots. Great intellects cannot help being despots and they've always done more harm than good. They will be banished or put to death. Cicero will have his tongue cut out, Copernicus will have his eyes put out, Shakespeare will be stoned--that's Shigalovism. Slaves are bound to be equal. There has never been either freedom or equality without despotism, but in the herd there is bound to be equality, and that's Shigalovism! Ha ha ha! Do you think it strange? I am for Shigalovism."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin tried to quicken his pace, and to reach home as soon as possible.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "If this fellow is drunk, where did he manage to get drunk?" crossed his mind.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Can it be the brandy?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Listen, Stavrogin. To level the mountains is a fine idea, not an absurd one. I am for Shigalov. Down with culture. We've had enough science! Without science we have material enough to go on for a thousand years, but one must have discipline. The one thing wanting in the world is discipline. The thirst for culture is an aristocratic thirst. The moment you have family ties or love you get the desire for property. We will destroy that desire; we'll make use of drunkenness, slander, spying; we'll make use of incredible corruption; we'll stifle every genius in its infancy. We'll reduce all to a common denominator! Complete equality! 'We've learned a trade, and we are honest men; we need nothing more,' that was an answer given by English working-men recently. Only the necessary is necessary, that's the motto of the whole world henceforward. But it needs a shock. That's for us, the directors, to look after. Slaves must have directors. Absolute submission, absolute loss of individuality, but once in thirty years Shigalov would let them have a shock and they would all suddenly begin eating one another up, to a certain point, simply as a precaution against boredom. Boredom is an aristocratic sensation. The Shigalovians will have no desires. Desire and suffering are our lot, but Shigalovism is for the slaves."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You exclude yourself?

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin broke in again.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "You, too. Do you know, I have thought of giving up the world to the Pope. Let him come forth, on foot, and barefoot, and show himself to the rabble, saying, 'See what they have brought me to!' and they will all rush after him, even the troops. The Pope at the head, with us round him, and below us--Shigalovism. All that's needed is that the Internationale should come to an agreement with the Pope; so it will. And the old chap will agree at once. There's nothing else he can do. Remember my words! Ha ha! Is it stupid? Tell me, is it stupid or not?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "That's enough!

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin muttered with vexation.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Enough! Listen. I've given up the Pope! Damn Shigalovism! Damn the Pope! We must have something more everyday. Not Shigalovism, for Shigalovism is a rare specimen of the jeweller's art. It's an ideal; it's in the future. Shigalov is an artist and a fool like every philanthropist. We need coarse work, and Shigalov despises coarse work. Listen. The Pope shall be for the west, and you shall be for us, you shall be for us!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Let me alone, you drunken fellow!" muttered Stavrogin, and he quickened his pace.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Stavrogin, you are beautiful," cried Pyotr Stepanovitch, almost ecstatically.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Do you know that you are beautiful! What's the most precious thing about you is that you sometimes don't know it. Oh, I've studied you! I often watch you on the sly! There's a lot of simpleheartedness and naïveté about you still. Do you know that? There still is, there is! You must be suffering and suffering genuinely from that simple-heartedness. I love beauty. I am a nihilist, but I love beauty. Are nihilists incapable of loving beauty? It's only idols they dislike, but I love an idol. You are my idol! You injure no one, and every one hates you. You treat every one as an equal, and yet every one is afraid of you--that's good. Nobody would slap you on the shoulder. You are an awful aristocrat. An aristocrat is irresistible when he goes in for democracy! To sacrifice life, your own or another's is nothing to you. You are just the man that's needed. It's just such a man as you that I need. I know no one but you. You are the leader, you are the sun and I am your worm."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: He suddenly kissed his hand.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: A shiver ran down Stavrogin's spine, and he pulled away his hand in dismay.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: They stood still.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Madman!" whispered Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Perhaps I am raving; perhaps I am raving," Pyotr Stepanovitch assented, speaking rapidly.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "But I've thought of the first step! Shigalov would never have thought of it. There are lots of Shigalovs, but only one man, one man in Russia has hit on the first step and knows how to take it. And I am that man! Why do you look at me? I need you, you; without you I am nothing. Without you I am a fly, a bottled idea; Columbus without America."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin stood still and looked intently into his wild eyes.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Listen. First of all we'll make an upheaval," Verhovensky went on in desperate haste, continually clutching at Stavrogin's left sleeve.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "I've already told you. We shall penetrate to the peasantry. Do you know that we are tremendously powerful already? Our party does not consist only of those who commit murder and arson, fire off pistols in the traditional fashion, or bite colonels. They are only a hindrance. I don't accept anything without discipline. I am a scoundrel, of course, and not a socialist. Ha ha! Listen. I've reckoned them all up: a teacher who laughs with children at their God and at their cradle is on our side. The lawyer who defends an educated murderer because he is more cultured than his victims and could not help murdering them to get money is one of us. The schoolboys who murder a peasant for the sake of sensation are ours. The juries who acquit every criminal are ours. The prosecutor who trembles at a trial for fear he should not seem advanced enough is ours, ours. Among officials and literary men we have lots, lots, and they don't know it themselves. On the other hand, the docility of schoolboys and fools has reached an extreme pitch; the schoolmasters are bitter and bilious. On all sides we see vanity puffed up out of all proportion; brutal, monstrous appetites.... Do you know how many we shall catch by little, ready-made ideas? When I left Russia, Littre's dictum that crime is insanity was all the rage; I come back and I find that crime is no longer insanity, but simply common sense, almost a duty; anyway, a gallant protest. 'How can we expect a cultured man not to commit a murder, if he is in need of money. But these are only the first fruits. The Russian God has already been vanquished by cheap vodka. The peasants are drunk, the mothers are drunk, the children are drunk, the churches are empty, and in the peasant courts one hears, 'Two hundred lashes or stand us a bucket of vodka. Oh, this generation has only to grow up. It's only a pity we can't afford to wait, or we might have let them get a bit more tipsy! Ah, what a pity there's no proletariat! But there will be, there will be; we are going that way...."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "It's a pity, too, that we've grown greater fools," muttered Stavrogin, moving forward as before.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Listen. I've seen a child of six years old leading home his drunken mother, whilst she swore at him with foul words. Do you suppose I am glad of that? When it's in our hands, maybe we'll mend things... if need be, we'll drive them for forty years into the wilderness.... But one or two generations of vice are essential now; monstrous, abject vice by which a man is transformed into a loathsome, cruel, egoistic reptile. That's what we need! And what's more, a little 'fresh blood' that we may get accustomed to it. Why are you laughing? I am not contradicting myself. I am only contradicting the philanthropists and Shigalovism, not myself! I am a scoundrel, not a socialist. Ha ha ha! I'm only sorry there's no time. I promised Karmazinov to begin in May, and to make an end by October. Is that too soon? Ha ha! Do you know what, Stavrogin? Though the Russian people use foul language, there's nothing cynical about them so far. Do you know the serfs had more self-respect than Karmazinov? Though they were beaten they always preserved their gods, which is more than Karmazinov's done."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Well, Verhovensky, this is the first time I've heard you talk, and I listen with amazement," observed Stavrogin.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "So you are really not a socialist, then, but some sort of... ambitious politician?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "A scoundrel, a scoundrel! You are wondering what I am. I'll tell you what I am directly, that's what I am leading up to. It was not for nothing that I kissed your hand. But the people must believe that we know what we are after, while the other side do nothing but 'brandish their cudgels and beat their own followers. Ah, if we only had more time! That's the only trouble, we have no time. We will proclaim destruction.... Why is it, why is it that idea has such a fascination. But we must have a little exercise; we must. We'll set fires going.... We'll set legends going. Every scurvy 'group' will be of use. Out of those very groups I'll pick you out fellows so keen they'll not shrink from shooting, and be grateful for the honour of a job, too. Well, and there will be an upheaval! There's going to be such an upset as the world has never seen before.... Russia will be overwhelmed with darkness, the earth will weep for its old gods.... Well, then we shall bring forward... whom?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Whom?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Ivan the Tsarevitch."

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Who-m?"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Ivan the Tsarevitch. You! You!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Stavrogin thought a minute.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "A pretender?" he asked suddenly, looking with intense surprise at his frantic companion.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "Ah! so that's your plan at last!"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: "We shall say that he is 'in hiding,'"

title: The possessed :  or, The devils
text: Verhovensky said softly, in a sort of tender whisper, as though he really were drunk indeed.

title: The possessed :  or, The devils

text: She despised herself—her cheeks burned.

text: With folded hands, and teeth biting hard into her lips, she stood in one spot, motionless.

text: “So that’s the sort of person you are!” he cried panting.

text: “At last I have found you out, have I?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Found me out?” repeated Zina, looking at him as though he were a madman.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Suddenly her eyes flashed with rage.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How dare you address me like that?” she cried, advancing towards him.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I have heard all!” said Mosgliakoff solemnly, but involuntarily taking a step backwards.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “You heard? I see—you have been eavesdropping!” cried Zina, looking at him with disdain.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, I have been eavesdropping! Yes—I consented to do a mean action, and my reward is that I have found out that you, too, are——I don’t know how to express to you what I think you!” he replied, looking more and more timid under Zina’s eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And supposing that you have heard all: what right have you to blame me? What right have you to speak to me so insolently, in any case?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I!—I? what right have I? and you can ask me this? You are going to marry this prince, and I have no right to say a word! Why, you gave me your promise—is that nothing?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “When?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How, when?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Did not I tell you that morning, when you came to me with your sentimental nonsense—did I not tell you that I could give you no decided answer?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But you did not reject me; you did not send me away. I see—you kept me hanging in reserve, in case of need! You lured me into your net! I see, I see it all!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: An expression of pain flitted over Zina’s careworn face, as though someone had suddenly stabbed her to the heart; but she mastered her feelings.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “If I didn’t turn you out of the house,” she began deliberately and very clearly, though her voice had a scarcely perceptible tremor in it, “I refrained from such a course purely out of pity. You begged me yourself to postpone, to give you time, not to say you ‘No,’ to study you better, and ‘then,’ you said, ‘then, when you know what a fine fellow I am, perhaps you will not refuse me! These were your own words, or very like them, at the very beginning of your courtship!—you cannot deny them! And now you dare to tell me that I ‘lured you into my net,’ just as though you did not notice my expression of loathing when you made your appearance this morning! You came a fortnight sooner than I expected you, and I did not hide my disgust; on the contrary, I made it evident—you must have noticed it—I know you did; because you asked me whether I was angry because you had come sooner than you promised! Let me tell you that people who do not, and do not care to, hide their loathing for a man can hardly be accused of luring that man into their net! You dare to tell me that I was keeping you in reserve! Very well; my answer to that is, that I judged of you like this: ‘Though he may not be endowed with much intellect, still he may turn out to be a good enough fellow; and if so, it might be possible to marry him. However, being persuaded, now, that you are a fool, and a mischievous fool into the bargain,—having found out this fact, to my great joy,—it only remains for me now to wish you every happiness and a pleasant journey. Good-bye!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: With these words Zina turned her back on him, and deliberately made for the door.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff, seeing that all was lost, boiled over with fury.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh! so I’m a fool!” he yelled; “I’m a fool, am I? Very well, good-bye! But before I go, the whole town shall know of this! They shall all hear how you and your mother made the old man drunk, and then swindled him! I shall let the whole world know it! You shall see what Mosgliakoff can do!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Zina trembled and stopped, as though to answer; but on reflection, she contented herself by shrugging her shoulders; glanced contemptuously at Mosgliakoff, and left the room, banging the door after her.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: At this moment Maria Alexandrovna made her appearance.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She heard Mosgliakoff’s exclamation, and, divining at once what had happened, trembled with terror.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff still in the house, and near the prince!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff about to spread the news all over the town!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: At this moment, when secrecy, if only for a short time, was essential!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But Maria Alexandrovna was quick at calculations: she thought, with an eagle flight of the mind, over all the circumstances of the case, and her plan for the pacification of Mosgliakoff was ready in an instant!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What is it, mon ami?” she said, entering the room, and holding out her hand to him with friendly warmth.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “How—‘mon ami?’ ” cried the enraged Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Mon ami, indeed! the moment after you have abused and reviled me like a pickpocket! No, no! Not quite so green, my good lady! I’m not to be so easily imposed upon again!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I am sorry, extremely sorry, to see you in such a strange condition of mind, Paul Alexandrovitch! What expressions you use! You do not take the trouble to choose your words before ladies—oh, fie!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Before ladies? Ho ho! You—you are—you are anything you like—but not a lady!” yelled Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

Really, Maria Alexandrovna, this is a little too much of a good thing! No human being can stand that sort of thing, Maria Alexandrovna! You must be aware of that fact!”

But I have made up my mind to open my heart to you, especially as I am, perhaps, in some degree to blame before you. Sit down; let us talk it over!”

text: Maria Alexandrovna’s voice was tender to a sickly extent.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “And you—and you—with your principles, and with your bringing up, could condescend to such an action—Oh, oh!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Maria Alexandrovna, this is a little too much!” he cried.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Consider what you condescend to do, with your principles, and then judge of other people.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “One more question,” she continued, without replying to his outburst: “who recommended you to be an eavesdropper; who told you anything; who is the spy here? That’s what I wish to know!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, excuse me; that I shall not tell you!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Very well; I know already. I said, Paul, that I was in some degree to blame before you. But if you look into the matter you will find that if I am to blame it is solely in consequence of my anxiety to do you a good turn!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “What? a good turn—me? No, no, madam! I assure you I am not to be caught again! I’m not quite such a fool!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: He moved so violently in his arm-chair that it shook again.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Now, do be cool, if you can, my good friend.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: If I did not tell you all before, it was simply because the whole matter was in an embryo condition in my mind.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: It was then quite possible that what has happened would never happen.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You see, I am quite open with you.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “In the second place, do not blame my daughter. She loves you to distraction; and it was only by the exercise of my utmost influence that I persuaded her to drop you, and accept the prince’s offer.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I have just had the pleasure of receiving convincing proof of her ‘love to distraction!’ ” remarked Mosgliakoff, ironically and bitterly.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Very well. But how did you speak to her? As a lover should speak? Again, ought any man of respectable position and tone to speak like that? You insulted and wounded her!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Never mind about my ‘tone’ now! All I can say is that this morning, when I went away with the prince, in spite of both of you having been as sweet as honey to me before, you reviled me behind my back like a pickpocket! I know all about it, you see!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, from the same dirty source, I suppose?” said Maria Alexandrovna, smiling disdainfully.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, Paul, I did revile you: I pitched into you considerably, and I admit it frankly. But it was simply that I was bound to blacken you before her. Why? Because, as I have said, I required her to consent to leave you, and this consent was so difficult to tear from her! Short-sighted man that you are! If she had not loved you, why should I have required so to blacken your character? Why should I have been obliged to take this extreme step? Oh! you don’t know all! I was forced to use my fullest maternal authority in order to erase you from her heart; and with all my influence and skill I only succeeded in erasing your dear image superficially and partially! If you saw and heard all just now, it cannot have escaped you that Zina did not once, by either word or gesture, encourage or confirm my words to the prince? Throughout the whole scene she said not one word. She sang, but like an automaton! Her whole soul was in anguish, and at last, out of pity for her, I took the prince away. I am sure, she cried, when I left her alone! When you entered the room you must have observed tears in her eyes?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff certainly did recall the fact that when he rushed into the room Zina was crying.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But you—you—why were you so against me, Maria Alexandrovna?” he cried.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Why did you revile me and malign me, as you admit you did?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Ah, now that’s quite a different question. Now, if you had only asked me reasonably at the beginning, you should have had your answer long ago! Yes, you are right. It was I, and I alone, who did it all. Do not think of Zina in the matter. Now, why did I do it? I reply, in the first place, for Zina’s sake. The prince is rich, influential, has great connections, and in marrying him Zina will make a brilliant match. Very well; then if the prince dies—as perhaps he will die soon, for we are all mortal,—Zina is still young, a widow, a princess, and probably very rich. Then she can marry whom she pleases; she may make another brilliant match if she likes. But of course she will marry the man she loves, and loved before, the man whose heart she wounded by accepting the prince. Remorse alone would be enough to make her marry the man whom she had loved and so deeply injured!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Hem!” said Paul, gazing at his boots thoughtfully.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “In the second place,” continued Maria, “and I will put this shortly, because, though you read a great deal of your beloved Shakespeare, and extract his finest thoughts and ideals, yet you are very young, and cannot, perhaps, apply what you read.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You may not understand my feelings in this matter: listen, however.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I am giving my Zina to this prince partly for the prince’s own sake, because I wish to save him by this marriage.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: We are old friends; he is the dearest and best of men, he is a knightly, chivalrous gentleman, and he lives helpless and miserable in the claws of that devil of a woman at Donchanovo!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Heaven knows that I persuaded Zina into this marriage by putting it to her that she would be performing a great and noble action.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I represented her as being the stay and the comfort and the darling and the idol of a poor old man, who probably would not live another year at the most!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I showed her that thus his last days should be made happy with love and light and friendship, instead of wretched with fear and the society of a detestable woman.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Oh! do not blame Zina.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She is guiltless.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I am not—I admit it; for if there have been calculations it is I who have made them!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: But I calculated for her, Paul; for her, not myself!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I have outlived my time; I have thought but for my child, and what mother could blame me for this?

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Tears sparkled in the fond mother’s eyes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Mosgliakoff listened in amazement to all this eloquence, winking his eyes in bewilderment.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, yes, of course! You talk well, Maria Alexandrovna, but you forget—you gave me your word, you encouraged me, you gave me my hopes; and where am I now? I have to stand aside and look a fool!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “But, my dear Paul, you don’t surely suppose that I have not thought of you too! Don’t you see the huge, immeasurable gain to yourself in all this? A gain so vast that I was bound in your interest to act as I did!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Gain for me! How so?” asked Paul, in the most abject state of confusion and bewilderment.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Gracious Heavens! do you mean to say you are really so simple and so short-sighted as to be unable to see that?” cried Maria Alexandrovna, raising her eyes to the ceiling in a pious manner.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh! youth, youth! That’s what comes of steeping one’s soul in Shakespeare! You ask me, my dear friend Paul, where is the gain to you in all this. Allow me to make a little digression. Zina loves you—that is an undoubted fact. But I have observed that at the same time, and in spite of her evident love, she is not quite sure of your good feeling and devotion to her; and for this reason she is sometimes cold and self-restrained in your presence. Have you never observed this yourself, Paul?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Certainly; I did this very day; but go on, what do you deduce from that fact?”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “There, you see! you have observed it yourself; then of course I am right. She is not quite sure of the lasting quality of your feeling for her! I am a mother, and I may be permitted to read the heart of my child. Now, then, supposing that instead of rushing into the room and reproaching, vilifying, even swearing at and insulting this sweet, pure, beautiful, proud being, instead of hurling contempt and vituperation at her head—supposing that instead of all this you had received the bad news with composure, with tears of grief, maybe; perhaps even with despair—but at the same time with noble composure of soul——”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No, no—don’t interrupt me! I wish to show you the picture as it is. Very well, supposing, then, that you had come to her and said, ‘Zina, I love you better than my life, but family considerations must separate us; I understand these considerations—they are devised for your greater happiness, and I dare not oppose them. Zina, I forgive you; be happy, if you can!’—think what effect such noble words would have wrought upon her heart!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes—yes, that’s all very true, I quite understand that much! but if I had said all this, I should have had to go all the same, without satisfaction!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “No, no, no! don’t interrupt me!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I wish to show you the whole picture in all its detail, in order to impress you fully and satisfactorily.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Very well, then, imagine now that you meet her in society some time afterwards: you meet perhaps at a ball—in the brilliant light of a ball-room, under the soothing strains of music, and in the midst of worldly women and of all that is gay and beautiful.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You alone are sad—thoughtful—pale,—you lean against some pillar (where you are visible, however!) and watch her.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She is dancing.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: You hear the strains of Strauss, and the wit and merriment around you, but you are sad and wretched.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

With what sort of eyes will she gaze on you as you stand there? ‘And I could doubt this man!’ she will think, ‘this man who sacrificed all, all, for my sake—even to the mortal wounding of his heart! Of course the old love will awake in her bosom and will swell with irresistible power!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna stopped to take breath.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Paul moved violently from side to side of his chair.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina now goes abroad for the benefit of the prince’s health—to Italy—to Spain,” she continued, “where the myrtle and the lemon tree grow, where the sky is so blue, the beautiful Guadalquiver flows! to the land of love, where none can live without loving; where roses and kisses—so to speak—breathe in the very air around. You follow her—you sacrifice your business, friends, everything, and follow her. And so your love grows and increases with irresistible might. Of course that love is irreproachable—innocent—you will languish for one another—you will meet frequently; of course others will malign and vilify you both, and call your love by baser names—but your love is innocent, as I have purposely said; I am her mother—it is not for me to teach you evil, but good. At all events the prince is not in the condition to keep a very sharp look-out upon you; but if he did, as if there would be the slightest ground for base suspicion? Well, the prince dies at last, and then, who will marry Zina, if not yourself? You are so distant a relative of the prince’s that there could be no obstacle to the match; you marry her—she is young still, and rich. You are a grandee in an instant! you, too, are rich now! I will take care that the prince’s will is made as it should be; and lastly, Zina, now convinced of your loyalty and faithfulness, will look on you hereafter as her hero, as her paragon of virtue and self-sacrifice! Oh! you must be blind,—blind, not to observe and calculate your own profit when it lies but a couple of strides from you, grinning at you, as it were, and saying, ‘Here, I am yours, take me! Oh, Paul, Paul!’ ”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Maria Alexandrovna!” cried Mosgliakoff, in great agitation and excitement, “I see it all!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: I have been rude, and a fool, and a scoundrel too!

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: He jumped up from his chair and tore his hair.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, and unbusinesslike, that’s the chief thing—unbusinesslike, and blindly so!” added Maria Alexandrovna.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “I’m an ass! Maria Alexandrovna,” he cried in despair.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “All is lost now, and I loved her to madness!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Maybe all is not lost yet!” said this successful orator softly, and as though thinking out some idea.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh! if only it could be so! help me—teach me. Oh! save me, save me!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “My dear boy,” said Maria Alexandrovna, sympathetically, and holding out her hand, “you acted impulsively, from the depth and heat of your passion—in fact, out of your great love for her; you were in despair, you had forgotten yourself; she must understand all that!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh! I love her madly! I am ready to sacrifice everything for her!” cried Mosgliakoff.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Listen! I will justify you before her.”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Oh, Maria Alexandrovna!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She pressed his hand warmly, and Mosgliakoff walked out of the room on tip-toes.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “There goes one fool, got rid of satisfactorily!” observed Maria Alexandrovna to herself,—“but there are more behind——!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: At this moment the door opened, and Zina entered the room.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: She was paler than usual, and her eyes were all ablaze.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Mamma!” she said, “be quick about this business, or I shall not be able to hold out. It is all so dirty and mean that I feel I must run out of the house if it goes on. Don’t drive me to desperation! I warn you—don’t weary me out—don’t weary me out!”

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Zina—what is it, my darling? You—you’ve been listening?” cried Maria Alexandrovna, gazing intently and anxiously at her daughter.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: “Yes, I have; but you need not try to make me ashamed of myself as you succeeded in doing with that fool. Now listen: I solemnly swear that if you worry and annoy me by making me play various mean and odious parts in this comedy of yours,—I swear to you that I will throw up the whole business and put an end to it in a moment. It is quite enough that I have consented to be a party in the main and essence of the base transactions; but—but—I did not know myself, I am poisoned and suffocated with the stench of it!”—So saying, she left the room and banged the door after her.

title: Uncle's Dream; and The Permanent Husband
text: Maria Alexandrovna looked fixedly after her for a moment, and reflected.

text: “So you are going to be married, Prince?”

text: “So you really are going to marry?”
